BusinessLocal NewsAre we in a housing bubble ? Not really . It just feels like it.http : **37;15556;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;15595;TOOLONG ... title= " Houses are selling quickly in Ottawa . " alt= " Houses are selling quickly in Ottawa . " data-portal-copyright= " James Bagnall " **28;15631;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1344754 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; One of the most enduring myths about the National Capital Region is that our economy is immune from the dramatic ebbs and flows experienced by the country&amp;rsquo ; s other major cities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s not . During the past quarter century we&amp;rsquo ; ve been hit by two dramatic downsizings of the federal government &amp;mdash ; one in the mid-1990s , the other in the early 2010s . Our economy has also been side-swiped by the telecom crash of 2001 and the collapse in 2009 of the largest private-sector employer , Nortel Networks . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The region has been fortunate in one respect , however . The government and high-tech sectors &amp;mdash ; which together account for nearly 30 per cent of the total workforce &amp;mdash ; never shrank in tandem . When government employment fell in the 1990s , high-tech was resurgent . In the wake of Nortel&amp;rsquo ; s collapse and the global financial crisis , the Conservatives padded the government workforce to offset the damage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;15661;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;15696;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Which is why the capital region&amp;rsquo ; s economy gives the impression of calm , despite the frenzy below the surface . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But now something rather odd is happening . The key sectors are all growing at the same time . The result : a jobs boom which , in turn , has been a catalyst for the region&amp;rsquo ; s housing market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Consider the employment data released Friday by Statistics Canada . The federal agency estimated nearly 800,000 people were working in Ottawa-Gatineau in December , up 62,600 from a year earlier . That&amp;rsquo ; s a gain of 8.5 per cent , the highest among the country&amp;rsquo ; s 33 largest cities but for Brantford , where the job market grew nine per cent . In contrast , employment across the country expanded by just 1.9 per cent over the past year . In another sign of the capital region&amp;rsquo ; s strength , about 80 per cent of the jobs added were full-time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; High-tech accounted for about 4,000 net new jobs while the federal government contributed 16,000 &amp;mdash ; thus establishing Justin Trudeau&amp;rsquo ; s bone fides as labour friendly . StatCan estimated the federal government employed 160,000 locally in December while the tech sector supported about 43,000 workers directly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt;Big shifts in Ottawa real estate in the past 3 yrs . Overall , ave . prices for residential resale properties were up 22% from 2016 to 2019 ( annual data ) , but the range of hikes was enormous -- 8 of the 10 biggest gainers were in the west . Half the bottom ten were in outlying areas . &lt;a href= " https : //t.co/KmcajJld76 " &gt;pic.twitter ... -- James Bagnall ( @JamesBagnall1 ) &lt;a href= " https : **33;15732;TOOLONG ... 12 , **33;15767;TOOLONG &lt;script async src= " https : **33;15802;TOOLONG " charset= " utf-8 " &gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt;After 3 yrs of rapid price gains , here 's how average resale prices stood in Ottawa in 2019 . Seven districts now average more than $800,000 -- compared to just three districts in 2018 . Data courtesy of &lt;a href= " https : **27;15837;TOOLONG ? src=h ... &lt;a href= " https : //t.co/u0Gg8GkLJE " &gt;pic.twitter ... -- James Bagnall ( @JamesBagnall1 ) &lt;a href= " https : **33;15866;TOOLONG ... 12 , **33;15901;TOOLONG &lt;script async src= " https : **33;15936;TOOLONG " charset= " utf-8 " &gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the latest jobs data suggest these two economic engines are also stimulating hiring more widely . Over the past year the region&amp;rsquo ; s economy has added more than 16,000 professionals who supply technical expertise to federal departments and high-tech firms . This sector employed nearly 80,000 in December . Wholesalers and retailers combined for 14,000 net new hires ; hotels and restaurants added 8,400. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Little wonder that , despite a rapidly growing labour force ( which includes people looking for work ) the capital region&amp;rsquo ; s jobless rate was just 4.4 per cent in December , just above historic lows. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nor is the employment surge a one-year fluke . The capital region has added 74,100 jobs since December 2016 &amp;mdash ; up 10.2 per cent , tied for second with Toronto , behind only Barrie . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Plenty of people have been moving to Ottawa and Gatineau to take advantage of the hot job market . StatCan estimates the region&amp;rsquo ; s working age population grew by 25,000 last year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This , in turn , is fuelling new home construction and the resale market alike . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everybody is hiring &amp;mdash ; government , hospitals , high-tech , &amp;rdquo ; says Bill Meyer , who leads a team of Remax real estate agents . &amp;ldquo ; Students have bought up nearly all the condos , &amp;rdquo ; he adds . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a perfect storm for real estate&amp;rdquo ; . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt;Whether you measure it by the last year or last 3 years , employment growth in Ottawa has been fastest or nearly so among the country 's 33 largest cities . It 's what happens when high-tech and government are both in hiring mode . &lt;a href= " https : //t.co/JtvItd0jzz " &gt;pic.twitter ... -- James Bagnall ( @JamesBagnall1 ) &lt;a href= " https : **33;15971;TOOLONG ... 12 , **33;16006;TOOLONG &lt;script async src= " https : **33;16041;TOOLONG " charset= " utf-8 " &gt;&lt;/script&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ottawa Real Estate Board last week reported the average price for residential resale properties was $500,000 &amp;mdash ; up 10.3 per cent year over year . Condos fetched an average $311,000 &amp;mdash ; a gain of 11.5 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At first glance these increases don&amp;rsquo ; t look sustainable , given that the region&amp;rsquo ; s economy is growing less than two per cent per year in real terms ( after deducting inflation ) and that developers have been adding 8,000 to 9,000 new houses , town homes and condos each year , which should help keep a lid on prices through the expanded supply . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , federal government employment has a disproportionate impact on the housing market , which experienced historically low price gains during the five years leading up to and following Jim Flaherty&amp;rsquo ; s deficit-busting budget in 2012 . There&amp;rsquo ; s some catch-up taking place now that government workers and contractors are more comfortable with the Liberals&amp;rsquo ; spending intentions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for all those new houses and condos , the population is growing fast enough to absorb all the new construction , and then some . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Which has led to a squeeze on listings for existing homes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The last time we had this few homes for sale was January 2004 , &amp;rdquo ; says Meyer . Just 1,800 residential and condo units were being advertised in December , down 33 per cent from a year earlier . This , in a region with more than half a million homes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We used to tell people , sell first , then we&amp;rsquo ; ll buy , &amp;rdquo ; says Paul Rushforth , who owns the real estate firm that bears his name . &amp;ldquo ; But now you can&amp;rsquo ; t sell until you find something , and it&amp;rsquo ; s very difficult to find something . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The shortage of listings has produced what no home buyer wants &amp;mdash ; seemingly endless bidding wars . Meyer notes his group sold 217 properties last year , roughly two-thirds following a bidding war . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nevertheless , the market doesn&amp;rsquo ; t appear to have lost its moorings yet , the way real estate did in Toronto and Vancouver in 2015 and 2016. &amp;ldquo ; The market didn&amp;rsquo ; t go crazy last year , &amp;rdquo ; Rushforth says . &amp;nbsp ; &amp;ldquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s still no appetite for overpriced listings . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indeed , the Ottawa Real Estate Board calculated the average gain for the combined residential and condo market last year was 8.4 per cent . &amp;nbsp ; While that was the highest since 2003 , it&amp;rsquo ; s nowhere near previous surges experienced in Ottawa . In the late 1960s , 1973-74 and 1983-84 , residential and condo prices soared 20 per cent or more . &amp;nbsp ; In 2002 , they jumped 14 per cent . No other year since has registered anything close to that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In short , we&amp;rsquo ; re still some distance from an employment and real estate bubble . " data-portal-copyright= " Bill Brooks " **28;16301;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1537911 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The job facing Jim Little , the incoming chief executive of the Ottawa Senators , is quite simple : He has to bring back the fans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Going into Saturday&amp;rsquo ; s match against the Montreal Canadiens , the Senators had played 20 home games this season with average attendance of fewer than 11,800 , dead last in the 31-team National Hockey League , despite the fact many of those seats were filled by giving away tickets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For a small market team like the Senators , this matters a lot financially . Because nearly 6,800 seats are unfilled each game , Senators owner Eugene Melnyk is leaving an estimated $500,000 on the table for every home match in the form of foregone ticket revenue . That&amp;rsquo ; s $20 million to date . For a team that barely broke even on operations last year on total revenues of $165 million &amp;mdash ; the recent estimate from Forbes Magazine &amp;mdash ; that gap must be addressed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Little , 55 , won&amp;rsquo ; t find it easy . The slide in attendance began during the 2016-17 season and has accelerated since then . Former top gun Cyril Leeder and chief marketing officer Peter O&amp;rsquo ; Leary were casualties of that initial decline . Melnyk replaced Leeder , now CEO of Myers Automotive Group , with Tom Anselmi early in 2017 . O&amp;rsquo ; Leary was fired in late 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;16331;TOOLONG ... title= " A file photo of Jim Little , named on Friday as new CEO of the Ottawa Senators . But Anselmi resigned in early 2018 , when it became clear Melnyk and Trinity Development founder John Ruddy wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t come to terms on the overall $4-billion mega project . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ever since , Melnyk has been both owner and acting CEO , watching with increasing frustration as many fans have simply stopped coming to Senators home games . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The reasons are many , ranging from a weak team to the lack of a downtown arena , &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;but a key one concerns Melnyk , a Barbados resident who has not endeared himself to the Ottawa community . More than two-thirds of Ottawa residents surveyed a year ago by Ekos Research Associates believed Menyk bore the brunt of responsibility for the collapse of the LeBreton project , while fewer than 40 per cent blamed Ruddy . Late in 2017 , Melnyk had mused about moving the team if fan support did n't improve . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Before 2017 , the team regularly attracted more than 18,000 fans per game and maintained a solid core of 13,000 season-ticket holders . The latter are now substantially fewer in number . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During the hunt for a new CEO , which began at the end of last season , Melnyk recognized he needed to hire someone who could rebuild links with the community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Leeder , who had been part of the group that brought the NHL back to Ottawa in 1992 , was known and generally liked throughout the capital region . He was on a first-name basis with nearly all the 125 companies and organizations that rented suites in the Canadian Tire Centre and knew very well the importance of maintaining good relations with the business community . The Senators depend on corporate clients to fill 35 per cent of the seats every game , all the more important given that federal government employees are not allowed to accept tickets as gifts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;16397;TOOLONG ... title= " Cyril Leeder on the day he left the employ of the Ottawa Senators in 2017. Little will have to move much more quickly , but Melnyk thinks he&amp;rsquo ; s up to the job . Little was one of four candidates Melnyk interviewed in October , when a road trip took the Senators to Las Vegas . &amp;ldquo ; Jim stood out immediately , &amp;rdquo ; Melnyk wrote in a reply to queries by this newspaper . &amp;ldquo ; His passion for winning is apparent as soon as you meet him . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; LIttle , a McGill University arts graduate , is familiar with the world of sports thanks to a series of corporate marketing gigs . During the 2000s , he oversaw RBC&amp;rsquo ; s sponsorships for the Olympics and golf . Thirty-three hundred employees &amp;mdash ; Little among them &amp;mdash ; representing approximately 25 per cent of Shaw&amp;rsquo ; s total workforce , accepted buyouts. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Little had been one of Shaw&amp;rsquo ; s top 10 executives , the company&amp;rsquo ; s financial hiccup was not exclusively a marketing issue . Ten years ago BlackBerry was at flood tide , the world&amp;rsquo ; s biggest maker of smartphones with annual sales of $20 billion ( all figure U.S. ) &amp;nbsp ; The Waterloo firm seemed well on its way to taking over from Nortel Networks as the country&amp;rsquo ; s flagship technology company . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then , seemingly out of the blue , Apple roared past , sucking nearly all the life from the firm then known as Research in Motion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Apple&amp;rsquo ; s ascent was nearly vertical . Revenue from iPhone sales topped $142 billion in its most recent fiscal year , ended Sept. 30 . Meanwhile , BlackBerry is expected this fiscal year ( ending Feb. 29 ) to generate revenues of little more than $1 billion across all its product lines . Hardly any of it will involve smartphones. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For all of Nortel&amp;rsquo ; s strategic failings , the telecom equipment maker never let an opportunity **25;17358;TOOLONG big slip from its grasp . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And yet , BlackBerry lives on . It earned billions of dollars in profits before its reckoning with Apple &amp;mdash ; giving it the wherewithal to pay for a brutal downsizing and radical restructuring . BlackBerry&amp;rsquo ; s head count now stands at roughly 4,000 compared to nearly 18,000 at the peak . About 500 are based in Kanata , the home of QNX , which BlackBerry acquired in 2010. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;17385;TOOLONG ... title= " A BlackBerry smartphone. " alt= " A BlackBerry smartphone. " data-portal-copyright= " GLENN CHAPMAN " **28;17421;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1202022 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; BlackBerry redirected its expertise in wireless technologies towards corporations , hospitals and government , offering ways of securely linking all the electronics within . Its engineers then targeted the emerging Internet of Things &amp;mdash ; &amp;nbsp ; which , through 5G wireless technology , will make it possible to transform electronics in the home and car into networks accessible through smartphone apps . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The result of all this effort will be on display Tuesday morning in Las Vegas , at the Consumer Electronics Show . BlackBerry will be showcasing a multi-layered software platform that allows automakers to develop driver profiles , scan vehicles&amp;rsquo ; software systems for potential maintenance issues , and head off threats from hackers . The new suite of software products will also give automakers the ability to keep software up to date over a car&amp;rsquo ; s lifetime . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s the first set of products developed with artificial intelligence and machine learning technology , which BlackBerry picked up a year ago when it shelled out $1.4 billion in cash and shares for California-based Cylance. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; BlackBerry&amp;rsquo ; s technology is already embedded in more than 150 million vehicles worldwide , making it a leader in this niche . BlackBerry&amp;rsquo ; s operating system software , built by QNX , guides digital instrument panels , handsfree and entertainment systems , and helps avoid crashes . Audi , BMW , Ford , GM , Honda , Volkswagen &amp;mdash ; you name it , BlackBerry&amp;rsquo ; s in there , acting as the brain of the machine . QNX software is also central to efforts aimed at developing driverless vehicles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;17451;TOOLONG ... title= " An infotainment console is photographed inside a Mercedes-Benz in the BlackBerry QNX Autonomous Vehicle Innovation Centre ( AVIC ) at the Blackberry QNX headquarters in Ottawa Thursday , March 22 , 2018. " alt= " An infotainment console is photographed inside a Mercedes-Benz in the BlackBerry QNX Autonomous Vehicle Innovation Centre ( AVIC ) at the Blackberry QNX headquarters in Ottawa Thursday , March 22 , 2018. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;17487;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1340250 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Now , with Cylance software , the automakers can customize both the electronics contained within vehicles as well as the overall management of the software contained in the fleets of cars they sell . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The automobile is becoming a supercomputer on wheels , &amp;rdquo ; says Charles Eagan , BlackBerry&amp;rsquo ; s chief technology officer since June 2018. &amp;ldquo ; Securing software in autos is a massive opportunity for us because security is not something you retrofit . You try to design it in from the beginning . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eagan knows a fair bit about the power of BlackBerry&amp;rsquo ; s underlying technology &amp;mdash ; and the importance of combining it with artificial intelligence . A University of Waterloo grad ( applied math and electrical engineering ) , Eagan was a senior R&amp;amp ; D executive with QNX from 2005 to 2007 , when it was owned by Harman International . Eagan later worked at a series of tech firms before joining BlackBerry in 2011 &amp;mdash ; the year after it paid $200 million to purchase QNX from Harman . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eagan led the development effort to forklift the QNX operating system into the BlackBerry 10 handset &amp;mdash ; the company&amp;rsquo ; s Hail Mary attempt to catch and surpass the iPhone all in one go . He remains proud of what the firm accomplished . &amp;ldquo ; We created the most advanced , secure smartphone ever , &amp;rdquo ; he says , &amp;ldquo ; and we did it in record time . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But , as the world now knows , it didn&amp;rsquo ; t matter . Apple&amp;rsquo ; s momentum by then was overwhelming . Eagan left BlackBerry in 2015 only to return again in 2018. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;17517;TOOLONG ... title= " An older QNX concept vehicle . " alt= " An older QNX concept vehicle . " data-portal-copyright= " PROVIDED " **28;17553;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1535073 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Eagan is not one to dwell on the past . Based in Kanata , he is in charge of the company&amp;rsquo ; s recently-created BlackBerry Labs &amp;mdash ; a unit dedicated to commercializing products that combine technologies from the company&amp;rsquo ; s various divisions . A particular emphasis for the Labs&amp;rsquo ; 120 engineers will be the Internet of Things , and how to embed Cylance&amp;rsquo ; s artificial intelligence in the company&amp;rsquo ; s other product lines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The pressure on Eagan is intense . Not only are his competitors many , he&amp;rsquo ; s operating in an industry in which technology becomes obsolete relatively quickly . BlackBerry devotes slightly more than 25 per cent of its revenues on R&amp;amp ; D &amp;mdash ; even more than wireless technology rivals Nokia and Ericsson , which spend about 20 per cent of revenues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That , and the unusual spending associated with integrating Cylance&amp;rsquo ; s technology , accounted for BlackBerry&amp;rsquo ; s $111 million net loss during the nine months ended Nov. 30 , on revenues of $758 million . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The consensus forecast according to Thomson Reuters for fiscal 2021 , which begins Mar. 1 , calls for BlackBerry to produce a profit of nearly $100 million ( 16 cents per share ) on revenues of $1.2 billion . That&amp;rsquo ; s lower than the firm&amp;rsquo ; s profits from two years ago , but would nevertheless mark the beginning of a revival that received a catalyst this week in Las Vegas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Just don&amp;rsquo ; t dwell on where the company could be had it bought QNX sooner , and made more equal the early war against iPhone. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;17583;TOOLONG ... While this suggests reasonable options for buyers , the combined listings represent less than half of one per cent of the city&amp;rsquo ; s 400,000 residences . That&amp;rsquo ; s a tight market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Worse , as far as potential buyers are concerned , the number of residential for sale signs tumbled nearly 27 per cent year over year to 1,525 while condominiums available for resale were nearly impossible to find . Just 267 were listed in December , down a startling 57 per cent from a year earlier . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt;One more slice of Ottawa 's single family home resale market in 2019 . Compared to 2017 , residential resale listings are down 43 per cent while the number of available condos has slumped more than 70 per cent . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;blockquote class= " twitter-tweet " data-width= " 550 " data-dnt= " true " &gt;&lt;p lang= " en " dir= " ltr " &gt;Here 's the breakdown by district for single family homes sold in Ottawa in 2019 -- average prices for houses resold compared to 2018 . The explanation : properties put up for sale simply sold much faster . Residential homes took 44 days on average in 2019 to find a buyer , compared to 57 days the previous year , while condos last year were snapped up in 45 days after initial listing , compared to 71 days in 2018. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The real estate board&amp;rsquo ; s outgoing president Dwight Delahunt said properties in certain popular districts &amp;ldquo ; were snapped up by prepared buyers&amp;rdquo ; almost immediately , often following bidding wars . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Across the city there was wide variation in the residential resale market , ranging from a 31.5 per cent gain for the 36 properties sold last year in the district that includes Country Place , Pineglen and Crestview , to an eight per cent drop for the 109 residences sold in Bells Corners . Both of these extremes were influenced by unusual sales activity in a section of each district . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the Country Place district , six homes sold in the area north of West Hunt Club Road and west of the Rideau River for an average of $820,500 compared to two sales in this sub-district in 2018 , for just $644,000 . Even so , price gains throughout the wider district were robust . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Bells Corners district happens to include Cedar Hill and Orchard Estates , which in 2019 recorded just six sales averaging $1 million for each property compared to 12 sales in the $1 million-plus category during 2018 . Most price increases in other parts of the Bells Corners district ranged from nine per cent to 22 per cent year over year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Overall , 20 of the 46 real estate districts tracked by this newspaper registered average price rises in excess of 10 per cent with a heavy concentration in the western areas of the city . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;18603;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1533603 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa entrepreneur Mike Diduca hopes to open a cannabis superstore this spring in a Montreal Road building now containing a Royal Bank branch . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Sussex Drive at Rideau , one of the city&amp;rsquo ; s most famous intersections , plans are afoot for a cannabis boutique called mihi. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Elsewhere around town , new outlets of Hobo and Superette , two of the city&amp;rsquo ; s original cannabis stores , could pop up as well . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That&amp;rsquo ; s a hint of what to expect as the province opens up the cannabis retail trade after the initial number of shops was restricted because of a shortage of pot . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Licence applications open Jan. 6 for entrepreneurs who want to run cannabis shops . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It will be a gradual rollout , though . The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario plans to start issuing licences in April at the moderate clip of about 20 a month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Diduca plans to call his store Budroom . He is negotiating with the landlord of the bank building in Gloucester , on Montreal Road near Shefford . At about 4,600 square feet , it could be the largest cannabis store in Canada , he says . Unless , of course , someone else opens a larger one . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Diduca says he&amp;rsquo ; s inspired by Planet 13 , a huge , glitzy cannabis store in Las Vegas that has an interactive lotus flower on the roof and LED art on the floors . He&amp;rsquo ; s planning banks of digital video walls and a conveyor belt running through the store to deliver goods from the back . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The mihi chain that hopes to open four stores in Ottawa this spring is aiming for a calm , zen design . A model mihi store built in Burlington , Ont. , features a spare design with lots of wood . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;18633;TOOLONG ... title= " A model mihi store in Burlington gives a good indication of what stores in the chain will look like . But plans by mihi and other entrepreneurs were stalled when the government announced that the rights to apply for the first handful of licences would be awarded by lottery . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The mihi chain has held on to four leases in Ottawa and plans to open stores here as soon as licences are awarded , said Steffen Schenk , a company vice-president . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Besides the storefront on the ground floor of the condo building on the west side of Sussex at Rideau , the company has rented a space at the College Square mall on Baseline Road at Woodroffe Avenue and unspecified locations in the Bells Corners and Heron Gate neighbourhoods . The company hopes to have 16 stores open across Ontario this spring , Schenk said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa now has three cannabis stores : Superette , Hobo and Fire &amp;amp ; Flower . They are run by lottery winners under licensing arrangements with retail corporations that hope to expand . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Hobo , a B.C.-based chain owned by the Donnelly Group , initially hopes to open 10 more stores in Ontario , vice-president Harrison Stoker said . A &amp;ldquo ; portion&amp;rdquo ; of the stores will be in Ottawa . &amp;ldquo ; I can&amp;rsquo ; t give it away , &amp;rdquo ; he says with a laugh , adding the company is negotiating leases . &amp;ldquo ; But we love Ottawa . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Superette is also scouting leases and plans to apply for licences for one or two stores in Ottawa , said Drummond Munro , company president and chief vibe officer . Its goal is 10 new stores in Ontario in 2020 , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A spokesperson for Fire &amp;amp ; Flower wasn&amp;rsquo ; t immediately available for comment , but the retail chain with stores in Western Canada has long planned to open more stores in Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s no limit to the number of people or corporations that can apply for cannabis store licences in Ontario . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , the initial fever pitch of excitement over cannabis retail appears to have been tempered , said Mark Asfar , a lawyer at Momentum Law in Ottawa who specializes in cannabis regulations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The province killed some of the appetite among investors by introducing the lotteries , leaving entrepreneurs who had invested in business plans and leases hanging , Asfar said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Asfar initially had a couple of dozen clients eager to open cannabis stores in Ottawa , but only about half a dozen are still interested , he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; However , he said he was optimistic there would be several new stores in Ottawa starting this spring , and eventually maybe even some by mom-and-pop operators , since the financial requirements imposed on entrants in the last lottery are not part of the new licensing regime . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; jmiller@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **26;18699;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;18727;TOOLONG ... drug store among first in province to offer rapid HIV test&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;18762;TOOLONG ... BusinessLocal BusinessLocal NewsFinkelstein and Taub : A love letter to Ottawa 's futurehttp : **34;18879;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;18915;TOOLONG ... title= " Ottawa entrepreneurs Harley Finkelstein and Lindsay Taub , shown with their daughters Zoe and Bayley , are pumped about the future of this city . " alt= " Ottawa entrepreneurs Harley Finkelstein and Lindsay Taub , shown with their daughters Zoe and Bayley , are pumped about the future of this city . " data-portal-copyright= " Courtesy : Harley Finkelstein " **28;18951;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1529120 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Full disclosure : This will not be another story calling Ottawa crappy or sleepy or boring . This will be exactly the opposite : a love letter to Ottawa , containing our hope for this city over the next decade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We&amp;rsquo ; re not from here , but we chose to live and raise our family in Ottawa . Lindsay runs an ice cream shop in our neighbourhood ; Harley just said hello to Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s 1,000th local employee . We will live here for the rest of our lives . Because of the strong roots we&amp;rsquo ; ve grown and the incredible communities we&amp;rsquo ; ve discovered , we feel a deep level of responsibility to help guide this city to achieve its full potential . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa is of course working through its own issues , such as homelessness and the opioid crisis , and there&amp;rsquo ; s a lot of work to be done &amp;mdash ; but there is also so much opportunity ahead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As we enter 2020 , what better time to set goals and ambitions for the next decade ? Here&amp;rsquo ; s one for all of us : Let&amp;rsquo ; s transform our city into the best possible version of itself within the next 10 years . There&amp;rsquo ; s a saying often heard in the Shopify hallways that goes , &amp;ldquo ; Hell is meeting yourself in the future and finding out what you ? could ? have been . &amp;rdquo ; We can&amp;rsquo ; t let that happen to our city . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are signs that it could happen , though : Earlier this year , the NCC planned a pop-up bistro in a downtown neighbourhood . Wine and croissants in the park &amp;hellip ; what&amp;rsquo ; s not to love ? But too many people said , &amp;ldquo ; Not on my street , &amp;rdquo ; and the idea was shut down . Or perhaps you&amp;rsquo ; ve strolled by what used to be a vibrant patio along the Rideau Canal near the University of Ottawa , which has sat empty for months on end . The entrepreneurs behind these ideas , and many others , have had to endure Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s risk-averse culture every time they try to start something innovative . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The thing is , every time we say no to something new in this city , not only do we lose that opportunity , but we lose a bit of the gusto from the people who pitched it . We&amp;rsquo ; ve trained ourselves to maintain the status quo. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What would happen if we did things differently ? What if , instead of saying no , we said ? yes ? to more pop-ups , more movies in the park , better use of our beautiful waterways , and the development of our once-iconic Sparks Street ? What if we had more street food , more outdoor hockey rinks , and more weird and wonderful experiences completely unique to our city ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;18981;TOOLONG ... title= " Let 's revitalize our once-iconic Sparks Street . " alt= " Let 's revitalize our once-iconic Sparks Street . " data-portal-copyright= " Tony Caldwell " **28;19017;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1529116 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thankfully , there are hints of this all over the city , too . Tavern on the Hill allows gorgeous views of Parliament accompanied by gourmet hot dogs . Wesley Clover Park hosts the Magic of Lights : two kilometres of pure Christmas joy that families can drive through over the holidays . During the Canada 150 celebrations , Dinner in the Sky gave us the chance to experience fine dining at a table suspended 150 feet in the air . Haunted Walks have been giving Ottawans historical tours paired with spooky stories for years . These are the kind of vibrant experiences we need more of in our city over the next decade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We all have a role to play . Start a business , or support the people who do . You can be risk-averse , but allow others to take risks . Say yes instead of no to new things . Some experiments will fail , but each will teach us how to do it better next time , and that&amp;rsquo ; s how you build world-class cities . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The stage is already set : our local government is excited for change , our revamped National Capital Commission is committed to innovation , and Ottawa is already an incredible city to live and work in . So let&amp;rsquo ; s do this . Let&amp;rsquo ; s transform our city . Let&amp;rsquo ; s put wind in the sails of our creativity and culture . There is a heartbeat to this city ; let&amp;rsquo ; s increase the beats per minute . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This level of ambition is our wish for our city over the next decade . And if we succeed , the letter we write in 2030 will look very different from this one . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **30;19047;TOOLONG **26;19079;TOOLONG and &lt;strong&gt;Lindsay Taub&lt;/strong&gt; are entrepreneurs based in Ottawa , where they live with their two daughters , Bayley and Zoe . Harley is the COO of &lt;a href= " https : //www.shopify.ca/ " &gt;Shopify , &lt; ... and Lindsay is the Founder of &lt;a href= " https : //sundaeschool.ca/ " &gt;Sundae School . &lt;/a&gt;&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;19107;TOOLONG ... 2020 Vision -- How an Ottawa co-op aims to fight climate change&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;19142;TOOLONG ... The future of city planning in Ottawa does n't look very democratic&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Harley Finkelstein , Lindsay TaubMon , 30 Dec 2019 19:22:58 **45;19212;TOOLONG ... BusinessSutcliffe : In the new decade , Ottawa needs a new attitude toward businesshttp : **32;19259;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19293;TOOLONG ... title= " Prime Minister Justin Trudeau prepares to break ground at the Boundary Road location of the big Amazon warehouse in Orl ? ans in 2018. " alt= " Prime Minister Justin Trudeau prepares to break ground at the Boundary Road location of the big Amazon warehouse in Orl ? ans in 2018. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19329;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1528954 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Exactly 20 years ago , as the calendar flipped over to a milestone new year , people in Ottawa were anxious about Y2K and bullish on Nortel . So let&amp;rsquo ; s not get carried away with the idea that a year or two of business events is an easy thing to predict , let alone an entire decade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As 2020 begins , Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s business community is perhaps stronger than it has been since the 1990s . We like to think that we earn our economic development wins through hard work and careful strategy . The arrival of a new Amazon distribution centre was trumpeted as a coup for Ottawa , but it&amp;rsquo ; s not like it would have made sense to short its shipments to Eastern Ontario out of San Jose or Boston . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The truth is that the entrepreneurial spark can ignite almost anywhere . When it does , it has as much to do with happenstance as planning . There are now no fewer than 1,000 jobs in our city , for example , that can be traced back to a German millennial meeting a woman from Ottawa on a ski trip , moving here , starting an online snowboarding company , not being pleased with the e-commerce platforms available , and launching Shopify. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That sequence of events is about as easy to replicate as dialling a random number , getting Drake&amp;rsquo ; s cellphone , and so delighting him with your unexpected call that he invites you to sit court-side with him at a Raptors game . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19359;TOOLONG ... title= " Fiona McKean and husband Tobi L ? tke , the founder of Shopify , are shown in this file photo in front of the Opinicon Resort , whose restoration and renovation she oversaw. " alt= " Fiona McKean and husband Tobi L ? tke , the founder of Shopify , are shown in this file photo in front of the Opinicon Resort , whose restoration and renovation she oversaw. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;19395;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1528956 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; But while we did little to deserve Shopify , that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t mean we can&amp;rsquo ; t appreciate its success . And more than sit back and enjoy the ride &amp;ndash ; crossing our fingers that it continues its explosive growth , while simultaneously hoping there are more Tobi Lutkes moving to Ottawa for love &amp;ndash ; we should ensure that the ground into which Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s seed was planted is even more fertile for future entrepreneurs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There are dozens of Shopify millionaires who will start their own companies or invest in others in the next few years . This next generation of start-ups could be crucial to the future of our local economy . Beyond that , an entire generation of digital natives is coming of age , attending Ottawa universities and colleges and getting hired for their first jobs . We must find ways to keep them in Ottawa , so they fuel our growth rather than move elsewhere for the best and most productive years of their careers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While any new employment contributes to the economy , not all jobs are created equal . City leaders have a tendency to treat growth in the service industry as though it has as much value as a new company that sells its products around the world . Our primary focus should be on industries that bring new money to Ottawa , particularly technology and tourism . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We can start by becoming a place that embraces change rather than resisting it . Unlike some jurisdictions , our city officials haven&amp;rsquo ; t banned ride-sharing services like Uber and Lyft , but they were reluctant rather than enthusiastic adopters . If Ottawa wants to attract companies developing disruptive technologies , and a generation of smart , innovative people for whom those products and services seem intuitive rather than frightening , we should be seen as a place of innovation , not bureaucracy . The local test track for driverless cars is a shining example . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Our tourism industry could also use more support . For too long , the sector has endured a pattern of two steps forward , one step back . When a new source of funding is uncovered , another program is cancelled . In addition , thanks to light rail and other infrastructure projects , the downtown core has become an unappealing construction zone . And major landmarks , including the Parliament Buildings , are less accessible because of security and restoration work . Soon we won&amp;rsquo ; t have the familiar vista of the Peace Tower to share with tourists . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As the nation&amp;rsquo ; s capital and a centre for technology , we have a unique opportunity for diverse and aggressive economic growth in the next decade . We should do everything we can to both stimulate innovation and move out of its way . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **28;19425;TOOLONG Sutcliffe&lt;/strong&gt; is an Ottawa writer , broadcaster and entrepreneur . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;19455;TOOLONG ... BusinessNewsmaker of the decade -- Shopify : ' This is kind of blowing my mind'http : **35;19607;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;19644;TOOLONG ... title= " Tobi L ? tke , founder and CEO of Shopify. " alt= " Tobi L ? tke , founder and CEO of Shopify. " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;19680;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1528118 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; **28;19710;TOOLONG : &lt;/strong&gt;Over the past 10 years we 've watched Ottawa transform , from billions of dollars invested in infrastructure to our ever-expanding suburbs . Our city 's transformation has n't just been physical . We 've been changed by tragedy , too . We 've faced floods and tornadoes , we 've faced terror and fear , and we 've witnessed nightmares on our roads . But most importantly , perhaps , this decade has also given us heroes -- people who inspired us with their brilliance and courage . These stories helped shape the Ottawa we live in today and here , in our annual newsmakers series , we return to examine the biggest stories of the decade . Today , Shopify. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;div id= " 1576082438.003200 " class= " c-virtuallistitem " role= " listitem " aria-expanded= " false " &gt; &lt;div class= " c-message c-message--light c-message--adjacent c-message--last " role= " document " &gt; &lt;div class= " c-messagecontent **36;19740;TOOLONG " &gt; &lt;div class= " c-messagemessageblocks **32;19778;TOOLONG " &gt; &lt;div class= " p-blockkitrenderer **32;19812;TOOLONG " &gt; &lt;div class= " **30;19846;TOOLONG **37;19878;TOOLONG " &g; ... &lt;div class= " p-richtextblock " dir= " auto " &gt; &lt;hr&gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt; " The spark for a high-tech recovery in Ottawa-Gatineau could well be struck by a software company you 've never heard of , in a place you would n't expect . " &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I wrote these words about Shopify and its ByWard market location in mid-November , 2011 , when the capital region&amp;rsquo ; s tech sector was still reeling from the collapse of Nortel Networks and the aftermath of the 2008-09 financial crisis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Journalists should know better than to try predicting seminal shifts , but if you&amp;rsquo ; re ever right in this business , you should let people know . And this time we were right . At least in terms of business , this past decade was very much the story of the e-commerce technology firm that transformed from a startup into one of the country&amp;rsquo ; s most valuable firms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Consider the size and speed of Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s advance from 2009 to December 2019 : &lt;/p&gt; **30;19917;TOOLONG surged from 15 to more than 4,000. &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Revenues rocketed from a few million dollars to an estimated US$1.6 billion . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;The company 's market value exploded from less than US$20 million to US$45 billion . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;The number of online storefronts built with Shopify software multiplied from fewer than 10,000 to one million . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; The remarkable bit : Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s co-founder and chief executive Tobi L&amp;uuml ; tke fully expected his firm would not only grow at a torrid pace , but would do so in a manner that was sustainable . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I want to build one of Canada&amp;rsquo ; s greatest success stories , &amp;rdquo ; the 31-year-old entrepreneur said in an interview with this newspaper late in 2011. &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s been my goal for a very long time . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;19949;TOOLONG ... title= " Tobi Lutke in 2011. " alt= " Tobi Lutke in 2011. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;19985;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1528112 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Most are by now familiar with the story of how L&amp;uuml ; tke and fellow co-founders Daniel Weinand and Scott Lake grew so frustrated with trying to sell snowboards online they created their own enabling software . In 2006 , they launched Shopify , which would provide all of the software tools entrepreneurs required to sell their products online . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Existing software was not designed with the new entrepreneur in mind , so we rejected the existing models and created our own , &amp;rdquo ; L&amp;uuml ; tke explains in his blog. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20015;TOOLONG ... title= " ( L-R ) Co-founder of Shopify , Daniel Weinand and chief platform officer , Harley Finkelstein are photographed in their office in Ottawa on Monday , Dec. 16 , 2013. " alt= " ( L-R ) Co-founder of Shopify , Daniel Weinand and chief platform officer , Harley Finkelstein are photographed in their office in Ottawa on Monday , Dec. 16 , 2013. " data-portal-copyright= " James Park " **28;20051;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1528111 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In retrospect , it all seemed so easy . In some ways , it was . The founders saw a need and moved to fill it without overthinking it . &amp;ldquo ; I never focused on the high failure rate of startups , especially ones where the founders have little to no startup experience , &amp;rdquo ; Weinand told Entrepreneur magazine in 2016. &amp;ldquo ; In a way , being oblivious to this reality allowed us to keep focused . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The founders , unusually , had the advantage of time . They had a few years to fully develop their core software platform before potential competitors could really see what they were doing . And by then , it was too late . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s financial performance has been remarkably steady compared with previous generations of tech stars from Ottawa . Telecom rockets such as Mitel ( 1970s ) , Newbridge ( 1980s and 1990s ) and JDSU ( 1990s ) were forever faced with shipping more hardware every quarter to keep investors happy . One late delivery by a significant customer would make a mess of revenue projections and sabotage the company&amp;rsquo ; s share price . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In sharp contrast , Shopify generates its revenues in a manner that makes unpleasant surprises less likely . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Merchants pay Shopify a monthly fee for the software platform that operates their storefront . They also shell out for add-on services ranging from shipping to processing payments . While Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s technology lacks the flexibility of custom-built online storefronts , it offers setup speed and ease of use &amp;mdash ; qualities much appreciated by entrepreneurs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20081;TOOLONG ... title= " Shopify 's Ottawa offices on Elgin Street . The waterfall on the 13th floor . " alt= " Shopify 's Ottawa offices on Elgin Street . The waterfall on the 13th floor . " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;20117;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1528116 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The monthly subscriptions provide built-in stability for Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s revenues because merchants tend to stick with Shopify once they&amp;rsquo ; ve signed on , and the payments are automatic . Not only that , the software applications are riding a generational shift from bricks and mortar to online shopping . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Through word-of-mouth , judicious advertising and now , sheer momentum , Shopify has been adding merchants with metronome-like regularity . Once in a while , even L&amp;uuml ; tke expresses some surprise at where this has taken the firm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; More than a million merchants are now building their businesses on Shopify &lt;strong&gt; , &lt;/strong&gt; &amp;rdquo ; he said following the publication of the firm&amp;rsquo ; s most recent quarter . &amp;ldquo ; This is kind of blowing my mind right now , &amp;rdquo ; he added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This is not to say Shopify is immune from setbacks . More than half of its revenues depend on how well its customers are doing &amp;mdash ; so a recession would severely crimp sales . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Such a reversal would also do serious damage to Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s extravagant market value . With a share price tracking towards US$400 last week on the New York Stock Exchange and topping $500 on the TSX , Shopify is trading well in excess of where its sales and growth suggest they should be . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Yet for all of the company&amp;rsquo ; s stunning trajectory , the direct impact on the Ottawa area has been surprisingly modest . &amp;nbsp ; Consider that just one-quarter of the firm&amp;rsquo ; s more than 4,000 employees are based here at the global headquarters on Elgin Street . The company&amp;rsquo ; s Toronto-area workforce next year will likely exceed that of Ottawa . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20147;TOOLONG ... title= " Inside look at the Shopify headquarters on Elgin St in Ottawa , May 30 , 2018. " alt= " Inside look at the Shopify headquarters on Elgin St in Ottawa , May 30 , 2018. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;20183;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1528117 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It is also an unusual facet of Shopify that 25 per cent of its workforce operates out of home offices around the globe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With plans in place to add ever more languages to its online platform and related services , Shopify&amp;rsquo ; s spread worldwide will see its Ottawa operations continue shrinking as a percentage of its total workforce . That&amp;rsquo ; s just how it goes with successful multinationals . At the peak of the telecom boom , fewer than 20 per cent of Nortel&amp;rsquo ; s workforce was based in the Ottawa area &amp;mdash ; the home for the firm&amp;rsquo ; s global R&amp;amp ; D effort . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What really matters for Ottawa is the example set by Shopify &amp;mdash ; not to mention the hundreds of millions of dollars its executives and employees have pulled out of the firm thanks to the stunning rise in its share price . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; L&amp;uuml ; tke and his colleagues have brought back to life the idea that you can build a global enterprise from a base in Ottawa . Just a few months before I interviewed L&amp;uuml ; tke on that day in 2011 , Nortel sold off the last of its intellectual property &amp;mdash ; the product of more than a century of astonishing corporate history . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With any luck , Shopify will carry the torch for decades more to come . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;20213;TOOLONG ... of the decade -- Phoenix : How to make sure your staff does n't get paid&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;20248;TOOLONG ... becomes terror : two crashes , nine deaths , a broken trust&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;20283;TOOLONG ... of the decade -- Confederation Line LRT : ' A new beginning for public transit&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; James BagnallTue , 24 Dec 2019 12:08:34 **45;20318;TOOLONG ... BusinessLocal BusinessNewsmaker of the decade : A decade of planning , but ' All LeBreton has ever got is words'http : **34;20365;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;20401;TOOLONG ... title= " LeBreton Flats : empty since the 1960s . Will the latest effort by the National Capital Commission finally produce a plan that will fill it ? " alt= " LeBreton Flats : empty since the 1960s . Will the latest effort by the National Capital Commission finally produce a plan that will fill it ? " data-portal-copyright= " Handout image " **28;20437;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1467829 " /&gt; **28;20467;TOOLONG the past 10 years , we 've faced floods and tornadoes , terror and fear and nightmares on our roads . Most importantly , this decade has given us heroes -- people who inspire with their brilliance and courage . These stories helped shape the Ottawa we live in today . In our annual newsmakers series , we examine the decade 's biggest stories . Today , LeBreton Flats . **26;20497;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It takes little more than 10 minutes to walk from Bayview Road to Booth St. along the southern fringe of LeBreton Flats . Turn north and it&amp;rsquo ; s just a few minutes more to the Sir John A. Macdonald Parkway . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Astonishingly this prime , 53-acre site has lain mostly fallow since the 1960s despite , or maybe because of , its proximity to the Parliament Buildings . More than half a century ago , it was cleared of gritty , industrial buildings and single-family homes to make way for a community of government office buildings . In what was to become a theme , the plan was never realized . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20525;TOOLONG ... title= " A view of Lebreton Flats area . " alt= " A view of Lebreton Flats area . " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;20561;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1459444 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , LeBreton has been condemned to serve as a &lt;em&gt;tabula rasa&lt;/em&gt; for several generations of politicians and developers , a place where dreams come to die . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The National Capital Commission &amp;mdash ; the owner of most of LeBreton &amp;mdash ; has mulled multiple proposals over the years . Museums , convention centres , a world exposition , rail terminal , aquarium , housing , retail developments , with the notable exception of the Canadian War Museum , all have been promoted and discarded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; All the ( Flats ) has ever got was words &amp;mdash ; great heaps of them , in report after report , plan after plan , each erased to make way for a new one , &amp;rdquo ; author Phil Jenkins wrote in his 2008 history of LeBreton , &lt;em&gt;An Acre of Time&lt;/em&gt; . &amp;ldquo ; More than 30 years&amp;rsquo ; worth of words , millions and millions of words , and not one serious building has been built there , &amp;rdquo ; he concluded . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Indeed , this is where things stood as the 2010s began . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The NCC&amp;rsquo ; s vision at the time was to encourage the formation of some 2,500 residential units , office buildings and a modest number of retail outlets . The ultimate goal was to create a community of 4,500 residents and 6,500 workers , all served by public transit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the only development of note was several hundred residential units built by Claridge on the eastern periphery . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; All that changed a few years later when three catalysts converged : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;In February 2013 , the city awarded the first phase of the light rail transit project to Rideau Transit Group , which would eventually lead to two new stations at either end of Lebreton. &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;On Dec. 11 , 2013 , city council revised Ottawa 's official development plan to encourage more population density along the mass transit routes . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;li&gt;Mark Kristmanson was appointed NCC chief in February 2014 . Later that year , he invited the private sector to produce fresh ideas for remaking the entire LeBreton site . &lt;/li&gt; &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; When the NCC whittled down five contenders to just one on April 28 , 2016 , it seemed LeBreton&amp;rsquo ; s long wait for redevelopment was finally over . RendezVous LeBreton , a joint venture between Ottawa Senators owner Eugene Melnyk and Trinity Development founder John Ruddy , would fill the 53-acre site over the next two decades with houses , apartments , a hotel , office buildings and entertainment attractions . A $600-million National Hockey League stadium would be the centrepiece . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Unfortunately , the very catalysts that pushed LeBreton redevelopment to the starting line also worked at cross-purposes as the $4-billion project entered the crucial and ultimately futile financing stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The LRT project , combined with the new city policy of densification , created irresistible pressure for developers to propose massive new apartment or condominium towers . Ruddy did so at 900 Albert St. , the site of LRT&amp;rsquo ; s new Bayview station , located a few steps southwest of LeBreton. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although the city had approved zoning changes to permit towers at 900 Albert in 2012 and Trinity had submitted a more ambitious planning rationale for the site in March 2016 , Melnyk claimed in legal filings that he was not aware of the full extent of Ruddy&amp;rsquo ; s plans until late 2017 . Whatever the timing , Melnyk became convinced the marketing of apartments at 900 Albert would profoundly interfere with the economics of the LeBreton project , which depended heavily on the sale of residential and retail properties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This commercial disagreement , among others , would erupt into $1.7-billion in claims and counterclaims late in 2018 , with the RendezVous LeBreton partnership finally dissolving earlier this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While discordant personalities were significant influences in triggering the legal mess , the NCC appears to have significantly underplayed the commercial risk . Although remaking LeBreton would be nearly 10 times the cost and would take at least twice the time as the complicated Lansdowne redevelopment in south Ottawa , the NCC paid surprisingly little attention to the financial strength of the bidders or the stability of the winning partnership . Just 20 of a potential 140 points were awarded on the basis of ownership , management , financial capability and how the financial plan would be implemented . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The ability to work together was obviously vital . Yet it was clear from the beginning that the partnership was troubled . The day after the NCC picked RendezVous LeBreton as its preferred bidder , Melnyk threatened the team&amp;rsquo ; s project manager , Graham Bird , with legal action and termination . When trying to arrange financing , Melnyk and Ruddy wound up calling the same people , sometimes with contradictory messages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Melnyk , as his colleagues know well , prefers to be in charge . And , because the National Hockey League stadium and associated projects were to be developed early on , he faced more immediate financial risks than Ruddy , who could afford to spread his retail and residential projects over two decades . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;20591;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;20626;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; The perspectives of the RendezVous LeBreton partners were also a study in contrast . Melnyk , the outsider and unpredictable pharmaceutical entrepreneur , kept his eye firmly on the commercial opportunity . Those close to him say he was also seeking recognition from a community that has not always greeted him warmly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For Ruddy and Bird , the idea of LeBreton was epic . Hometown boys , they viewed the project as a historic opportunity to make a permanent imprint on the last large piece of open property in the nation&amp;rsquo ; s capital . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , they and Melnyk will spend part of January in Toronto providing evidence to support their lawsuits against each other . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Meantime , the NCC has launched yet another effort to redevelop LeBreton . The commission &amp;ldquo ; is embarking on a process to create a renewed vision for a dynamic Capital destination and a complete community where people can live , work and play , &amp;rdquo ; the crown corporation declares without evident enthusiasm on its website. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;20662;TOOLONG ... title= " National Capital Commission 's concept map of a new plan for rebuilding LeBreton Flats . " alt= " National Capital Commission 's concept map of a new plan for rebuilding LeBreton Flats . " data-portal-copyright= " NCC " **28;20698;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1510129 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The fresh vision looks to be very much like the plan submitted originally by Melnyk and Ruddy , only the NCC intends to roll out this latest version one bit at a time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Will it happen finally ? Will LeBreton fill up ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Maybe . But consider this line from the LeBreton Flats Plan published by the NCC 23 years ago : &amp;ldquo ; Driving the planning was an unwavering conviction shared by all that the time had come to bring life and activity back to the Flats . &amp;rdquo ; That plan , too , proposed housing , office and retail development , cultural institutions and open spaces . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Sometimes , when you can do absolutely anything , it&amp;rsquo ; s difficult to do something . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The most recent decade at LeBreton remained true to the experience of the previous four . &amp;nbsp ; Nothing happened . With any luck , the 2020s will finally break this pattern .
