" data-portal-copyright= " Jean Levac " **28;28628;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1493802 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Police The Police was the first song that Chr ? tien , who 's 41 , penned for the new album , a track that launched him and his bandmates off on another round of politically charged songwriting . Also included are the Trump-inspired disco burn of House of Cards , the anti-nuclear War Games and the biting Slumlord , written to express Chr ? tien 's frustration with Ottawa landlords . He 's been renting in the city for more than 20 years , and has experienced a multitude of problems , including rats , bug infestations , and lack of heat . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " We 've had to sleep with mitts and tuques on in the dead of winter because there 's no heat , " says the bandleader , who 's married to Souljazz singer-percussionist Marielle Rivard ; they have a three-year-old son . " We 've had all kinds of stuff , even with the baby . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Souljazz , of course , is known for their social commentary -- ever since their BBC-championed 2007 album , Freedom No Go Die , the band has been trying to make the world a better place by injecting messages into their heady brew of sax-loaded Latin- and jazz-laced funk . Three of their previous albums were nominated for Juno Awards . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Chr ? tien grew up in Sudbury and came to Ottawa to study music at university . The band began in 2002 , evolving during a Thursday-night stint at Babylon nightclub on Bank Street in the early 2000s . The core lineup consists of Chr ? tien on organ , piano and vintage keyboards , with saxmen Zakari Frantz , Steve Patterson , Ray Murray and percussionists Philippe Lafreni ? re and Marielle Rivard . Formerly an instrumental act , the members now share vocal duties . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;When asked what keeps them together , Chr ? tien says it boils down to the fact that everyone gets to be creative . " We 're always changing , trying new things , keeping it fresh , " he says . " It 's not the Pierre project , it 's a collective . I think everyone feels involved and motivated . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;On the new record , another influence that 's bubbling to the surface is Afro-punk , evident in the pointed lyrics and raw , vibrant energy of the music . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " A lot of artists are blending classic punk sounds and attitude with more urban and Afro styles , " Chr ? tien says . " I find it really interesting . It sounds like two things that should n't go together -- funky dance music and punk -- but it kinda works in a weird way . That was the musical inspiration for the album . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The band kicked off the album-release tour last month with a terrific show in front of an enthusiastic crowd of young and older fans at their old stomping ground at Babylon . They 're in the area for two nights this weekend at Wakefield 's Black Sheep Inn , then back on the road for dates in Quebec and Ontario . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;In between the two local venues was a journey to Europe , where the band has a label , gets radio play and regularly sells out concerts . It was a jam-packed adventure that included almost 20 shows from Athens to Dublin in less than a month . During our interview , Chr ? tien was still visibly jetlagged as he talked about the pace of the tour . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " Every night you play until two in the morning , then you 're up at seven to run to the airport to go to the next country , do the soundcheck , play the show , go to bed and get maybe two or three hours of sleep , " he said . " It 's hard to think . It 's like you 're drunk on no sleep . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;One highlight was Paris , where they squeezed two concerts into one evening . The first one was at 9 p.m. in the northern suburbs of Paris , followed by a second one east of the city . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " We packed up as quick as we could and they drove us out to the venue . We just jumped on stage , no sound check or anything , and started performing , " Chr ? tien says . " Sonically I do n't know if it was perfect but by that time we had been on tour for a month so everything was second nature . ArtsMusicNAC preview : Matt Mays , at 40 , ready to get ' weirder'http : **31;28810;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;28843;TOOLONG ... title= " Matt Mays. " alt= " Matt Mays. " data-portal-copyright= " Devin-McLean " **28;28879;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1491271 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;NAC Presents Matt Mays : Howl at the Night tour&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;with Skye Wallace&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;8:30 p.m . Nov. 3 , Babs Asper Theatre , National Arts Centre&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canadian rocker Matt Mays is making his way across the country on the first theatre tour of his two-decade-plus career . Dubbed Howl at the Night , the journey brings him and a full band to 18 cities , ending with two shows in hometown Halifax , and including his first appearance at the National Arts Centre . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In this edited interview , the **27;28909;TOOLONG talks about the tour , how his new single , Let There Be Love , came out of his struggle with anxiety , and the liberating effect of turning 40. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : It 's often a challenge for artists to make the jump from playing clubs to theatres . What 's your secret ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : I think it 's just because I 've been around so long . This is my 20th fall tour . The first tour was 1999 , touring across Canada with the Guthries . I 've got a really strong relationship with people who come to the shows , and it 's nice they 're still coming out after all these years . We 've had some really special times in all these towns we 've been playing in for 20 years now . It 's great that people have stayed with me for so long , and they still come out ... especially Ottawa . It was our first town that really started showing up after Halifax . I 'm thankful for that . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Do you get nervous when everyone is sitting there quietly ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Yeah , the silence is weird . The whole pin drop thing , it definitely freaks me out but it also gives a chance for people to listen to some of the lyrics I 've worked really hard on . When you 're in a club , people are usually a bit hosed , or talking and it 's so loud . Do n't get me wrong , I do n't want people to think it 's going to be a super mellow quiet show because we plan to go berserk towards the end as usual . It 's going to be loud and crazy and you might not hear the lyrics . But it 's nice that the songs that I want to come across , it 's a lot easier for me to do that when it 's quieter and people ca n't move to get up . I 've kind of got them there . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Are you bringing a band ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Yeah , it 's the full eight-piece band . I 'm playing the first song solo , and we 're building the show , adding a musician for each of the first eight songs . Then the eight of us are going to play the rest of it together , just to crescendo the show . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Wow , that 's a big band . Why so many players ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : There 's a lot of parts in my tunes , and a lot of bands these days use backing tracks , just hit play on something . But I do n't want to do that . We 're all super close and we 've all toured a lot together this year , and it 's something I 've always wanted to do where no part is left out , whether it 's some percussion or background vocals . It just feels right . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;28938;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;28974;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You just released a cool new song , Let There Be Love . What inspired it ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : A few things , including friends of mine who are amazingly gifted and doing really well in their lives on the outside , but struggling and having a hard time figuring out life , as am I , and a lot of people around me . As I travel , I find I just sort of start leaning on things that are actually real , like friendship and love , and especially self-love , which is a tough one . Like a lot of people , I suffer from some pretty heavy-duty anxiety , which is , I know , ironic because I 'm the singer in a band . But I deal with that a lot and I 'm getting help for it . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : There are actually two versions of the song , one electric and one acoustic , like your last album , Once Upon a Hell of a Time , and its acoustic counterpart . What 's the appeal of doubling your workload ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : I think about music a lot , and I 've always been confused why a song has to end up one way and that has to be it for everybody . I think the process of writing it and putting it down in time , that has to be a real relationship , one on one , but after that , it can be done a million different ways , if it 's done from the heart . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Why release the song now ? Why not wait and put it on an album ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : I felt it was a good time , I did n't want to wait . I know there 's a zillion love songs out there , but this one , to me , has its own kind of niche because it 's about all the different kinds of love , not just love between two people . It 's about the omnipresent love that we should keep nurturing and keep the pilot light going on . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Sounds like a reminder that people could use right now . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Yeah , we have to remind ourselves to love ourselves and other people instead of our phones . I deleted any account that made me feel jealous or envious or anxious in general , and it changed my life . I did n't even know I had anxiety until I was 35 . I worry about young people who ca n't even identify it yet . Call it anxiety , nervousness , fear , whatever you want to call it , it 's a definite feeling and it 's OK to have it . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Is an album in the works , too ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Yeah , we 'll be getting in the studio this winter and get a record finished . I 've got a bunch of songs that I want to get out . I 've been working 9-5 in two studios in Toronto so I 've got a lot of material and the band is primed . I feel super liberated as an artist these days . I 'm just going to release a bunch of music and get weird , and go for it . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You turned 40 this year . Is it possible you 've grown up ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : ( Laughs ) Yeah , something kind of solidifies . To me , a lot of my heroes really mellowed out after 40 but I just want to get weirder , take more chances in music . I think maybe it 's just the times or whatever , but I feel my eccentricities are starting to show themselves more . There 's no dampers on any of it . I 'm not afraid to say no or yes . It 's really a nice feeling , discovering myself a little deeper . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; lsaxberg@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;LISTEN TO THE DOWN TO BUSINESS PODCAST&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " **40;29010;TOOLONG ... ArtsMusicThe Lazys jump into rock stardomhttp : **33;29099;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;29134;TOOLONG ... title= " The Lazys " alt= " The Lazys " data-portal-copyright= " Warner Music Canada " **28;29170;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1485145 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Australian hard-rock band The Lazys have found a second home in Canada , thanks in part to the support of Billy Talent&amp;rsquo ; s Ian D&amp;rsquo ; Sa . He has produced , championed and otherwise supported the band since they first stepped foot on North American soil . As singer Leon Harrison tells Lynn Saxberg in this edited interview , the boost is also helping them crack the international market . Here&amp;rsquo ; s more from the conversation : &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How does a band from Sydney , Australia become one of the hottest new acts in Canada ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : It goes back to 2014-15 , we did a lot of stuff at Canadian Music Week , met a bunch of people , including the one and only Ian D'Sa from Billy Talent . He saw us performing and started up a friendship pretty much directly after that . A few things happened , and we did a couple of songs with him that gave us our start at radio . From there , he was really interested to produce a full-length album , which we did in 2017 . It came out last year , and basically from there , it went to Europe and the U.K. , and Canada continued to support us . It all morphed from a music conference in Toronto . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What do you think makes Canada a good jumping off point for the global music industry ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : There 's a strong music industry in Toronto , really supportive . I guess Ian 's name and expertise was a major draw card , and producing with him was really good . It was a step up for us . And yeah , there 's a lot of rock ' n ' roll radio stations that are very supportive in Canada . It just started clicking . A lot of Australian bands have to move away to get any kind of recognition , and we 're one of them now . They 're more into that indie pop dance thing and we just did n't fit in so we left . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Is Canada a better market for rock ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Everybody loves a good rock band , and now we 're starting to experience that in the Europe and U.K. markets . I think if you write good songs and entertain people in a good old rock ' n roll fashion , they seem to respond . There are lot of rock bands in Canada , and a lot are starting to break through , and they 're hungry and I 'm happy to be part of that . We 're always battling the immortals , the Rolling Stones , AC/DC , Zeppelin , and all the grandpa bands but it boils down to the fact that in their day , they wrote great songs , had great soloing , and put on great shows , so there is a level of expectation if you 're a rock band . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Tell me about Tropical Hazards , the record that Ian D'Sa produced . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : I guess just a lot more time was put into the songwriting . Ian definitely helped . It was basically like a trio , me , him and Matt in the studio and just work until everybody 's happy . If everybody in the room is happy , others who listen will be . We do n't stop until we feel it 's worthy to release . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Amid all the testosterone-driven rock , there 's a sensitive ballad about murdered and missing Indigenous women called Daughter . Where did that come from ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : That kinda stems back to when I went to college . Before I dropped out to tour , I was doing Indigenous studies as part of my degree . I found it interesting because Australia has some of the same issues as Canada , and there 's a big gap between Indigenous and non-Indigenous . I heard about the epidemic in the western part of Canada , where women were going missing , and police were n't trying to find them or figure out what happened . So when you think about , it 's a pretty badass rock n roll song because we 're saying bugger you , we know what 's happening . People are n't stupid . If we get to use the record to voice concerns and issues that happen in society , that 's a good platform . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : The a new video that looks like a highlight reel from your travels over the past year . What kind of year has it been ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : It 's been crazy . That video kind of sums up the last 8-12 months . We 've been across Europe and the U.K. twice this year now . We did our first run of summer festivals through Europe and the U.K. , and played to the biggest crowds we 've ever played to . It was just so good for the band to play to all sorts of different audiences in different countries and meet people and hopefully they join the Lazys thing . They seem to really like what we do live and it translates and they have a good time . Again , that 's all you can do as a rock band . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : The song , Half Mast Blues , has a bit of a message to it , too . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Yeah , it 's pretty funny . It 's one we wanted to attack kinda like The Jack , the AC/DC song where you have a funny topic but you do n't really spell it out to people too obviously . So we made it a pirate and the fact that he continues to get a little drunk with his partner , and has a bit of erectile dysfunction disorder . It was just a bit of tongue in cheek . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What 's your approach to the live show ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Basically just leaving it all on the stage . We 're there to do a job and it 's really fun , and I guess you could relate it to a sporting event . You go out and get a goal , and make the fans happy and take the title and that 's what we do when we play live , and so far , so good . I think when you put your entire self into a performance , and it 's honest and real and engaging , then you ca n't really go wrong . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Is the buzz on the Lazys getting back to Australia now ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : To our demographic , yes . But there 's a lot of lazy people in the music industry there , and the rock radio system . Excuse the pun . They still play Creed and Live and all those bands nobody gives a shit about anymore . The emphasis is n't on bringing new talent . It 's a small place . There 's a lot of venues that shoot people down , neighbours that complain , gaming machines that take priority . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : I 'm curious to know if you had any connections in Canada before you decided to come to music week . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Not really . We just heard about this music conference , with bands getting opportunities from it , and nothing was really happening in Australia . We 'd done similar events in Australia and just been overlooked so it was kind of our calling card . But also at the time , it was a make or break situation as to whether we continued . Then we met Ian and he fell in love with the band , and we picked up a great agent and record label and it all started falling into place . The workload did n't get any easier but we stepped into the professional landscape . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;The Lazys&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;with Inire and Taming Sari&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **33;29200;TOOLONG : Wednesday , Oct. 16 , 8 p.m. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Where : &lt;/strong&gt; Brass Monkey , 250A Greenbank Rd. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tickets &amp; info&lt;/strong&gt; : &lt;a href= " http : //eventbrite.com " &gt;eventbrite.co ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN ARTS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29235;TOOLONG ... bets , Oct. 17 to 23 : Tegan and Sara , and a Korean film fest&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29270;TOOLONG ... new at the National Gallery : Six decades of photography in Japan , and Canada 's New Generation award winners&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29305;TOOLONG ... ArtsMusicNAC preview -- Sarah McLachlan : ' I want to suck the marrow out of every day'http : **36;29387;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;29425;TOOLONG ... title= " Sarah McLachlan . " alt= " Sarah McLachlan . " data-portal-copyright= " Kharen Hill " **28;29461;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1475865 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;NAC Gala&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Sarah McLachlan&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Also performing : National Ballet of Canada principle dancer Greta Hodgkinson , singer-songwriter isk ? , actor Mani Soleymanlou and conductor Alexander Shelley with the NAC Orchestra&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;When and where : 6:30 p.m . Saturday , Southam Hall , National Arts Centre&lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;Tickets : Limited seats remain , priced around $200 , available at NAC box office and ticketmaster.ca . Includes pre-concert reception at 5:30 p.m. and post-concert dance . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; Superstar songstress Sarah McLachlan is taking a break from her mom duties and music-school responsibilities to come to Ottawa to star in the National Arts Centre&amp;rsquo ; s golden-anniversary gala on Saturday , an annual fundraiser for the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s Youth and Education Trust . The Canadian Music Hall of Famer is bringing her band , which includes Whitehorse members Luke Doucet and Melissa McClelland , and will also perform with the NAC Orchestra . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Lynn Saxberg caught up with the 51-year-old musician to talk about playing with symphonies , the rewards and challenges of running a music school , and how being happy makes it tough to write introspective songs . Here&amp;rsquo ; s an edited version of the interview . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You are no stranger to symphony shows ; in fact , you did some over the summer . Do you enjoy presenting your music with the ultimate wall of sound behind you ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Yeah , it&amp;rsquo ; s such a fun way to present my music , to have that immense beauty and power behind you when you&amp;rsquo ; re performing . It feels pretty spectacular . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : The National Arts Centre has been commissioning charts so that emerging artists can play with symphonies . How many of your songs have charts ? What do you think of that idea ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Probably about 25 of my songs are charted , including about eight Christmas songs . It&amp;rsquo ; s a great hybrid . If theatre and symphonies want to continue to live , they need to be able to engage different audiences . I think the idea of stepping away from purely classical music , and delving into the pop world , or different genres , to get new audiences in and become aware of the beauty and amazingness of it , is great . We need to figure out new , innovative ways to keep bringing people in and growing as artists . It&amp;rsquo ; s all part of the big picture . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;29491;TOOLONG ... title= " Sarah McLachlan . " alt= " Sarah McLachlan . " data-portal-copyright= " Kharen Hill " **28;29527;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1475865 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Do you have formal training in your background ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Yeah , I spent 12 years studying classical guitar , six years of piano and eight years of theory . I went to the Maritime Conservatory of Music . It was the only thing available . I stuck with it until I was 17. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Now you run the Sarah McLachlan School of Music , which provides free musical training to at-risk children and youths . How is that going ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : It&amp;rsquo ; s amazing , thank you . We have three schools now . Vancouver is the mothership , and Surrey and Edmonton are smaller &amp;mdash ; they&amp;rsquo ; re after-school programs . We&amp;rsquo ; re in our 18th year and we serve over 1,000 kids over all our programs . It&amp;rsquo ; s an amazing thing to be part of , to be able to create a culture and space for kids to be able to experience what it is to play music , not only by yourself but together with other people . There&amp;rsquo ; s persistence and resilience in working hard at something and having that sense of achievement , and also going out in front of your peers and performing a song that you&amp;rsquo ; ve written yourself . It creates empathy , understanding and inclusivity and it&amp;rsquo ; s a beautiful thing to be part of . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You must have some success stories after 18 years . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Absolutely . We have lots of successes that are musically driven but we also have sometimes more powerful stories , like when a kid is transitioning , has no friends and hasn&amp;rsquo ; t really been able to speak about it . Then three years later , they&amp;rsquo ; re graduating , standing up in front of a room singing a song that they wrote about their experience , and saying , &amp;lsquo ; There&amp;rsquo ; s no way I would have survived if I didn&amp;rsquo ; t have this place , this support , this second family of kids and teachers who believed in me and let me be me. &amp;rsquo ; I get goosebumps . I&amp;rsquo ; ve got so many stories like that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Do you have any plans to expand the school to other cities ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Right now in Edmonton and Surrey , we&amp;rsquo ; re still in regular schools . It&amp;rsquo ; s amazing to have that space but it&amp;rsquo ; s a little more limited . So we&amp;rsquo ; re looking for permanent space in both of those locations . Another thing we&amp;rsquo ; re really trying to do is build a different kind of fundraising model because up to now , I&amp;rsquo ; ve been doing most of it and it&amp;rsquo ; s just not sustainable . There&amp;rsquo ; s only one of me and there are three schools . But , for the first time , we did a fundraiser this year where we netted enough to cover our annual operating budget a year ahead . Which is huge . We&amp;rsquo ; ve never been in that position before . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What about your music career ? Are you working on anything these days ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Yes . I&amp;rsquo ; m slowly chipping away at writing for a new record . I don&amp;rsquo ; t feel any burning need to finish it . I always have a bit of a block when it comes to making a record because I know when you make a record , it means leaving . It means going on tour , going to promote it , and having two teenagers at home , one doesn&amp;rsquo ; t want to leave for very long . You need to be around if s&amp;ndash ; t hits the fan . Things can go south pretty quick . I just feel like I want to be home . I&amp;rsquo ; m really happy right now , too . So that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t really help . Maybe next year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Being happy is a problem ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Unfortunately and fortunately , when I&amp;rsquo ; m in trauma or something terrible is happening , or I&amp;rsquo ; m sad or upset , there are always lots of opportunities to mine that and write about it , and figure out a way through it . But there&amp;rsquo ; s not a lot of that going on right now . Nobody&amp;rsquo ; s dying , I&amp;rsquo ; m healthy , the kids are healthy . Life is absolutely fantastic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You do n't mind being in your 50s ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Other than my body pissing me off because it doesn&amp;rsquo ; t work as well as it used to , it&amp;rsquo ; s pretty amazing . I love psychologically where I&amp;rsquo ; m at . Things that used to bother me just don&amp;rsquo ; t matter now , and I&amp;rsquo ; m way better at looking at what&amp;rsquo ; s important , and how to spend my time . I feel incredibly lucky . I want to suck the marrow out of every day , especially the days that we are feeling good and healthy and strong . I just want to make the most of it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Last question : There 's been some reflection on the impact of Lilith Fair recently . Would you consider reviving it ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : People are always asking me to bring it back but again , it&amp;rsquo ; s bandwidth . I was 27 years old and didn&amp;rsquo ; t have any kids , and had way more time on my hands . I think it would be great for a lot of reasons to bring it back but I honestly think it would take someone of a younger generation to spearhead it . I feel like if Taylor Swift or Lizzo wanted to take on something like this and be all about women&amp;rsquo ; s empowerment and equality and inclusiveness , then hell yeah . I could get on board with that . I just don&amp;rsquo ; t know if I could spearhead it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; lsaxberg@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29557;TOOLONG ... ArtsMusicRIP , jazz piano great Harold Mabernhttp : **34;29709;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;29745;TOOLONG ... title= " Jazz pianist Harold Mabern plays Salt Restaurant on Preston Street Aug. 15 with Toronto saxophonist Kirk MacDonald " alt= " Jazz pianist Harold Mabern plays Salt Restaurant on Preston Street Aug. 15 with Toronto saxophonist Kirk MacDonald " data-portal-copyright= " Alan Nahigian " **28;29781;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 593651 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Harold Mabern , a Memphis-raised pianist beloved for his soulfulness and power at the keyboard and his gift of gab off the bandstand , has died , his record label Smoke Sessions Records announced Thursday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mabern , who continued to tour , record and play in New York&amp;rsquo ; s jazz clubs with players half his age , was 83 . WBGO&amp;rsquo ; s Nate Chinen reports &lt;a href= " https : **33;29811;TOOLONG ... that Mabern died of a heart attack , and that he is survived by two children and a granddaughter , while his wife , Beatrice , died in 2010. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Word of Mabern&amp;rsquo ; s passing prompted tributes throughout the online jazz community . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29846;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29881;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29916;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;29951;TOOLONG ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Guitarist Peter Bernstein wrote on Facebook : &amp;ldquo ; Mr. Mabes I am having trouble finding words to say goodbye to you . It&amp;rsquo ; s hard to imagine the world without you . A true master of music but also of giving , you are generosity personified . All we can do is remember you and try to be better people . R.I.P . Maestro Mabern. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;div&gt;Born on March 20 , 1936 , the musically self-taught Mabern grew up under the influence of the stellar pianist Phineas Newborn Jr . and was soon running with such peers as Frank Strozier , Booker Little and George Coleman . Mabern and Coleman were friends throughout the pianist 's lifetime , and Mabern plays on Coleman 's upcoming album , The Quartet . &lt;/div&gt; &lt;div&gt;&lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;&lt;br&gt; Mabern moved to Chicago in 1954 , where he played with such elite saxophonists as Johnny Griffin , Gene Ammons and Clifford Jordan . Five years later , he moved to New York , where he would join the groups of Lionel Hampton and Art Farmer and Benny Golson 's Jazztet , Miles Davis and Wes Montgomery . **35;29986;TOOLONG ... &lt;div&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 480 " src= " https : **34;30023;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;30059;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;div&gt;&lt;/div&gt; &lt;div&gt;Mabern released more than 20 albums as a leader . A favourite of mine is the trio album Straight Street , a Japanese recording that also features bassist Ron Carter and drummer Jack DeJohnette . Mabern appears on almost 100 albums as a sideman. &lt;/div&gt; &lt;div&gt; Mabern taught for more than three decades at New Jersey 's William Paterson University , where his students included drummers Joe Farnsworth and saxophonist Eric Alexander , two younger musicians who would join him on innumerable performances after they graduated . &lt;/div&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Until his passing , Mabern was the quintessential New York jazzman working in the trenches , playing past midnight at Smalls Jazz Club or Smoke , two bastions of straight-ahead , swinging music . &lt;br&gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;30095;TOOLONG ... title= " Harold Mabern , hitting hard at Smalls in September 2017 " alt= " Harold Mabern , hitting hard at Smalls in September 2017 " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;30131;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1243172 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;In recent years&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; , Mabern developed more connections with Canada 's jazz scene . He played and recorded with saxophonists Kirk MacDonald and Cory Weeds , and is featured on two of MacDonald 's most recent albums , including the Juno-winning Vista Obscura . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Here are clips of Mabern with MacDonald ( playing in Montreal ) and Weeds ( playing in Vancouver ) , throwing himself into some minor blues with his driving , swirling approach . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;30161;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;30197;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;30233;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;30269;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; On Facebook , MacDonald wrote : &amp;ldquo ; I was shocked and deeply saddened to hear the devastating news of Harold Mabern&amp;rsquo ; s passing . We have lost a musical giant ! Harold&amp;rsquo ; s spirit and unconditional generosity with his gifts and wisdom was something to behold . Harold was a torchbearer who was an inspiration to his peers and a great mentor and inspiration to so many musicians of all generations around the world for decades . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I feel fortunate to have known Harold and honoured to have shared the bandstand with him numerous times over the past five years . My deepest condolences to the Mabern family and Harold&amp;rsquo ; s extended musical family . Thank you Harold for the music and inspiration . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mabern played with MacDonald in Ottawa in the summer of 2015 . I was fortunate enough to interview him in advance of that gig , and below is the story that resulted . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; *** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Harold Mabern was a late starter when it came to jazz piano , but he 's more than made up for it with his longevity . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Brooklyn-based pianist , 79 , didn&amp;rsquo ; t start playing his instrument until he was 15 , growing up in Memphis , Tennessee . But within a decade , the self-taught musician was accompanying the cream of the jazz crop in New York , right up to Miles Davis and Sonny Rollins , as well as singers Sarah Vaughan and Betty Carter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the last decade , he&amp;rsquo ; s only grown busier , recording as a leader and sideman and touring , frequently with former students whom&amp;nbsp ; he taught at William Paterson University in New Jersey . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His appeal extends beyond the United States , such that Toronto saxophonist Kirk MacDonald enlisted Mabern to play on his most recent record , &lt;em&gt;Vista Obscura&lt;/em&gt; . This spring , that album won a Juno Award for best jazz album of the year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He&amp;rsquo ; s just such a great personality , &amp;rdquo ; MacDonald says of Mabern. &amp;ldquo ; His energy is infectious . It can be overwhelming &amp;hellip ; just his love for life and music . He&amp;rsquo ; s really one of the sweetest people you would ever meet . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; MacDonald and Mabern are touring&amp;nbsp ; this week and next , playing gigs from Sydney , N.S. , to Toronto . In Ottawa , the duo plays Salt Dining Lounge on Preston Street Saturday night . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Mabern , an effusive talker and storyteller who recently returned from a two-week tour in Japan , happily discussed his life as a jazzman ; an edited transcript of our&amp;nbsp ; conversation follows . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;How did you get started playing piano ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m completely self-taught . No shame in my game . When I was 15 , I finally got a piano for about $50 , but I still really didn&amp;rsquo ; t know what I was doing . At the time , I think I knew about four songs . &amp;nbsp ; Unfortunately , I didn&amp;rsquo ; t have the luxury of playing Chopin Etudes. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Do you play classical music now ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Oh no . Most jazz piano players play classical music but I don&amp;rsquo ; t fool with it . I do love classical music . Chopin is my favourite and Ravel and Debussy , and Gustav Mahler . But maybe one day I&amp;rsquo ; ll sit down and pick some notes out and see what I can do . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;How did you progress so quickly as a jazz pianist ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When I moved to Chicago , that&amp;rsquo ; s when I started putting time into it . In &amp;rsquo ; 54 , I moved to Chicago . &amp;nbsp ; Music was being played in Chicago 24/7. &amp;nbsp ; That&amp;rsquo ; s when I really learned how to play music . &amp;nbsp ; Music was on every corner . You had great pianists on every corner who could play . The camaraderie was very good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chicago , it&amp;rsquo ; s very diverse . You had to play all kinds of music . You had to play blues . You had to play for singers . I tell students the best way to be a great jazz pianist is to play for singers . That will teach you how to be a very good accompanist . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Memphis , we had to play rhythm &amp;lsquo ; n&amp;rsquo ; blues . We didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to play rhythm &amp;lsquo ; n&amp;rsquo ; blues . We wanted to play bebop . And then as you look back , you say , &amp;ldquo ; Oh boy , what a pleasure , &amp;rdquo ; because as you know everybody can&amp;rsquo ; t play the blues . You can&amp;rsquo ; t teach that . It&amp;rsquo ; s something you can do or can&amp;rsquo ; t do and it has to do with the environment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Chicago , all the musicians could play anybody&amp;rsquo ; s music . How did that happen ? I don&amp;rsquo ; t know . We just listened . If Dizzy Gillespie came and Wynton Kelly , my hero , couldn&amp;rsquo ; t make it , I could go in and play the whole book without the music . If Bobby Timmons couldn&amp;rsquo ; t finish the gig with Art Blakey , I could play that music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We were playing and practising music 12 hours a day . I had a lot to do to get ready for&amp;nbsp ; New York . I&amp;rsquo ; m still getting ready for New York . You never stop learning . The day you stop being a student , you might as well pack it in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;How did you start making a mark in New York ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; My first gig was with Harry &amp;ldquo ; Sweets&amp;rdquo ; Edison. &amp;nbsp ; One night ( saxophonist ) Cannonball Adderley said , &amp;ldquo ; Hey , Big Hands , you want a gig ? &amp;rdquo ; He took me down to Birdland . Tuesday night , the place was packed . Must have been 15 piano players in Birdland that night . Cannonball introduced me to &amp;ldquo ; Sweets&amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; Sweets&amp;rdquo ; says , &amp;ldquo ; You want to play ? &amp;rdquo ; I say &amp;ldquo ; yeah . &amp;rdquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m nervous . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I tell young students now , the old-timers assumed if you&amp;rsquo ; re a musician , you knew everything . They didn&amp;rsquo ; t ask you what you knew . So &amp;ldquo ; Sweets&amp;rdquo ; looked at me and he said , &amp;ldquo ; Habit . Eight-bar introduction . In A-flat. &amp;rdquo ; I thought , what&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; Habit ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The song was &lt;em&gt;You 're Getting To Be A Habit To Me&lt;/em&gt; . I fumbled the first chorus . The second chorus , I had it . He hired me on the spot . That was the first song I played in New York City . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;What was it like to play with Miles Davis in the early 1960s ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I can&amp;rsquo ; t believe that the six weeks I worked with Miles nobody had a tape recorder there to record ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a wonderful experience for me playing with Miles . He was very inspirational to me . He was saying ( imitates Davis&amp;rsquo ; raspy voice ) : &amp;ldquo ; You sure can swing . &amp;rdquo ; If Miles Davis was saying I can swing , that&amp;rsquo ; s all I needed to know . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;You 're coming to Canada right after a two-week tour of Japan . How was that ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; We call New York the Big Apple , but as far as we&amp;rsquo ; re concerned , my friends and I , we say Tokyo , Japan , kicks New York&amp;rsquo ; s butt . First of all , there&amp;rsquo ; s 14 million people there . But the thing is , the people over there are so honest . Their mindset is they&amp;rsquo ; re so honourable , they take such great pride in their work . They treat you like a super-duper human being . I always tell people , in Japan they&amp;rsquo ; ve got money for two things : tall buildings and jazz . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; ve been over there 27 times . I love me some Tokyo , Japan , and when we come back to the United States , I get depressed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;How are you enjoying playing with Kirk MacDonald ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Oh , love it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This date I did with him , that&amp;rsquo ; s probably the hardest record date that I&amp;rsquo ; ve ever done . He wrote some music , man . He&amp;rsquo ; s got one tune &amp;hellip ; I thought , &amp;ldquo ; If I can&amp;rsquo ; t hear this song , I can read it . &amp;rdquo ; I was up all night . It was only this one song , with a couple of bars I just couldn&amp;rsquo ; t get . Finally ( bassist ) Neil Swainson told me how to look at it and we were able to get two takes . I said , &amp;ldquo ; Sshh , don&amp;rsquo ; t nobody say a word because I don&amp;rsquo ; t want to have to do another . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He&amp;rsquo ; s a very challenging player . Excellent tenor player . It&amp;rsquo ; s definitely an enjoyable moment to play with him . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;You 'll turn 80 next year . Do you expect you 'll slow down ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The only time I get tired is when I&amp;rsquo ; m not playing . I&amp;rsquo ; m blessed . I&amp;rsquo ; m booked up for the most part until April 2016 . As long as I feel I can work , let me work . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; *** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Rest in peace , Harold Mabern. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;30305;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **36;30336;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : //twitter.com/peterhum " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **30;30374;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;br&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **28;30406;TOOLONG " target= " blank " rel= " noopener " **30;30436;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumFri , 20 Sep 2019 21:33:15 **45;30468;TOOLONG ... Plant plays CityFolk : ' I 'll probably retire when I run out of breath'http : **33;30515;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;30550;TOOLONG ... title= " Robert Plant . " alt= " Robert Plant . " data-portal-copyright= " mads perch " **28;30586;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1463799 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Robert Plant &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; 9:15 p.m . Sunday , City Stage , CityFolk , Lansdowne Park &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tickets and info : &lt;a href= " http : //cityfolkfestival.com " &gt;cityfol ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; *** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;When it comes to working into one 's sunset years , Robert Plant relates more to Bob Dylan than Elton John . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Although the 71-year-old rock legend expressed the utmost respect for his fellow Brit , John , who 's 72 and circumnavigating the globe on an epic farewell tour , the former Led Zeppelin frontman said he 's nowhere near ready to follow his footsteps . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " Elton is looking for more time to spend with his family , and that 's not a bad idea , " Plant said in an interview . I have n't reached a point where I 've got nothing left , and I feel pretty good about what I do . I love to tour and I love to sing and twist the songs around . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;It 's a mindset that puts him more in tune with 78-year-old Dylan , who once gave Plant the advice to keep going as long as possible . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " I respect and admire him , not only for waking me up as a kid , a teenager , but also for the fact that he takes such joy in re-entering his own adventures from a different angle . ' " Dylan asked him . " ' You got ta keep going . ' &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Play , and let the music take you to fine people and introduce you to the underbelly of all these areas ' cultures . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " I 'll probably retire when I run out of breath . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;That does n't seem to be happening any time soon . Plant 's most recent album , 2017 's Carry Fire , recorded with his Sensational Space Shifters band , finds him at a creative peak . His voice is as strong and supple as ever , and the music brims with vitality , meandering purposefully between psychedelia , folk and blues . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;To get to that point , he feels it 's important to leave space for spontaneity in the studio . He does n't want to have things too mapped out . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " It 's pretty nebulous and non-definable , clutching stuff and bringing it out of the air , and laying it down in some form or another with instruments , " says the musical mastermind . " It takes a myriad of different forms to get to the point in the song where you think you 've actually got it . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " There 's an air of adventure , and I think with contemporary recording techniques , you can create impressions as a song develops its stature and its shape takes place . You can hang all sorts of different ideas on it as it grows and blossoms . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;His creative process often involves showing up to the session early . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " I go in fresh every morning . Sometimes I gave myself an hour or two before the guys came in to work on various tracks , and just moved things around , switched stuff about . Really , it 's almost like a watercolour painting . You may actually add another colour before the colour is dry for a different effect . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Plant has always been an artist who prefers to talk about his newest material instead of revisiting the past . But he was encouraged by his label to explore his five-decade output in a new podcast that debuted this year . Each episode of Digging Deep with Robert Plant finds the singer-songwriter talking to a journalist about a specific song . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " I always deal in the current , present tense , and I 'm only ever really getting excited about what I 'm actually doing right now so I never thought about the idea of visiting the stuff again , " he says . " But every song has got a tale , and when I think about all the previous albums , all of them had some kind of attitude , whether it was trying to grasp the 80s or courting technology or not meeting with the approval of the Led Zeppelin fans at large . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " So I listen to the songs and think , ' Wow , those guys were great players . ' It 's nice to look at that stuff . I like the idea of visiting tracks with an interest in them . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;As for the current tour , Plant is looking forward to bringing the Sensational Space Shifters to Canada , though there are just two dates this time , Ottawa 's CityFolk and Fredericton 's Harvest Jazz and Blues Festival , before he continues into the U.S. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " I only go where I want to go , " says the Rock ' n ' Roll Hall of Famer . " I remember playing Winnipeg and , I think , Calgary in Zeppelin . Towns carry the personality of the weather , the climate and the culture swings with the seasons . Some regions are tough to live in and they have a different kind of crowd . The audience has a different kind of tenacity about them . Canada is riveting really because it 's quite dynamic along that long , long journey from east to west . A social media success story&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The old story about unknown bands getting discovered by jaded A&amp;amp ; Rs in dimly lit venues is mostly a thing of the past . From his sleepy Toronto suburb , Mendes developed a following the modern way : posting acoustic guitar covers on defunct social media app Vine , famous for its hard six-second time limit . His elevator pitch worked , as he amassed millions of followers , a manager and label deal with Island Records thanks to his online exploits . That was in 2014 &amp;ndash ; today , Mendes is approaching a whopping 50 million followers on Instagram , putting him alongside compatriots Justin Bieber and Drake among the most-followed Instagram accounts on Earth . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h3&gt;2 . A star-laden affair&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; The latest album from Mendes offers a who&amp;rsquo ; s who of young pop stars and behind-the-scenes hitmakers . Fallin&amp;rsquo ; All in You features a co-write from none other than Ed Sheeran , while Like to Be You was produced by John Mayer . Ryan Tedder of OneRepublic , Julia Michaels and Teddy Geiger &amp;ndash ; all mainstays on the singles charts as songwriters &amp;ndash ; also have their fingerprints on this release . Mendes giveth as well , guesting on Chance the Rapper&amp;rsquo ; s new album The Big Day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;31489;TOOLONG ... title= " Camila Cabello. " alt= " Camila Cabello. A little plain and that 's OK&lt;/h3&gt; &lt;p&gt; Pop stardom demands burning the candle at both ends , but the clean cut Mendes comes across as an early to bed type . I always &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;liked the big harmony sound . " I saw Ray Charles doing Georgia on my Mind and my skin went to goosebumps , " she recalls . " ' Oh my God , it 's amazing , ' I thought , and I wanted &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;to do the same thing . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Little &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;by little , I got deeper into the blues and was listening to Koko Taylor and Bonnie Raitt and of course some soul music -- Aretha Franklin -- and then the guitar stuff started to kick in. " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;There 's also growth in the music , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;with elements of jazz and progressive rock enhancing her unique , blues-based style . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " I feel that musically I have also &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;taken steps towards something new and that 's very fascinating . ArtsMusic'I 'm the last one ' : VJ 's piano bar plays its final notehttp : **36;32190;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;32228;TOOLONG ... title= " For nearly a quarter century , Viger Gendron owned and operated VJ 's piano bar on Laurier Avenue W. The bar closed last month . " alt= " For nearly a quarter century , Viger Gendron owned and operated VJ 's piano bar on Laurier Avenue W. The bar closed last month . " data-portal-copyright= " Bruce Deachman " **28;32264;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1444585 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Gatineau Club in Aylmer was among the hottest nightclubs in the Ottawa area in 1955 . Duke Ellington performed there that year , as did Josephine Baker , Tony Bennett , Billy Eckstine and Louis Armstrong . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Into this swirling , smoky world of jazz orchestras and pop vocalists , 18-year-old Viger Gendron came of age , waiting on tables and serving drinks while soaking up such hits as Bennett&amp;rsquo ; s Rags to Riches , Ellington&amp;rsquo ; s Satin Doll , and Satchmo&amp;rsquo ; s rendition of I Get Ideas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Because of you , &amp;rdquo ; Gendron sings , imitating Bennett , &amp;ldquo ; there&amp;rsquo ; s a song in my heart . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Gendron never abandoned the Great American Songbook , but the public&amp;rsquo ; s appetite for it ebbed . As a result , in late July this year , months shy of its 25th anniversary , Gendron closed his Laurier Avenue piano bar , VJ&amp;rsquo ; s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s the end of an era , &amp;rdquo ; he says , citing other Vegas-style piano bars in the area whose closures preceded his : Friday&amp;rsquo ; s Roast Beef House on Elgin Street ; the Beacon Arms Hotel&amp;rsquo ; s La Bibliotheque on Albert Street . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m the last one . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Surely there are others , but it&amp;rsquo ; s true that the sort of music lounge that Billy Joel sang about in his autobiographical hit song Piano Man has increasingly become an artifact . Today , you can peer through VJ&amp;rsquo ; s windows and see hints of the unpretentious , anachronistic bar that was . A small disco ball hangs from the ceiling , while eight empty chairs remain clustered around a grand piano , as if hoping for customers to call out another tune or put a last bill in the large glass resting atop its quiet lid . The piano&amp;rsquo ; s keys are absent , removed to make room for the electronic keyboard that could be slotted in their place , rendering the grand little more than a large mood-setting drink-holder. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Left to the imagination are the scores of photos of actors and musicians &amp;mdash ; Marilyn Monroe , Clint Eastwood , Clark Gable , Louis Armstrong , even an autographed Sinatra &amp;mdash ; that once covered the forest-green walls . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the floor near the piano , meanwhile , lies a discarded sheet of paper with the lyrics to George and Ira Gershwin&amp;rsquo ; s 1920s standard &amp;lsquo ; S Wonderful printed on it : &amp;ldquo ; You make my life so glamorous . You can&amp;rsquo ; t blame me for feeling amorous ! Wonderful , marvelous , that you should care for me ! &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Over the years , countless people in the mood for a melody came through the doors of VJ&amp;rsquo ; s , where Gendron , quick with a joke or to light up your smoke , held court . Just like at the Gatineau Club so many decades before , he tended bar and served tables . He&amp;rsquo ; d sing , too &amp;mdash ; Engelbert Humperdinck&amp;rsquo ; s After the Lovin&amp;rsquo ; , for example &amp;mdash ; while couples of a certain age danced wherever they could find room . Eventually , however , fewer and fewer people showed up . The Gershwin glamour wore off . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The younger crowd don&amp;rsquo ; t come to piano bars , &amp;rdquo ; he says . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s the older , middle-age people , from 50 to 70. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He adds that shorter lunchtimes for nearby public servants , coupled with stricter laws for impaired driving enacted last December , have further quieted business . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not like it was years ago , when we&amp;rsquo ; d pack them in on Friday nights . Now people have big mortgages and don&amp;rsquo ; t go out so much , and they just talk with each other on their computers and cellphones . And now if you have even one beer and drive , you might be charged . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;32294;TOOLONG ... title= " For nearly a quarter century , Viger Gendron owned and operated VJ 's piano bar on Laurier Avenue W. The bar closed last month . " alt= " For nearly a quarter century , Viger Gendron owned and operated VJ 's piano bar on Laurier Avenue W. The bar closed last month . " data-portal-copyright= " Bruce Deachman " **28;32330;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1444587 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; There were other opportunities over the years . Named Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s high school athlete of the year in 1953 , Gendron pursued careers in football and hockey . In 1956 , he played a couple of pre-season games with the Montreal Alouettes before signing with the Sarnia Golden Bears . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the winter he played hockey , initially with Toronto St. Michael&amp;rsquo ; s of the OHA , before moving on to the Hamilton Tiger Cubs , Chatham Maroons and St. Catharines Teepees , at the latter alongside Bobby Hull and Stan Mikita . Hockey eventually took him to the U.S. , where he played for teams in the International , Eastern and Western hockey leagues : The Louisville Rebels , Troy Bruins , Muskegon Zephyrs , Toledo Blades , New Haven Blades , Charlotte Clippers and Los Angeles Blades . A tough blueliner nicknamed &amp;ldquo ; The Tiger&amp;rdquo ; and &amp;ldquo ; Fritz&amp;rdquo ; Gendron spent his share of time in penalty boxes from coast to coast , while a stickfight that cost him a month-long suspension saw him , in 1959 , try his luck with the Wembley Lions of the British National League . The league folded in 1960. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alas , an NHL tryout eluded him . &amp;ldquo ; There were only six teams , &amp;rdquo ; he explains . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the music was never far away . Although not well paid , his hockey career allowed him to spend a summer month one year in Las Vegas , where he attended shows by some of his favourite performers , including Frank Sinatra. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After his hockey career ended , he worked for a while for the Teamsters as a dock supervisor in San Pedro , California . But his wife , Shirley , who died almost four years ago , convinced him to move back to Ottawa , where her family was . And so Gendron , a lifelong non-drinker , returned to work in bars before opening his own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What now , my love , &amp;rdquo ; he sings , the opening line to Sinatra&amp;rsquo ; s 1966 cover version of the song of the same name . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; What now for the nearly 83-year-old Gendron ? He stays in shape and says he could work as a consultant at a gym close to his Centretown apartment . And there&amp;rsquo ; s a nearby bar where he&amp;rsquo ; s been offered night shifts , though he adds he&amp;rsquo ; s had enough of the 12- and 14-hour days that he regularly put in at VJ&amp;rsquo ; s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And while his music is from the past , he says he doesn&amp;rsquo ; t live there , preferring to look forward . &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s how you stay young . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And so , to his former customers who may be wondering where he&amp;rsquo ; s gone , he simply offers this : &amp;ldquo ; I might see you again , somewhere . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **30;32360;TOOLONG " **37;32392;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32431;TOOLONG ... candidates to interview for Ottawa police chief&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32466;TOOLONG ... double-dealing , death : An excerpt from the mystery novel Spiked&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32501;TOOLONG ... bar Hooley 's closes , owner blames Elgin Street construction&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Bruce DeachmanMon , 12 Aug 2019 10:49:58 **45;32536;TOOLONG ... " alt= " Pianist Hinrich Alpers plays Beethoven sonatas July 30 and Aug. 1 in Carleton Dominion-Chalmers Centre . " data-portal-copyright= " Hannes Caspar " **28;32653;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1434976 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You may find it hard to believe , but as a teenager I really didn&amp;rsquo ; t enjoy playing Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s piano music all that much , &amp;rdquo ; says German pianist Hinrich Alpers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fortunately Alpers has seen the light . After all , the Berlin-based 38-year-old will play two &amp;ldquo ; marathon&amp;rdquo ; concerts of Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s piano sonatas at this year&amp;rsquo ; s Chamberfest , performing 15 of the master&amp;rsquo ; s piano sonatas over two afternoons next week . Alpers , an audience favourite over the years at the festival is to return next year and the year after to complete his overview of the Beethoven sonatas. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below , Alpers offers his take on Beethoven , Ottawa audiences and what he&amp;rsquo ; s been cooking lately . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Q : What are your earliest memories of Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s music ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : &amp;ldquo ; My&amp;rdquo ; beloved Beethoven came as a music cassette for Christmas when I had just started to play the piano , and it told the story of Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s life and his music . As it happens , it may have influenced me rather subconsciously , as I am now myself giving concerts and talks about Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s life and works all the time ! I particularly remember the &amp;ldquo ; Thunderstorm&amp;rdquo ; movement of the Sixth Symphony . It amazed me so much that the Sixth is now my favourite symphony . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Q : What place do Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s sonatas have your repertoire ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : The sonatas are , of course , a cornerstone in piano literature , and as such I love them all dearly ! The whole cycle of Beethoven sonatas holds a special place in my musical universe because it enables us&amp;nbsp ; &amp;mdash ; the audience and myself &amp;mdash ; to go on a time journey through Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s life together . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From the very beginning of his career all the way into his 50s ( the so-called &amp;ldquo ; late&amp;rdquo ; Beethoven appreciated all over the world ) , he composed piano sonatas , and I like to follow him on that particular path through his life again and again . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; This year in Ottawa , we&amp;rsquo ; ll make the first half of that journey together , with the rest to follow next year and the year after that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Q : Do you have any concerns about the &amp;ldquo ; marathon&amp;rdquo ; nature of the concerts ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I&amp;rsquo ; m not concerned at all because with the two intermissions each and my introductions in between I don&amp;rsquo ; t see them really as &amp;ldquo ; marathon&amp;rdquo ; concerts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But you are mentioning a very interesting point , as I have heard actual marathon Beethoven sonatas performances &amp;mdash ; all sonatas within a day . While being rather a sportive achievement , I doubt that those have succeeded quite as much artistically , which is why I am giving some room to breathe in between . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Q : You have been a regular visitor to perform in Ottawa for more than a decade . What do you think of the audiences here ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : What a lovely chance for me to return the many compliments that I&amp;rsquo ; ve received during the past 11 years ! Well , audiences in Ottawa are just terrific , as they are not only friendly and welcoming but also so knowledgeable and patient . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; During my very first year in Ottawa , I had an encounter that sums up the entire spirit of the Ottawa Chamberfest and its audience to me . It was my first concert , and I went for my dress rehearsal at St. John the Evangelist , in pouring rain , and saw a long line of people in front of the door , all in raincoats and with umbrellas . At first I believed I had arrived at the wrong place . But then I was told they&amp;rsquo ; d all been waiting for an hour already in order to get the best seats to hear my performance . Isn&amp;rsquo ; t that lovely ? Ottawa Chamberfest and I were love at first sight ! &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Q : Your website notes that you listen to everything from Renaissance choral music to 21st century jazz . What appeals to you about these kinds of music that you don&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily play ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Every bit of music that I hear might eventually reflect in an interpretation of something else . I have always loved to listen to jazz , and for my own pleasure I also play quite a bit of it . There&amp;rsquo ; s an element of fun and implicitness in it which I believe I&amp;rsquo ; d like to allow to rub off on my actual &amp;ldquo ; classic&amp;rdquo ; pianism which I perform in public . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Naturally , while I studied in New York , I found myself in a rather perfect environment &amp;mdash ; I went to hear many of my jazz musician friends&amp;rsquo ; performances , and they&amp;rsquo ; re also the artists that I still follow and listen to . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Q : Your website also says that you enjoy culinary pursuits . What have you been up to in the kitchen ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I have started to dig into some Vietnamese cooking ! Having been there a few times , there are some flavours that I felt I needed more regularly , and over the internet , many of the recipes for my favourite dishes are easy to find . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Essential Beethoven : Hinrich Alpers &lt;br&gt; When : Tuesday , July 30 , at 1 p.m. and Thursday , Aug. 1 , at 1 p.m. &lt;br&gt; Where : Carleton Dominion-Chalmers Centre &lt;br&gt; Tickets and info : &lt;a href= " http : //chamberfest.com " &gt;chamberfest. ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; phum@postmedia.com &lt;br&gt; twitter.com/jazzblog &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32683;TOOLONG ... preview : St. Lawrence String Quartet promises ' stupendous tour de force of pure fun ' &lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32718;TOOLONG ... preview : Eclectic pianist Stephen Prutsman stages concerts for children on the autism spectrum&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;32753;TOOLONG ... story-teller ' picked to create public art at new central library&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Peter HumFri , 26 Jul 2019 19:22:54 **45;32788;TOOLONG ... The quartet can even bring &amp;ldquo ; a hint of rock &amp;lsquo ; n&amp;rsquo ; roll energy to Haydn and Beethoven , &amp;rdquo ; a Los Angeles Times reviewer wrote several years ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; An ensemble in residence at Stanford University in California since 1998 , the quartet during its three decades has frequently made the trip to Ottawa to perform . It returns this week to star in Chamberfest&amp;rsquo ; s first big concert at Carleton Dominion-Chalmers Centre on Thursday , when works by 18th-century Austrian composer Joseph Haydn , the father of string quartet music , 19th-century composer C&amp;eacute ; sar Franck and contemporary composer Bryce Dessner will be on the program . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Of course , we have to play Haydn because he&amp;rsquo ; s the best , &amp;rdquo ; Nuttall says . &amp;ldquo ; If you&amp;rsquo ; re playing string quartets , Haydn is the man . Opus 75 No. 5 is from the height of his powers . It&amp;rsquo ; s just effortless and inspiring and imaginative and moving and fun . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On Saturday afternoon , the quartet will play another Haydn string quartet at the National Gallery of Canada , but only after discussing the work and giving listeners a peek under the hood regarding what the piece involves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Nuttall says the quartet began combining education with performance to help listeners better connect with the greatness of Haydn . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We play Haydn and we think it&amp;rsquo ; s the greatest thing ever &amp;mdash ; and students would not share our enthusiasm , &amp;rdquo ; Nuttall says . &amp;ldquo ; We figured we were doing something wrong , because it&amp;rsquo ; s not Haydn&amp;rsquo ; s fault . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If people aren&amp;rsquo ; t really excited , the hair&amp;rsquo ; s not standing up on the backs of their necks , they&amp;rsquo ; re not amused and shocked , and it&amp;rsquo ; s just such incredible music &amp;hellip ; we were like , &amp;lsquo ; What&amp;rsquo ; s going on ? &amp;rsquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Haydn suffers more than any composer from lazy listening &amp;mdash ; the **35;33011;TOOLONG syndrome , where you put it on at cocktail parties and everyone feels smarter and calmer , &amp;rdquo ; Nuttall continues . &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s totally not the point . It actually works , but if you don&amp;rsquo ; t actually listen , you miss a lot of the jokes , you miss a lot of the musical connections . You miss a lot of the imaginative twists and turns of motivic development . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Hopefully people ( after the talk ) will listen in a more engaged and active way . Hopefully it opens doors &amp;mdash ; &amp;lsquo ; Hey , I want to hear more Haydn , I want to play more Haydn . ' &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;33048;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;33084;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; After its Thursday night concert , the quartet will play a late-night show that&amp;rsquo ; s typical of Chamberfest&amp;rsquo ; s more eclectic 10 p.m. programming . To me , it&amp;rsquo ; s the same same sort of focus and preparation that goes into a Wigmore Hall show , &amp;rdquo ; says Nuttall , referring to the famed Victorian concert hall in London , England . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; " A concert is a concert basically , whether it 's a talk-and-play for a bunch of kindergarteners or a three-hour marathon of all six Opus 20 quartets for a bunch of hardcore string quartet fans in London . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For that matter , rehearsing is a pleasure and not a chore , he says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s like , wow , we get to spend the time to break this apart and discover new things about it , &amp;rdquo ; Nuttall says . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a joy . ArtsMusicPoor ticket sales forced cancellation of Nordstock , organizer sayshttp : **36;33333;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;33371;TOOLONG ... title= " microphones on stage " alt= " microphones on stage " data-portal-copyright= " Ssorca " **28;33407;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1434791 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ottawa&amp;rsquo ; s Nordstock festival , intended as a celebration of the 50th anniversary of the famed Woodstock festival , has been cancelled , with executive director Timothy Laflamme admitting he was in over his head . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 33-year-old first-time festival organizer said there wasn&amp;rsquo ; t enough money from ticket sales to cover the costs associated with mounting a festival . Nordstock was to be held Aug. 9-11 at Lansdowne Park , featuring a roster of cover bands paying tribute to the artists who played the original Woodstock . Tickets went on sale about eight months ago . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Unfortunately , the ticket sales weren&amp;rsquo ; t there to help balance out all the deposits that were due to the city , and the sound and lighting and stage ( companies ) , &amp;rdquo ; Laflamme said in an interview . &amp;ldquo ; That&amp;rsquo ; s the sad reality of it . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He said it became evident Tuesday that the costs would be impossible to cover . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; When they come calling for hundreds of thousands of dollars , I don&amp;rsquo ; t have that kind of money and sales were not satisfactory . It became too large of a hill to climb . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Announced last fall as Woodstock North , the organizing team initially included Laflamme , Fenton Brothers&amp;rsquo ; guitarist John Fenton , who was booking the bands , and his friend , Larry Johnson , a retired businessman . With a decade or so as a festival volunteer , Laflamme was the only one with hands-on experience . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But the event was soon clouded by bad luck , starting with a cease-and-desist letter from the original Woodstock stakeholders on the use of the Woodstock name . In January , the Ottawa event was renamed Nordstock to avoid legal action . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Then , by spring , Fenton was diagnosed with stage 4 liver cancer and stepped away from the planning , followed by Johnson . Laflamme was determined to continue . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We all had a big dream , &amp;rdquo ; Laflamme said , &amp;ldquo ; but some of us decided to leave because they couldn&amp;rsquo ; t put the energy in it anymore . There&amp;rsquo ; s no hard feelings , but because we had taken people&amp;rsquo ; s money and made commitments , I wanted to persevere . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Laflamme said he put more than $15,000 of his own money into the operation in the last five weeks to cover marketing and staffing costs . &amp;ldquo ; I took the reins and pushed as hard as I could in every facet , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ticket refunds will be available at point of purchase . A market area had also been planned , with vendors paying a $200 registration fee to participate . Laflamme hopes that money can be refunded , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the end , Laflamme called it a huge learning experience . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We had a great vision for what it could be , and we just didn&amp;rsquo ; t have the resources to execute that vision , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; To be honest , I&amp;rsquo ; m extremely disappointed in myself for not being able to complete the project and I feel bad for everybody who made plans to come . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;33437;TOOLONG ... wish I could n't remember ' : Driver recounts fatal collision with 13-year-old cyclist&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;33472;TOOLONG ... story-teller ' picked to create public art at new central library&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;33507;TOOLONG ... residents demand sidewalk be reopened at Magee House&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " **29;33542;TOOLONG " **36;33573;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; Lynn SaxbergThu , 25 Jul 2019 00:35:41 **45;33611;TOOLONG ... to grow a music festival : Kemptville fest thrives on boomershttp : **33;33658;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;33693;TOOLONG ... title= " Kim Mitchell .
