" data-portal-copyright= " " **28;33729;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1429317 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Between shrinking budgets and rising costs , these are challenging times for Ontario music festivals . It 's difficult to start an event , and even more difficult to keep it going year after year . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The Kemptville Live Music Festival is one of the rare success stories among young festivals in the province . The fifth annual edition of the event takes place July 18-21 , and it 's shaping up to be the biggest yet . Tickets are going fast , with attendance expected to hit the 25,000 mark over the weekend . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Certainly the main attraction is the lineup , which in past years has brought major names such as Blue Rodeo , Tom Cochrane , Gordon Lightfoot and the Beach Boys to Kemptville , a small town less than an hour 's drive south of Ottawa . Programming the lineup is the work of artistic director &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Bob Beshara , who founded the festival in 2015. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;He 's done a terrific job this year , too , with a classic rock-heavy assemblage of dad faves anchored by George Thorogood , Steve Earle and the Dukes , April Wine and Kim Mitchell . It 's a make-up date for Mitchell , who was originally scheduled to perform at the festival last year , but had to cancel for medical reasons . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Of course , bands of a certain era appeal to fans of a certain age , and catering to them is a key component of this festival 's popularity . According to executive director Karen Bedard , most people who buy tickets to Kemptville Live are in the 45-65 plus age bracket , with the over-65 demographic growing the fastest . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " It changes a lot of factors , " Bedard said in an interview . " Accessibility is one of the things we 've identified as a priority . There are a lot more accessibility needs in that demographic . We know our people wo n't be standing . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The concert site on the grounds of Kemptville College is designed for accessibility , allowing more room per person than the one-metre square usually allocated for crowd-planning purposes . Boomer-aged festivalgoers need about three times that much space to accommodate lawnchairs , umbrellas and picnic baskets , and possibly also strollers , wheelchairs or other medical devices . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Without public transit in Kemptville , organizers offer plenty of free parking in the surrounding area and provide shuttles to the site . Drop-off zones and complimentary golf-cart shuttles are available , too . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;New this year is a second , on-site bar so patrons do n't have to stand in line as long to buy a beer . There 's also a smoking area where cannabis and vaping will be allowed . The campgrounds have been expanded , too . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Kemptville Live has been lucky with Celebrate Ontario grants , this year receiving about $80,000 from the province , down from last year 's $100,000 . The money is intended to encourage tourism initiatives . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Bedard says the festival draws more people from out of town every year . While most come from other Ontario communities , a growing number come from Canada 's Maritime provinces , the eastern United States and beyond , including a handful from the United Kingdom . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Still , making ends meet is a challenge for the non-profit organization . Inclement weather could sink the budget , and it 's a stretch to ask small , local businesses for more money every year . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " Funding is always a risk , " Bedard said . " We recognize that , and it was part of our first five-year plan . We do have some great local sponsors , but we anticipated that funding would go down over time so we have to make sure we rely on ticket sales . I&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;t would only take one bad weekend to lose a lot of money . We reinvest any earnings we have right back into the organization and sock it away for next year . ArtsMusicBluesfest Review : Snoop Dogg , Wu-Tang Clan weather the stormshttp : **34;34574;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;34610;TOOLONG ... title= " Snoop Dogg played on the City Stage at Bluesfest , Saturday , July 13 , 2019. " alt= " Snoop Dogg played on the City Stage at Bluesfest , Saturday , July 13 , 2019. " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;34646;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1428576 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;34676;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Snoop Dogg / Wu-Tang Clan &lt;br&gt; RBC Ottawa Bluesfest &lt;br&gt; Saturday &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was two of hip-hop&amp;rsquo ; s heaviest hitters from coast-to-coast squaring off on Bluesfest&amp;rsquo ; s main stage Saturday with Staten Island&amp;rsquo ; s legendary Wu-Tang Clan up against Long Beach , California&amp;rsquo ; s top dog , Snoop Dogg. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A wicked thunderstorm blew in halfway through a rousing set by Canadian hip-hop icon K&amp;rsquo ; Naan , washing out the rest of the evening programming and forcing festival organizers to scramble the schedule to ensure both Wu-Tang and Snoop got their share of the spotlight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was just after 9 p.m. &amp;mdash ; about an hour past Wu-Tang&amp;rsquo ; s scheduled start &amp;mdash ; when the show resumed as each of the Clan&amp;rsquo ; s multifaceted MCs took the stage in order . Their leader and visionary RZA called on the crowd repeatedly to show them the &amp;ldquo ; energy&amp;rdquo ; they needed to propel them onstage with all the fanfare you&amp;rsquo ; d expect from the fabled Shaolin-inspired crew . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And the Wu-Tang Clan brought the ruckus from the very first bass drop on Bring Da Ruckus as each of Ghostface Killah , Raekwon and Inspectah Deck stormed on stage in time for each respective verse , and each unleashing rhymes with a fury to match the storm that had just blown through . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Celebrating 25 years since their landmark debut Enter the Wu-Tang ( 36 Chambers ) dropped &amp;mdash ; and making them a perfect pairing with Bluesfest , closing out its own quarter-century celebrations this weekend &amp;mdash ; RZA promised they&amp;rsquo ; d get to play all the songs from that monumental record . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; They did that and more , continuing track-by-track with Shame on a N&amp;mdash ; - , with the late Ol&amp;rsquo ; Dirty Bastard&amp;rsquo ; s portrait on the backdrop in tribute , and his son Young Dirty Bastard now handling his ol&amp;rsquo ; man&amp;rsquo ; s parts with same wild-eyed abandon . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; RZA pumped the crowd up trading rhymes with GZA , and had the crowd raising their hands in the Clan&amp;rsquo ; s trademark &amp;ldquo ; W&amp;rdquo ; formation and chanting &amp;ldquo ; Wu-Tang Forever&amp;rdquo ; across a LeBreton Flats park that quickly filled to brimming once the weather lifted . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As if there weren&amp;rsquo ; t enough voices blasting from the silhouetted stage , they invited Cappadonna , &amp;ldquo ; the tenth member of the Wu-Tang&amp;rdquo ; to trade rhymes before veering back on course with Can It Be All So Simple , Da Mystery of Chessboxin , and C.R.E.A.M. , with each corresponding video flashing across the screen . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; RZA told his faithful to &amp;ldquo ; never forget this one lesson in hip-hop , &amp;rdquo ; and clearly it was lesson learned as the whole crowd chanted along on Wu-Tang Clan Ain&amp;rsquo ; t Nuthin to F&amp;rsquo ; Wit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That sentiment was self-evident by the time they shared the tale of their beginnings to introduce their ( eventual ) breakout hit Protect Ya Neck . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Everything has a beginning , &amp;rdquo ; RZA said , &amp;ldquo ; And for us it was this single that we sold out the back of a truck , that we went from record store to record store to sell . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thankfully that wasn&amp;rsquo ; t the ending as Wu-Tang treated fans to a cover of The Beatles&amp;rsquo ; Come Together , and an unexpectedly faithful take on Nirvana&amp;rsquo ; s Smells Like Teen Spirit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; *** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No stranger to showing up fashionably late , this time it wasn&amp;rsquo ; t by choice as Snoop Dogg hit the stage just after 10:30 p.m. , and stayed on well past the curfew . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; At 15 minutes to midnight , he was still blasting out tunes from House of Pain&amp;rsquo ; s Jump Around to his duet with Wiz Khalifa , Young , Wild and Free , as the refrain that contains the Snoop Dogg credo rang out across the festival grounds to close the night . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So what we get drunk / So what we smoke weed / We&amp;rsquo ; re just having fun / We don&amp;rsquo ; t care who sees . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And just like he did when he rocked Bluesfest&amp;rsquo ; s 2014 edition , Snoop took his fans on a trip through the best of his own catalogue , including his many collaborations , along with a string of handpicked hits from his own favourites . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Tha Shiznit , DJ Khaled&amp;rsquo ; s All I Do Is Win , and 50 Cent&amp;rsquo ; s P.I.M.P. opened the show in short order before he brought out his buddy Warren G. to trade verses on This DJ and Do You See . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He tipped his hat to Dr. Dre on The Next Episode and Nuthin&amp;rsquo ; But a G Thang , and always lived up to the lyric he sang on So Fly : &amp;ldquo ; So fly , Super fly . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Any time you want us to come back , &amp;rdquo ; he promised at the end . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bluesfest&amp;rsquo ; s grand finale comes Sunday with Backstreet Boys closing out the 25 **25;34712;TOOLONG anniversary edition . &lt;/p&gt; Colbie Caillat&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;RBC Ottawa Bluesfest&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; **37;35030;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bluesfest salvaged a soggy night Thursday as fast-rising crossover country star Kane Brown delivered a stirring show that threatened to be washed out earlier by a torrential evening thunderstorm. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The skies cleared in time , though , and the crowd finally turned up to a sopping wet LeBreton Flats as the 25-year-old Brown came out atop the laser-lit stage , dressed in all-black with a black ball cap sporting his own &amp;ldquo ; KB&amp;rdquo ; brand as the strains of the Lil Nas X hit Old Town Road faded from the pre-show loudspeakers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Backed by a crack six-piece band , featuring the traditional country sounds of acoustic guitar , banjo and fiddle , with a jolt of electricity courtesy of some hard-rocking electric guitar , bass and drums , the band cooked behind Brown&amp;rsquo ; s twangy Georgia baritone voice on the opening hit Baby Come Back to Me. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35069;TOOLONG ... title= " Kane Brown . " alt= " Kane Brown . " data-portal-copyright= " HANDOUT " **28;35105;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425793 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The nice acoustic and banjo riff that kicked off What Ifs was soon swallowed up by the booming rock n&amp;rsquo ; roll rhythm section as Brown gave a shout-out to all the &amp;ldquo ; party people&amp;rdquo ; in the crowd . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It took awhile for the party to really get started , though , after a rainstorm and circling lightning washed out Thursday&amp;rsquo ; s evening opening acts and forced the festival to delay its start by an hour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Several acts were cancelled , including Gavin McLeod , Abby Stewart and local gal Brea Lawrenson&amp;rsquo ; s opening set on the City Stage , while DJ Pauly D cancelled his headlining set on the Videotron Stage due to weather-related travel issues . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The weather actually let us play ! &amp;rdquo ; Brown cheered after showing off a video montage during Weekend with him and his pals hanging out at a lakeside barbecue. &amp;ldquo ; I thought I was gon na have to cancel , and I don&amp;rsquo ; t get to come up to Canada all that often . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He showed just how much he appreciated the love the fans gave him as he thanked &amp;ldquo ; everybody who got me on stage today&amp;rdquo ; on Used to Love You Sober , with a hot fiddle solo that gave way to the sing along chorus , as Brown turned the mic over to the crowd to take over the vocals. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The night&amp;rsquo ; s most tender moment came with Brown sharing the story of his tough upbringing in the small town of Fort Oglethorpe , Georgia , with an abusive stepfather and his experiences with racism &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; The type of stuff that&amp;rsquo ; ll put a hole in your soul , &amp;rdquo ; as he sang on Learning , a song that chronicles his early struggles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I don&amp;rsquo ; t know how it is up here but I just think racism should go to hell , &amp;rdquo ; he said to a loud cheer . &amp;ldquo ; For anyone suffering out there , just know you can make it out . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brown dedicated the ballad Homesick to the troops overseas and showed a montage of U.S. soldiers sending well-wishes back home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But he soon traded the serious tone for more lighthearted party fare on Beautiful Girls , and showed he was equally at ease handling hits of any era on a mash-up of Ben E. King&amp;rsquo ; s classic Stand By Me , meandering unexpectedly into Marshmello&amp;rsquo ; s cheesy pop hit Happier . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Gone West feat . Colbie Caillat&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The evening rainfall didn&amp;rsquo ; t deter the few hundred brave , soggy souls who showed up early for Gone West , as the soothing Nashville foursome made sure to show their appreciation for those who stuck it out through the storm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That storm was wild and crazy and we didn&amp;rsquo ; t know if anyone was gon na show up , &amp;rdquo ; said singer Colbie Caillat as she told the modern day Music City love story of how their band came together . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35135;TOOLONG ... title= " Gone West performing on the city stage following a severe thunderstorm that blew through Ottawa on day 7 of RBC Bluesfest. " alt= " Gone West performing on the city stage following a severe thunderstorm that blew through Ottawa on day 7 of RBC Bluesfest. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;35171;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1427533 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As the story goes , Caillat met fellow songwriter Jason Reeves 14 years ago in Nashville and began co-writing her 2007 debut Coco , featuring her breakout hit single Bubbly , which she introduced as a tune written by a bright-eyed 20-year-old pondering &amp;ldquo ; the idea of love and what I hoped it would feel like . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Those hopes came true when she met Hawaiian songwriter Justin Young , and as Reeves explained in the intro to Realize , he may have had something to do with hooking them up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While Caillat and Reeves were co-writing that tune , Reeves &amp;ldquo ; snuck in&amp;rdquo ; a few lyrics about &amp;ldquo ; a friend of mine who had a giant crush on her , and maybe if she listened to the words she&amp;rsquo ; d realize she liked him too . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; And I did , &amp;rdquo ; Caillat chimed in with a wink at Young , her musical and romantic muse of the past 10 years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35201;TOOLONG ... title= " Gone West members ( from left ) Nelly Joy and Colbie Caillat performing on the city stage following a severe thunderstorm that blew through Ottawa on day 7 of RBC Bluesfest. " alt= " Gone West members ( from left ) Nelly Joy and Colbie Caillat performing on the city stage following a severe thunderstorm that blew through Ottawa on day 7 of RBC Bluesfest. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;35237;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1427543 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The same year they met and fell in love , in 2009 , Reeves began co-writing with a Nashville duo called The JaneDear Girls , featuring Nelly Joy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It was love at first write &amp;hellip ; for him , &amp;rdquo ; Joy joked , with a playful nudge to Reeves , now her husband of the past seven years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Fleetwood Mac comparisons are obvious &amp;mdash ; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s fun being two couples in a band , &amp;rdquo ; Caillat said at one point &amp;mdash ; but the similarities were evident on stage even before she explained the romantic intertwinings behind the music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Slow Down , with its cool , breezy chorus , slinky electric guitar hook and gorgeous four-part harmonies wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t have sounded out of place on Rumours . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35267;TOOLONG ... title= " Gone West members ( from left ) Jason Reeves and Nelly Joy performing on the city stage following a severe thunderstorm that blew through Ottawa on day 7 of RBC Bluesfest. " alt= " Gone West members ( from left ) Jason Reeves and Nelly Joy performing on the city stage following a severe thunderstorm that blew through Ottawa on day 7 of RBC Bluesfest. " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;35303;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1427541 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Home is Where the Heartbreak Is , What Could Have Been and Confetti all told the same heartsick tales of love gone wrong , but they kept the tone light , striking up a cover of Simon &amp;amp ; Garfunkel&amp;rsquo ; s Cecilia for the crowd as the wet LeBreton Flats lawn steadily swelled to more respectable numbers in anticipation of fast-rising crossover country star Kane Brown on the main stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;35333;TOOLONG ... title= " Gone West members Colbie Caillat and Justin Young performing on the city stage following a severe thunderstorm that blew through Ottawa on day 7 of RBC Bluesfest. ArtsMusicCatch them while you can : Hollerado set to call it quitshttp : **35;35618;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;35655;TOOLONG ... title= " Ottawa 's Hollerado starts a major cross-Canada tour this week . " alt= " Ottawa 's Hollerado starts a major cross-Canada tour this week . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;35691;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1003305 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; **38;35721;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;em&gt;5:30 p.m . Saturday , HOPE Volleyball Summerfest , Mooney 's Bay Park&lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Also performing : Beaches , 4 p.m. , and Elijah Woods x Jamie Fine , 2:30 p.m. &lt;/em&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;em&gt;Tickets : $20 advance , available at hopehelps.ca , or $27 at the gate . Children nine and under are admitted free . &lt;/em&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After 12 years as a band , Hollerado has decided to call it quits . Formed in Manotick by &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;singer-songwriter ... Menno Versteeg and his neighbourhood pals Jake and Nixon Boyd , with Nepean 's Dean Baxter on bass&lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; , Hollerado is wrapping things up at the end of this year . A final string of tour dates is in the works , likely including Ottawa in the fall , and the fun-loving indie-rockers just released a final album , Retaliation Vacation . In the meantime , they 're playing HOPE Volleyball Summerfest on Saturday . Here 's more on the end of an era from the 39-year-old Versteeg : &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Hollerado is pulling the plug ! What prompted this decision ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Nothing juicy . We&amp;rsquo ; re all still best friends ; it&amp;rsquo ; s not like we hate each other . Exactly the opposite . We&amp;rsquo ; ve had such a great time playing together for 14 years , and we just feel that this project has done what it needs to do . It&amp;rsquo ; s not like the money is good enough to do something you can&amp;rsquo ; t stand behind now , which a lot of bands do . &amp;lsquo ; My kid needs braces so I&amp;rsquo ; m going to keep playing shows . &amp;rsquo ; A lot of these songs we wrote 14 years ago , and we&amp;rsquo ; ve changed a lot in that time . It doesn&amp;rsquo ; t seem right to keep singing them if your heart isn&amp;rsquo ; t entirely behind it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : So your heart is not entirely behind it ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : It&amp;rsquo ; s not that I don&amp;rsquo ; t like the songs . We all like the songs , it&amp;rsquo ; s just ( that ) music is something we&amp;rsquo ; re doing for ourselves as much as the audience . When you&amp;rsquo ; re up there every night singing a song about yourself 15 years ago , it&amp;rsquo ; s hard to move on past that . We want to express the people we are now . We&amp;rsquo ; re all making things or working on music . Everyone is playing music like crazy . It&amp;rsquo ; s not like we&amp;rsquo ; re stopping &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Plus you run a label , Royal Mountain Records , featuring some great young acts like PUP and Dizzy . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Oh yeah , that&amp;rsquo ; s the other thing . A big part of the job taking up a lot of my time , in a good way , is helping other bands get their tour off the ground , which is a really rewarding thing in itself . I enjoy working with developing bands just starting their career , and helping them not make the mistakes I made . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : There 's also a new Hollerado record , and you guys sound invigorated on it . What did you set out to do with this one ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : We **25;35761;TOOLONG invigorated . We had a really great time making it . Just have the most fun , that&amp;rsquo ; s our mission this entire year . Once we decided we&amp;rsquo ; re going to call it , we&amp;rsquo ; re like , &amp;lsquo ; Alright , we&amp;rsquo ; ve been having the best time , let&amp;rsquo ; s do that again for a year , &amp;rsquo ; so that&amp;rsquo ; s totally the mantra of everything we&amp;rsquo ; re doing this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Does it actually feel like the final chapter ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Yeah , totally . We couldn&amp;rsquo ; t be happier . We&amp;rsquo ; re really thankful for everything , all the friends we&amp;rsquo ; ve met is insane . Everyone in our lives is somehow related to this band . So we&amp;rsquo ; re not moving on past that , you can&amp;rsquo ; t . But as far as making music as Hollerado , yeah , that&amp;rsquo ; s run its course . It&amp;rsquo ; s totally fine . No one should freak out about that . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Any regrets ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : We definitely made a lot of mistakes . When you&amp;rsquo ; re supposed to be making your third album &amp;mdash ; after you made a great first album and a second album that does really well , your third album is supposed to take you to the next level and you decide to make 111 songs and you spend two years making it , and they&amp;rsquo ; re songs that cover all styles of music , it&amp;rsquo ; s career suicide . As we learned . But we don&amp;rsquo ; t regret it at all . I would do it again . What an experience , what a way to learn about ourselves . It&amp;rsquo ; s collectively one of the projects that we are most proud of . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Are fans expressing their sadness about the demise of Hollerado ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Oh , of course , big time . ArtsMusicBluesfest preview : Kane Brown on finding success on the charts and at homehttp : **36;36353;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;36391;TOOLONG ... title= " Kane Brown . " alt= " Kane Brown . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;36427;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425793 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;36457;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Kane Brown&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thursday , 930-10:45 p.m. , City Stage &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; RBC Bluesfest , LeBreton Flats Park &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Kane Brown is one of the most anticipated headliners at RBC Bluesfest and an explosive success in country music &amp;mdash ; but the 25-year-old is still getting used to it all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So much has happened . I still feel like I&amp;rsquo ; m new . And when I tell people I still feel new , they&amp;rsquo ; re like , &amp;lsquo ; What do you mean you feel new ? &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; the American Music Award-winning artist said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For someone who considers himself a fresh face , Brown has already seen considerable success . Five years ago , he was a kid from Chattanooga , Tennessee posting country covers to Facebook and picking up followers in droves . Now , in his four years with the recording industry , Brown has two EPs , two albums and a slew of singles under his belt . His latest album , Experiment , debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard charts last fall . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And it&amp;rsquo ; s clear he still has lots of room to make bigger waves . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The recent changes in Brown&amp;rsquo ; s life have been many and frequent &amp;mdash ; both on a personal and a career level . Last month , he featured on a track with the hit-making DJ and producer Marshmello in the song One Thing Right . And last fall , just before Experiment&amp;rsquo ; s release , he married fellow musician Katelyn Jae . The couple announced Jae was pregnant last spring . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Critics have praised Experiment for its robust lineup of strong material , and for blending its country sound with rock , pop and even RnB . Brown spent much of his youth listening to RnB , and only made his commitment to country music later in high school . But for all of his diverse influences , his sound and themes are still decidedly country , which distinguishes him in a genre where new artists are increasingly latching onto other styles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; For me , I want to try and get back to the traditionalist country fans . I get it , my music&amp;rsquo ; s not traditional country &amp;mdash ; whose is , right now ? For me it was like , that was kind of my way , that if they wanted to listen to my music , they get to hear some of the old sounds that they don&amp;rsquo ; t hear much anymore . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brown also keeps tabs on the business side of his music . &amp;nbsp ; He likes to keep track of the stats for individual songs on streaming platforms , and said data can influence how he prepares a concert . &amp;ldquo ; I look at all my numbers , and if it&amp;rsquo ; s not streaming well , I take it out of my set , &amp;rdquo ; he said , naming American Bad Dream , an album track about gun violence in schools ( and the closest he&amp;rsquo ; s gotten to political ) , as one example . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of One Thing Right , he said that &amp;ldquo ; streaming-wise , I think it&amp;rsquo ; s my fastest-streaming song so far . &amp;rdquo ; The collab with Marshmello came together when the DJ reached out to Brown after the AMAs. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I already had this song from my album that didn&amp;rsquo ; t make the cut , but it was one of my favourite songs that I&amp;rsquo ; d written , &amp;rdquo ; he said of One Thing Right . &amp;ldquo ; Just wasn&amp;rsquo ; t right for the album . It was a hard choice , but we had to just leave it off . Honestly , I&amp;rsquo ; m kind of glad I did , I&amp;rsquo ; m glad Marshmello picked it up . I feel like it&amp;rsquo ; s a song a lot of people in the world can relate to , and he&amp;rsquo ; s got a way bigger fanbase than what I&amp;rsquo ; ve got . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brown built his own fanbase through social media , posting simple cellphone videos of himself singing country covers with his friends . But he said his relationship with social media has changed alongside his career . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m bigger than I&amp;rsquo ; ve ever been , which is how career works , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; When it comes to social media , man , you just start seeing a lot more hate . I had to kind of get away from it for a while . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I was so open when I got out there , I feel like that&amp;rsquo ; s what connected me with my fans . But now it&amp;rsquo ; s just , the more open I am with people , the more I feel like I&amp;rsquo ; m judged . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I care less now &amp;mdash ; people can say something about me and I just brush it off my shoulder . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brown said his journey to stardom was not easy , but that he&amp;rsquo ; s now happy where he&amp;rsquo ; s at in life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I got to live the hard life , not really having anything , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I always got picked on growing up , and I got to live through all the hard stuff , so now it&amp;rsquo ; s like I&amp;rsquo ; m living my life &amp;mdash ; a great life &amp;mdash ; got a beautiful wife , a baby on the way ; everything&amp;rsquo ; s going good for me , so why should I have to worry about anything ? &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Brown plays RBC Bluesfest on Thursday , the day before premiering his new single , Like a Rodeo. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;36493;TOOLONG ... preview : Alexisonfire back with first new music in a decade&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " http : **34;36528;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;36716;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1426120 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;36746;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Buddy Guy / Sue **30;36782;TOOLONG &lt;strong&gt;RBC Ottawa **34;36814;TOOLONG **36;36850;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Bluesfest gave its long-serving faithful what they 've been asking for all these years with a double-shot of true blues Tuesday as hometown hero Sue Foley heated up the stage for the long-awaited return of the legend himself , Buddy Guy . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The 82-year-old ( soon to be 83 ) Louisiana-born bluesman wore a wide smile as he strutted out on the Vid ? otron Stage on the festival 's quieter north side -- with an older and much mellower crowd than the one that turned up for KYGO on the main stage -- wearing his trademark black-and-white polka-dot shirt and his well-worn Stratocaster slung over his shoulder . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;He launched straight into Damn Right , I 've Got the Blues , from the 1991 album that cemented Guy 's stature among the best of the legendary electric Chicago bluesmen. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; " Did I play that too loud ? Never content to simply just land on a note , Foley instead digs in , stretches out and milks that note for all it&amp;rsquo ; s worth before moving on to the next flurry . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She promised to play plenty from The Ice Queen , her latest album on the famed Stony Plain label , and a warning for the crowd as she introduced Fool&amp;rsquo ; s Gold . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Don&amp;rsquo ; t believe everything you see or everything you hold &amp;hellip ; It might just be fool&amp;rsquo ; s gold . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;37086;TOOLONG ... title= " Sue Foley on the Videotron Stage as day 5 of the RBC Bluesfest takes place on the grounds of the Canadian War Museum . " data-portal-copyright= " Wayne Cuddington " **28;37122;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1426135 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was pure gold as the slow boogie unfolded with Foley grinding out some stinging lines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The album&amp;rsquo ; s title track was a highlight for the locals &amp;mdash ; Foley mentioned she and her band mates had plenty of friends and family in the crowd &amp;mdash ; though it would have been easy for anyone there to recognize the setting as she sang about hailing from a place &amp;ldquo ; where the ground stays frozen for more than half the year . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But if there were any ice floes still straggling on the Ottawa River , they would have instantly melted from the heat emanating off the evening stage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Ice Queen featured Foley&amp;rsquo ; s first real extended solo , and she made the absolute most of it with her hybrid of thumb-and-fingerpicking &amp;mdash ; instead of using a guitar pick &amp;mdash ; that gives each note an alternating soft , brushing sound or a driving attack . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The odd styling made perfect sense when Foley explained she used to take flamenco guitar lessons in Ottawa , and showed off a bit of what she incorporated into her own blues style on The Dance , followed by the traditional Cannonball Blues , a tribute to Mother Maybelle Carter and all the great blueswomen who continue to inspire her . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She&amp;rsquo ; s the one inspiring others now , though , and she showed why , inviting her pals in the Texas Horns to close things out with a furious double-shot of Texas blues on The Lucky Ones and Gaslight. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS : &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;37152;TOOLONG ... ReviewsMusicBluesfest preview : Alexisonfire back with first new music in a decadehttp : **34;37304;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;37340;TOOLONG ... title= " Alexisonfire. " alt= " Alexisonfire. " data-portal-copyright= " HANDOUT " **28;37376;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425728 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;37406;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; **41;37442;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;9:30-11 p.m . Friday , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;City Stage&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; RBC Ottawa Bluesfest , LeBreton Flats Park &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Alexisonfire is back , and not just as a festival headliner but also as a creative entity . The post-hardcore band from St. Catharines , which broke up in 2011 when guitarist Dallas Green made the decision to focus on his City and Colour side project , has been testing the waters of the music industry again , and finding them rather stimulating , according to lead singer George Pettit. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; New material is bubbling up and two searing new songs , Complicit and Familiar Drugs , have been released so far this year . Although there&amp;rsquo ; s no firm plan for a full album &amp;mdash ; yet &amp;mdash ; Pettit doesn&amp;rsquo ; t rule it out . In this interview ( edited for length and clarity ) , the 36-year-old also talks about his full-time gig as an Oshawa firefighter , how he keeps his pulverizing voice in shape and the curse of pre-show anxiety . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;37485;TOOLONG ... title= " Alexisonfire. " alt= " Alexisonfire. " data-portal-copyright= " HANDOUT " **28;37521;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1425728 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What prompted you guys to get back together and write some new songs ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Well , we 've been playing shows on and off for the last few years , accepting offers to play festivals , and spirits were high in the camp . We are all still pretty close , and so I remember sending out an email , ( saying ) , ' We 've been doing this for a little while , playing shows , and I 'd like to continue , and in order to do that , we got ta probably write some music . ' &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;It 's a tough thing for us to do because aligning all the schedules is very difficult . We all have our own lives outside of the band . But it got easier when Dallas moved back to Toronto from Nashville , and we started going to his place for regular practices and we started writing material . So then we did a quick little session in southern Ontario , just recorded as much as we could in that time . And we 've been trickling it out as the months go on this year . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : So your strategy now is to release them one at a time . Will there be an album ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : I do n't think anybody in this band is that strategic but loosely , I 'd say that is what 's going on . The future is still very much unwritten for Alexis . I would assume at some point there will be more music , but we have n't had that big conversation yet about what it 's going to be or if we 're all going to upset anything in our lives in order to write an album or do anything like that . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;We 're just kind of enjoying the moment and enjoying playing together . And releasing songs : that 's how people consume music now . I 'm a bit of a romantic in that I do like an album , but a lot of people are listening to playlists more than they are to albums. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How does it feel to be back on stage ? Do fans remember Alexisonfire ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Yeah , there 's more fans now than there were back in the heyday of Alexis . We 're playing some of the biggest shows we 've ever played and it 's good . I do n't play enough now where it 's an old-hat type of thing , which is nice . I get nervous , and I get anxiety before the show . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;I 'm a mess ahead of the show because we do n't play all the time anymore . Towards the end of Alexis , I 'd go on stage like I was putting my pants on . No big deal . I get nervous and antsy , but the fear kinda propels you to play better . I find it easier to get to a place of performance when you got a little bit of nerves in your stomach . It 's been really fun but not without a bit of anxiety and a bit of a worry . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : I understand you became a firefighter during the Alexisonfire downtime . Why did you decide to pursue that occupation ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Well , my band broke up and I had to do something . I think I wanted something that was going to get me off the road . The obvious thing to do would have been to get back into the music industry and do something like be a tour manager , but I just thought that fire-fighting would give me some sort of job stability . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;I looked into it and started talking to people I know who had friends who were firefighters . I made myself a fairly lengthy checklist of all the things I needed to do to become a firefighter , and spent three-and-a-half years doing all that stuff , then started applying to departments . It was a long journey but then I got hired in Oshawa and I 've been there ever since . It 's a very rewarding career , and it 's a fairly flexible schedule . It 's nice that I can do both and it 's not an issue at all . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Very cool . Have you been recognized when you 're out on a call ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Maybe twice . I 'm not that recognizable , to tell you the truth , and when I 'm in uniform , people are n't expecting to see me . I 'm not that famous really . I do n't think Alexisonfire is the type of band you look at pictures of very often , and now that MuchMusic is pretty much dead , we do n't really get a lot of screen time . I do appreciate a certain degree of anonymity . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Was it a challenge to get your voice back in shape for performing ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : No , not really . I have n't had an issue with my voice since probably 2003 . I lost my voice once when we were on tour , and I came back , healed up and then we went back on the road , and I never lost it again . I do almost no vocal warmups . I do things I probably should n't do for my voice all the time . And it just keeps doing what it does . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Having said that , I do n't necessarily have to hit fine notes . I 'm just belting it out . My voice is more like a jackhammer than a scalpel . I just never had an issue . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Touring can be a challenge for a band . How is it now for you ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : It 's nice now that my little guy is getting older and he flies really well . And my wife enjoys it . I brought my family to Australia with Alexisonfire , and New York and L.A. so I get to kinda experience touring again through the eyes of a child . When you have traveled as much as Alexisonfire , you can get jaded about the idea of travel so it 's nice having people around who are still bewildered by new places , and excited about them . I really appreciate bringing them on the road with me. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : It must feel like a new chapter for the band . &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;A : Yeah , it 's like the band is starting over , honestly . It 's a whole new experience , which is really cool . We found a way to do it , and try to do it as stress-free as possible so we 're not banging our heads against the pavement anymore . We 're not touring for 10 months out of the year . We 're playing in a band with self-care in mind , and we still very much like to keep grounded in a world outside the music industry as well . I think we 're in a good place . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; lsaxberg@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;ALSO IN THE NEWS&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;a href= " https : **33;37551;TOOLONG ... NewsMusicBluesfest preview Q&amp;amp ; A : Elle King on making music during the toughest time of her lifehttp : **36;38064;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;38102;TOOLONG ... title= " Elle King . " alt= " Elle King . " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38138;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1423460 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;38168;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Elle King has covered a wide musical landscape , and a lot of emotional ground along her rapid rise to fame after breaking out with her 2014 smash hit Ex&amp;rsquo ; s and Oh&amp;rsquo ; s. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; With a guitar-slinging , banjo-toting style that crosses over from rock to country to pop &amp;mdash ; influenced equally by Earl Scruggs and AC/DC &amp;mdash ; King and her band The Brethren are riding high again with 2018&amp;rsquo ; s Shake the Spirit , recorded through a turbulent time following a whirlwind romance , marriage and divorce . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve never set out to make one cohesive record , I&amp;rsquo ; m not that kind of artist , &amp;rdquo ; King said in an interview as her tour rolls into Bluesfest Wednesday . &amp;ldquo ; I sing , like five different genres in 20 minutes . I just have so many different influences and I wake up in a different musical mood every day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s not that I can&amp;rsquo ; t put myself in a box , it&amp;rsquo ; s that nobody&amp;rsquo ; s ever tried . Honestly I&amp;rsquo ; d like to see somebody try . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How did the ups and downs of the last couple of years inform the music , lyrics and emotions of Shake the Spirit ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : I was going through a lot in my personal life , and I didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to make a record . They kinda said , &amp;lsquo ; You have to make a record . &amp;rsquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; And so I just said , &amp;lsquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m gon na do it my way , &amp;rsquo ; because I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t physically or emotionally do it any other way . I tried working with ( other methods ) &amp;mdash ; I went to one songwriting session and the person made me cry because they wouldn&amp;rsquo ; t let me express myself , so I was like , &amp;lsquo ; Alright , f&amp;ndash ; k this . &amp;rsquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t really leave my house so my bandmates would just take turns flying out to California , and all by chance we found a studio in Texas , and it was one of those totally meant-to-be situations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; So we made a record through the toughest time in my life . And I really do feel that because I had this creative outlet during this time , I left all that behind me and I really came out of it a different person . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : There 's a real sense of catharsis , of shedding all this baggage , that goes back to your first hit Ex 's and Oh 's . Is that a challenge to get up in front of strangers and pour your soul out , or is that part of the catharsis ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : Every show is different , some shows I feel more comfortable and more safe than others . Sometimes I&amp;rsquo ; ll turn around and I will cut a song like Man&amp;rsquo ; s Man because that one is just a lot for me to sing . I put them on the record and they tell a story , but I&amp;rsquo ; m a human being and I can get inside my own head . So sometimes I won&amp;rsquo ; t play a certain song , but that&amp;rsquo ; s my right , I think . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But I can distance myself from those songs because when I wrote them and when we recorded them , I really left a lot of emotions there . Most songs I can just enjoy them for what they are , and feel proud that I made something through a lot of pain . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : You 've been very honest with fans through social media , but is that connection double-edged in that fans will expect you to live up to a certain image ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : No , I think expectations actually went down &amp;mdash ; I really had a hard time living up to the Elle that my fans thought was the big partier . That was so much more pressure . And people thought maybe I was a bit more fragile ( during my divorce ) , so a lot of my fans came to support . So I never felt that pressure . I felt a lot of pressure a couple years ago to get f&amp;mdash ; -d up , but I&amp;rsquo ; ve changed a lot and that&amp;rsquo ; s not my No. 1 priority in life . I feel like people respect that . I&amp;rsquo ; ve been very open and honest about where I&amp;rsquo ; m at in my life and my fans appreciate that . Mainly they just want to know that I&amp;rsquo ; m OK . I have very loving fans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : The rock n ' roll lifestyle can take a toll . Is there anything you would go back and tell the Elle of three years ago ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A : The rock n&amp;rsquo ; roll music biz , and doing drugs and partying might be the some of the most fun you could ever f&amp;mdash ; ing have . But it&amp;rsquo ; ll either kill you , or it&amp;rsquo ; ll kill your career real fast . So it all depends on what you want out of your life . I feel very thankful , I wake up in the morning one day and say , &amp;lsquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; m not gon na do that any more , &amp;rsquo ; and I don&amp;rsquo ; t do it any more . Other people struggle . It&amp;rsquo ; s a really dangerous game . Having fun and partying , it&amp;rsquo ; s literally Russian Roulette . So it&amp;rsquo ; s hard for me to give advice , because I never took it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Elle King &lt;br&gt; RBC Ottawa Bluesfest &lt;br&gt; Wed . Bluesfest picks for the first weekend of the festival&lt;/a&gt; &lt;/p&gt; Aedan HelmerFri , 05 Jul 2019 12:26:50 **45;38309;TOOLONG ... guide to Canada Day music on the Hill , including The Strumbellas and morehttp : **36;38356;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;38394;TOOLONG ... title= " The Strumbellas. " alt= " The Strumbellas. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38430;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1418457 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The Strumbellas ' keyboardist , Dave Ritter , remembers watching the Canada Day festivities in Ottawa on television while growing up in Oshawa. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " If you were n't going to be out enjoying the sun , the TV was on and you watched the Parliament Hill performance , " said the 39-year-old musician , recalling Barenaked Ladies ' Canada Day appearance in ' 97 as if it happened yesterday . " It was the thing to do in my house . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Now he and his Strumbellas bandmates are among the artists performing on the Hill as part of this year 's official July 1 celebrations . Free music , performances and family activities also take place at Major 's Hill Park , the Canadian Museum of History and pretty much every other patch of green space in the Ottawa-Gatineau region over the weekend . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Of course , the focus Monday is on the Hill , where an eclectic evening lineup starts at 6:45 p.m. with a DJ set by Polaris-winning artist Kaytranada . The program also features performances by country star Brett Kissel , pop chanteuse C ? ur de Pirate , deep-voiced Indigenous singer-songwriter William Prince , Star Academy finalist Marie-Mai , country maven Crystal Shawanda , Senegalese-Canadian pop artiste Karim Ouellet , and Wavin ' Flag Somali-Canadian K'naan. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;K'naan and Ouellet appear in the daytime show , too , which begins at noon , with the sumptuous backing of the NAC Orchestra performing new arrangements of their songs under the direction of maestro Alexander Shelley . Rounding out the lineup are non-binary singer-songwriter T. Thomason and Mohawk singer Shawnee , plus the Montreal dance company , Les Ballets Jazz de Montreal , with an excerpt of their Leonard Cohen homage , Dance Me. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;For The Strumbellas , the high-profile gig is a triumphant occasion , not only a long-awaited return to the nation 's capital ( where Ritter studied English literature at Carleton University ) , but also a chance for Canadian fans to welcome them back and toast their recent international success . Although there 's only time for a few songs , they 'll be back to play a full set at CityFolk in September . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The decade-old band struck gold in 2016 with their summer hit , Spirits , an infectious anthem brimming with handclaps and a big chorus , making it a perfect crowd singalong tune . The song was a breakthrough that sent them touring around the world , earned them spots at major festivals and TV talk shows , and won the 2017 Juno for single of the year . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;After picking up that award at Canadian Tire Centre ( the Junos were in Ottawa that year ) , they turned their attention to making a follow-up album , their fourth . Rattlesnake came out this spring , and it 's decidedly more pop than folk , as Ritter noted . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " We 're always trying to find the sound that 's bigger , better , more anthemic , and this is a continuation of that , " he said . " If you plot a trajectory from our first album , it was pretty folky and has more country elements , but as the albums progress , they get poppier , with more synthesizers and big strings and things like that . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " I do n't know what happened to us , " he added . " We were fans of alt-country but we all fell in love with pop music . I think we sort of keep trying to write Taylor Swift songs on some level . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Or maybe they 're evolving -- along with the rest of the country . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Between the Toronto Raptors ' success and the legalization of cannabis , Canada is outgrowing its image as a backwoods outpost . The nation is looking hipper every day . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;On their recent travels through the United States and Europe this year , Ritter and his compadres ( singer-songwriter- guitarist &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Simon Ward , lead guitarist Jon Hembrey , violinist Isabel Ritchie , bassist Darryl James and drummer Jeremy Drury ) &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;noticed a shift in the perception of Canadians . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " Especially with Drake and Bieber , Canadian music is not a novelty anymore , " Ritter said . " It does n't feel like we 're a fish out of water . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Drake , in particular , is putting Canada on the international map . Ritter is a big hip-hop aficionado who likes to remix music , create playlists for parties and believes Drizzy should be appreciated as a cultural ambassador and game-changer. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " Anyone who 's been that consistent for that long , who 's shifted genres , personas , and modes of working but still has everything clicking all the time is just a master , " he said . " Consistency is very difficult to have as a musician , and the people who are achieving that are at the top of the game . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Still , when it comes to being Canadian , there are some stereotypes that persist . " It 's true that we 're polite and kind people , " Ritter observed . " We may joke about saying sorry when you bump into someone , but it 's a nice thing to be known around the world as a kind and generous and reasonable people . July 1&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Elberlyn&lt;/span ... &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;River Doucette&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Silla and Rise&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Ben Caplan&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Bleu Jeans Bleu&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;DJ Shub&lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For more information , go to &lt;a href= " http : **34;38657;TOOLONG ... . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;LISTEN TO THE 10/3 PODCAST&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " **40;38693;TOOLONG ... Lynn SaxbergWed , 26 Jun 2019 11:44:25 **45;38735;TOOLONG ... ArtsLocal NewsMusicThe Citizen 's music writers share their 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival pickshttp : **35;38782;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;38819;TOOLONG ... title= " Saxophonist Melissa Aldana , who plays the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival on Wednesday , June 26. " alt= " Saxophonist Melissa Aldana , who plays the 2019 TD Ottawa Jazz Festival on Wednesday , June 26. " data-portal-copyright= " " **28;38855;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1414820 " /&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;38885;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the last few years , in step with the backlash against a p&amp;mdash ; &amp;ndash ; grabbing U.S. president and the rise of the MeToo Movement , it became more apparent than ever that jazz had problems with patriarchy and sexism. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Big-name jazz professors left their jobs after allegations of sexual misconduct surfaced . Prominent jazz pianists Robert Glasper and Ethan Iverson were vilified after their conversation , printed in March 2017 on Iverson&amp;rsquo ; s well-read blog , delved into a discussion of why women listeners prefer grooves over complex improvised melodies. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Women &amp;ldquo ; don&amp;rsquo ; t love a whole lot of soloing . When you hit that one groove and stay there , it&amp;rsquo ; s like a musical clitoris , &amp;rdquo ; Glasper notoriously said . &amp;ldquo ; You&amp;rsquo ; re there , you stay on that groove , and the women&amp;rsquo ; s eyes close and they start to sway , going into a trance . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Glasper&amp;rsquo ; s comments came as a shock to exactly zero people who&amp;rsquo ; ve spent any time in the jazz world , &amp;rdquo ; responded U.S. author and jazz journalist Michelle Mercer in a column that she wrote for NPR. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This scandal reveals that the issue of women in jazz goes deeper , into a gendered construction of the music itself , &amp;rdquo ; Mercer continued . &amp;ldquo ; We need an intelligent public discussion about gendered notions of jazz , and this hot mess might as well be the impetus for that discussion . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Since then , the jazz world has seen more music made with a feminist slant , more all-female bands , and even the recent creation of an Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice at Boston&amp;rsquo ; s Berklee College of Music &amp;mdash ; a respected institution that had been plagued by &amp;ldquo ; a culture of blatant sexual harassment , &amp;rdquo ; according to a November 2017 Boston Globe investigation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It may well be that this year&amp;rsquo ; s TD Ottawa Jazz Festival , which starts Friday and runs until Canada Day , advances the cause of women in jazz more boldly than any of its Canadian and U.S. counterparts , thanks to its new commitment to strive for gender parity in its bookings . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As usual , the festival continues to be basically two events in one &amp;mdash ; an outdoor festival based in Marion Dewar Plaza with much mass-appeal , cross-over music in the mix , plus an indoor festival based in the National Arts Centre presenting more uncompromisingly jazz-based music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But this year , the bookings prominently featuring women &amp;mdash ; vocalists and instrumentalists alike &amp;mdash ; make up roughly half of the festival&amp;rsquo ; s bookings , from Norah Jones , Jane Siberry , Judith Hill , Cuban vocalist Omara Portuondo and former Prince guitarist Donna Grantis in the first category to the bonafide jazz stars Patricia Barber , Cyrille Aim&amp;eacute ; e , Kris Davis , Mary Halvorson , Melissa Aldana , Anna Webber and Terri Lyne Carrington , plus rising stars Nubya Garcia and Sasha Berliner . Montreal-based saxophonist and composer Christine Jensen , a two-time Juno Award winner , will lead the festival&amp;rsquo ; s first gender-balanced big band that will include Canadian jazz stars Marianne Trudel , Allison Au , Tara Davidson and Rebecca Hennessy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Ottawa may involve the best assemblage of women jazz musicians ever ! &amp;rdquo ; Mercer commented when pointed to the lineup . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other commenters lauded the festival not only for trying to equalize the presence of men and women on its stages , but simply for the excellence of the musicians , gender aside , and the lineup&amp;rsquo ; s generational shift . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; While past jazz festivals in Ottawa and elsewhere could get caught up in nostalgically booking older musicians ( and attracting grey-haired listeners ) , this year&amp;rsquo ; s Ottawa festival also showcases more jazz musicians in their 30s , 40s and early 50s , including many of the women named above and also piano star Brad Mehldau , saxophonist Donny McCaslin and guitarist Gilad Hekselman. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The crush of talent seems all the more obvious given that this year&amp;rsquo ; s festival is shorter than usual , starting on a Friday rather than a Thursday and with its Monday without performances for the first time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Below , music writers Peter Hum and Lynn Saxberg zero in on the concerts they&amp;rsquo ; re most excited about . Coincidentally , women figure as much as men in their picks . &lt;/p&gt; **29;38921;TOOLONG Hum 's **31;38952;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Anna Webber 's Simple Trio&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Friday , June 21 , 6 p.m. , NAC Fourth Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The B.C.-born , New York-based saxophonist , flutist and composer has grown to become one of the most invigorating musicians on jazz&amp;rsquo ; s cutting edge . Be warned that Webber&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; Simple Trio&amp;rdquo ; is named archly , as her compositions are fiendishly tricky and innovative . It&amp;rsquo ; s a good thing pianist Matt Mitchell and drummer John Hollenbeck ( an American who&amp;rsquo ; s the current chair of McGill University&amp;rsquo ; s jazz department ) are world-class avant-gardists who revel in interpreting Webber&amp;rsquo ; s intriguing , challenging material . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;38985;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39021;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Gilad Hekselman Trio&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Friday , June 21 , 8 p.m. , NAC Fourth Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No less than jazz guitar hero Pat Metheny has singled out New York City-based guitarist Hekselman as a rising star . One listen to the 36-year-old native of Israel helps to explain why . Hekselman is a lucid , lyrical player at the fore of jazz&amp;rsquo ; s modern mainstream , blessed with a mastery of tone and a knack for making fresh , personal music feel accessible and even ineffably right . At the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s Fourth Stage , Hekselman will perform with Montreal-raised bassist Rick Rosato and drummer Jonathan Pinson , a supportive pair that accompanied the guitarist earlier this month in China and Japan . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;39057;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39092;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Kris Davis &amp; Ingrid Laubrock&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Sunday , June 23 , 6 p.m. , NAC Fourth Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In 2010 , Ben Ratliff , then the jazz critic for the New York Times , wrote : &amp;ldquo ; Over the last couple of years in New York , one method for deciding where to hear jazz on a given night has been to track down the pianist Kris Davis . &amp;rdquo ; In the decade since , the Calgary-raised musician has demonstrated astonishing breadth and imagination as a vital figure on jazz and creative music&amp;rsquo ; s leftmost flank . She and German saxophonist Laubrock are long-time , perfectly paired collaborators who explore bracing music that intertwines knotty compositions and unfettered improvising . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Jakob Bro / Thomas Morgan / Joey Baron&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tuesday , June 25 , 6 p.m. , NAC Fourth Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For the last decade , the award-winning Danish guitarist Bro , 41 , has been collaborating with the cream of the American jazz crop to make thoughtful and even dreamy music in line with ECM Records&amp;rsquo ; s evocative aesthetic . At the NAC Fourth Stage , Bro will lead a trio that includes bassist Thomas Morgan and drummer Joey Baron , two U.S. musicians with whom he has released two records on ECM in recent years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;39128;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39163;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;= Jazz Orchestra &amp; Christine Jensen&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tuesday , June 25 , 8 p.m. , NAC Studio&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A large ensemble formed to wave the flag for gender parity at this year&amp;rsquo ; s festival , this group also pulls together some of the best jazz musicians of their generation in Montreal , Toronto and Ottawa . Saxophonist Christine Jensen , the two-time Juno Award winner from Montreal , Toronto-based horn players , Rebecca Hennessy , Tara Davidson and Allison Au , plus pianist Marianne Trudel will shine most brightly as this command performance will feature their compositions as well as their playing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Melissa Aldana Quartet&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Wednesday , June 26 , 6 p.m. , NAC Fourth Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After winning the 2013 Thelonious Monk International Jazz Saxophone Competition at the age of 24 , the Chilean-born musician with a thrilling , virtuosic modern style saw her star rise dramatically . In Ottawa next Wednesday , Aldana kicks off a slate of especially promising concerts . Leading a quartet that includes the equally young and compelling pianist Sam Harris , Aldana will likely showcase some of the surging , heady music from her new album , Visions , whose compositions were inspired by the life and works of the late Mexican artist Frida Kahlo . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;39199;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39235;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Illegal Crowns&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Wednesday , June 26 , 8 p.m. , NAC Fourth Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The collective quartet called Illegal Crowns consists of four highly regarded and bristling improvisors : drummer Tomas Fujiwara , guitarist Mary Halvorson , cornet player Taylor Ho Bynum and pianist Benoit Delbecq . While the first three musicians , who are all New York City-based , are able to play together regularly , the quartet with French pianist Delbecq is a more sporadic project . Expect creative sparks to fly when the four strong and outward-bound personalities are reunited . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Brad Mehldau Quintet&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Wednesday , June 26 , 8:30 p.m. , TD main stage , Marion Dewar Plaza&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; There&amp;rsquo ; s seemingly little that Mehldau , the most influential pianist in jazz over the last two decades hasn&amp;rsquo ; t tried . He&amp;rsquo ; s led a breathtaking trio since the mid-1990s , dazzled as a virtuosic soloist who can delve into Bach one day and Radiohead the next , and played equally moving duets with classic soprano Renee Fleming and mandolinist Chris Thile . The 48-year-old will bring a new all-star quintet to Ottawa for what should be the most jazz-rich of the festival&amp;rsquo ; s main-stage concerts . Expect horn players Ambrose Akinmusire ( trumpet ) and Joel Frahm ( tenor saxophone ) to thrill , while drummer Leon Parker is renowned for his uniquely buoyant , minimalist swinging . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Hayden Chisholm Trio&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Wednesday , June 26 , 7 p.m. , NAC Studio&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Thursday , June 27 , 6 p.m. , NAC Fourth Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Raised in New Zealand and based in Serbia , alto saxophonist Chisholm is an infrequent visitor to North America . That&amp;rsquo ; s a shame , because the 44-year-old is an engaging musician with a softened , appealing tone , great melodic agility and a quirky penchants for microtones and the Indian drone-producing shruti box . He will perform twice at the festival , on Wednesday with a larger ensemble that will include Ottawa-area string players , and then on Thursday with his long-time collaborators Matt Penman on bass and Jochen Rueckert on drums . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;39271;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39307;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Terri Lyne Carrington and Social Science&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Thursday , June 27 , 8:30 p.m. , TD main stage , Marion Dewar Plaza&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A prodigious talent who received a full scholarship to Berklee College of Music when she was 11 , drummer Carrington has blossomed into not just a leader of formidable ensembles but also a champion of gender issues , having recently created an Institute for Gender Justice at her alma mater . In Ottawa , the 53-year-old will present her forward-thinking and politically progressive project Social Science , which includes the incandescent thirty-something musicians Aaron Parks ( keyboards ) and Matthew Stevens ( guitar ) and Kassa Overall ( DJ ) along with vocalist Debo Ray and multi-instrumentalist Morgan Guerin. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;39343;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39379;TOOLONG **28;39415;TOOLONG Saxberg 's **31;39445;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Judith Hill&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Friday , June 21 , 8:30 p.m. , TD Main Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The powerhouse singer was one of the backup vocalists profiled in the documentary 20 Feet From Stardom , recognizing her work with the likes of Prince , Stevie Wonder , Elton John , Michael Jackson and more . She stepped into the spotlight with her Prince-produced 2015 debut album , which demonstrated her skill as a songwriter , too . Last year&amp;rsquo ; s follow-up , Golden Child , is another showcase of her ability to weave synth pop , gospel , rock and soul into one funky brew . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : Her dad is pioneering funk bassist Robert Lee Hill ( and is in her band ) , while her mom , Michiko Hill , is an accomplished keyboardist . The couple also run a studio in L.A. Growing up , Judith always had singers in her room because her bedroom was the vocal booth . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Galactic featuring Erica Falls&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Saturday , June 22 , 8:30 p.m. , TD Main Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; New Orleans funk-and-jazz jam band Galactic blast off in a new direction with their 10th and latest album , Already Ready Already . Produced by band members Robert Mercurio and Ben Ellman , the record finds them joining forces with an array of emerging singers , including vocalist Erica Falls , who&amp;rsquo ; s heralded as the queen of New Orleans neo-soul . She&amp;rsquo ; s also touring with the band , providing a refreshing change from the band&amp;rsquo ; s usual male-dominated groove-making. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;39478;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39514;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : Galactic recently purchased Tipitina&amp;rsquo ; s , the legendary New Orleans nightclub where they&amp;rsquo ; ve been playing regular gigs for 25 years , including an annual all-nighter on the eve of Mardi Gras. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Jane Siberry&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Saturday , June 22 , 10:30 p.m. , OLG Stage , Confederation Park&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Canada&amp;rsquo ; s free-ranging songbird returns to one of her favourite nests , Ottawa , a city where she has found inspiration and plenty of support from the folk-music community over the years . She&amp;rsquo ; ll be accompanied by a small but mighty ensemble consisting of Ottawa-born , New York-based music director Peter Kiesewalter on piano , Julian Armour on bass and Whitney LaGrange on violin . It&amp;rsquo ; s hard to predict what she&amp;rsquo ; ll play but we know that Siberry&amp;rsquo ; s arty mid-&amp;rsquo ; 80s hit , Mimi On The Beach , has been resurfacing in recent concerts , and we hear there are new tunes to unveil , too . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : Siberry once revealed that she enjoys a simple baked potato before performing , and won&amp;rsquo ; t go on stage without lipstick and her hair done up . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **36;39550;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Sunday , June 23 , 8:30 p.m. , TD Main Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Chicago has been going strong for half a century , proud of the fact that they&amp;rsquo ; ve never missed a show in 52 years . They formed in Chicago , of course , in 1967 as the Chicago Transit Authority , with the intention of writing politically charged rock &amp;lsquo ; n&amp;rsquo ; roll songs powered by a horn section . Instead they shortened the name and hit the charts with songs like If You Leave Me Now , Saturday in the Park , Hard to Say I&amp;rsquo ; m Sorry and 25 or 6 to 4 , becoming staples of the &amp;rsquo ; 70s&amp;rsquo ; wave of soft rock . Three original members are still in the band , and they still tour with several truckloads of gear , making it the biggest production of the jazz festival&amp;rsquo ; s main stage this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : In the early years of touring , the budget only allowed for two hotel rooms , one for sleeping and one for partying . Which was fine because &amp;ldquo ; we didn&amp;rsquo ; t need much sleep back in those days , &amp;rdquo ; recalls trumpeter Lee Loughnane. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; **40;39588;TOOLONG &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Thursday , June 27 , 10:30 p.m. , OLG Stage , Confederation Park&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; DakhaBrakha was created 15 years ago by an avant-garde theatre director in Kyiv to liven up his shows , but probably not to dominate them , which is what happens whenever they play . With a name that means give/take in old Ukrainian , the quartet specializes in the folk music of their homeland , reinventing it for a modern age with an unapologetic feminist message . In traditionally-inspired costumes , Marko Halanevych , Olena Tsybulska , Nina Garenetska and Iryna Kovalenko rev up the rhythms with instruments from around the world , including tabla , djembe , accordion , bass , cello , didgeridoo and more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;39630;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39665;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : DakhaBrakha&amp;rsquo ; s first show at Bonnaroo in 2014 was such a hit that Rolling Stone declared them the breakout act of the festival , coining the new musical subgenre : &amp;ldquo ; Ukrainian folkdrone Bjorkpunk. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Omara Portuondo with NAC Orchestra&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Friday , June 28 , 8:30 p.m. , TD Main Stage&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The legendary Cuban singer , who&amp;rsquo ; s well into her 80s , is renowned as the diva ( and the only female voice ) of the Buena Vista Social Club . International fame came with the &amp;nbsp ; Grammy-winning Buena Vista album and an Oscar-nominated documentary , but she had been a superstar at home for decades , equally comfortable with all the Afro-Cuban styles , from boleros to rumba . On this tour , a final , worldwide journey she calls her Last Kiss tour , she&amp;rsquo ; ll be performing songs from Cuba&amp;rsquo ; s golden era with the lush and expert backing of the NAC Orchestra . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **34;39701;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **34;39737;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : Portuondo plays the good witch who lives in the Louisiana swamps in the Spanish version of Disney&amp;rsquo ; s animated The Princess and the Frog . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Cha Wa&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;br&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Friday , June 28 , 10:30 p.m. , OLG Stage , Confederation Park&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Two of the musical traditions that make New Orleans&amp;rsquo ; street culture so rich find a common groove in Cha Wa . The New Orleans band combines the big , brassy marching band sound with Mardi Gras Indian culture to come up with a funk-laced , sousaphone-soaked twist on the party music of the Big Easy . While some of the songs have a social-justice message , you can dance to any of them . Their latest album , Spyboy , is produced by fellow jazzfest player , Ben Ellman of the band Galactic. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Fun fact : Singer J&amp;rsquo ; Wan Boudreaux is the grandson of Big Chief Monk Boudreaux of the Golden Eagles Mardi Gras Indian tribe .
