ArtsMusicOn secret shows , a new record and overcoming negativity : An interview with Half Moon Runhttp : **37;39967;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;40006;TOOLONG ... title= " Supplied photo of Half Moon Run . " alt= " Supplied photo of Half Moon Run . " data-portal-copyright= " Jennifer McCord " **28;40042;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1412363 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Half Moon Run spent the first five years of their career touring the world , winning over huge crowds at festivals and stadium shows with their harmony-laden , electronic-infused folk rock . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; It was a thrill , but they also learned to value the small shows , where there&amp;rsquo ; s a more intimate connection with fans and they feel comfortable trying out new songs . In this edited interview , Devon Portielje , the Ottawa-born singer of the Montreal-based band , talks about the appeal of secret shows , what to expect on the upcoming album , due for release this fall , and how he learned to get out of a negative mindset . The band returns to Ottawa on Thursday to headline the first night of the Tim Hortons Dragon Boat Festival&amp;rsquo ; s free concert series . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : The last time I saw you guys was a secret show at a pub in Wakefield . What 's the appeal of these surprise gigs ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... Well , we usually announce them on our mailing list , and the attraction is that it 's a great show , from our perspective , but also for our fans . It 's a nice , tight , small venue . We bring in all our production , which is quite an affair now , and it 's a great place to try out new material in a safe environment . You go to a big festival and try out new material , sometimes you get a bit of a hostile audience . It 's nice to try something , and make it feel special and exclusive , perhaps . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Speaking of new material , how 's the new record coming along ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... It 's coming along great . We 're in the mixing process of it now , so it 's almost wrapped up , almost finalized . We brought up a producer , Joe Chiccarelli , who has a massive catalogue , tons of experience , tons of skills . We did about five weeks in Montreal at the studio . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;Q : &; ... &lt;strong&gt;Why did you pick Joe to produce ? **28;40072;TOOLONG &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... His massive catalogue was definitely important , but he seemed to be able to bring music forward . I do n't know how to describe it . A little bit brighter . We wanted to kind of come forward in the speakers a little bit to be more present , shall we say . So we wanted someone who 's performance oriented , to get a good performance on tape , and bring it forward to be more present . I know he 's done artists like Elton John and Frank Zappa but you 're not so much looking at the style or the taste , I was looking for the way the audio sounds . Does it sit back in the speakers ? Is it muffled or is it present and clear ? That 's really a fine art . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Did you have the songs ready before going into the studio ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... Yes . It is somewhat of a myth to be able to walk into a studio without your songs prepared . Your producer is going to hang his head . I know Fleetwood Mac spent six weeks working on drum tones in the studio but they put a million dollars into studio rental fees . It seems to be impractical for us . A lot of the music was captured in five or six takes , and we 're all playing mostly live together so it was really quite fast , us being so rehearsed before we go into the studio . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : What 's inspiring the songwriting on this record ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... Well , I 've had kind of a negative outlook on the world for a long time , and that kind of filters into the music a little bit , but I 've been reading evolutionary psychology books , and other non-fiction stuff , and they 've changed my whole outlook . Normally I would take inspiration from pain or challenge or misery or something , but now it 's like I have maybe more of a poetic way of looking at the world . The inspiration comes from peacefulness or an observation about somebody or something different rather than the more negative thing . And also love . I met my girlfriend during the writing period . That 's an interesting process , that kind of burgeoning relationship . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;Q : Half Moon Run has had a lot of luck since the beginning . What fuelled your negative outlook on life ? &lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... I guess it 's just the media representation of facts to make it seem like there 's more crime , or more pollution , or more this than that . Humans are more geared to remember and pay attention to negative input than positive because it 's related to survival . I 'm deeply in that trap . But you know , I do n't want to get too statistical , but I guess the way it seemed before , between pollution and climate change and wealth inequality and those kinds of things , it felt like we were entering a dark phase , but I think that 's probably been a feeling of humanity since the dawn of time . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : How did you change that outlook ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... Cognitive behavioural therapy , I 've been doing that . And meditating. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;I started the new year meditating every day , 10 minutes . I did about 80 days and then fell off a little bit . But that 's intense , controlling the mind . I guess it 's kind of biohacking . You can control your mental response to certain stimuli . It 's like I 'm using meditation as a tool . That ancient wisdom is coming back in a way that I did n't predict . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Q : Ultimately , what keeps it fun for you ? &lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;&lt;strong&gt;A : &; ... Mindfulness in the wonderful moments . I got really used to being on the road and playing in front of 5,000 people or something during festival runs , and you just get used to those massive highs . So now , it 's like i just want to be more present . Now I enjoy the writing process so much , that moment when you 're starting a song . There are no limits , and that 's a deep challenge . A lot of artists struggle with that . When do you stop writing ? But right at that inception , that moment when there 's no limits and you can go in any direction with the song , it 's a sacred feeling . Every song we 've ever written for us has been the best song we 've ever written in our lives for a very short period of time . You have to believe in that and catch that wave to continue the spark of writing . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; lsaxberg@postmedia.com &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Tim Horton 's Dragon Boat Festival&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;When &amp; where : &lt;/strong&gt; June 20-23 , Mooney&amp;rsquo ; s Bay Park , free admission &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;June 20&lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Half Moon Run , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Jacquie Neville , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Vile Bodies &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;June 21 &lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Alan Doyle , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Jane 's Party , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Basic White &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;June 22 &lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Jess Moskaluke , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Sacha , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The Dill &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;b&gt;June 23 &lt;/b&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;USS , &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Dub ? , Trails &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;LISTEN TO THE DOWN TO BUSINESS PODCAST&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " **40;40102;TOOLONG ... He was intent , totally focused on the music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; From my vantage point a few feet away in a front-row pew , I realized I was holding my breath as the musical suspense built . When he finished , there was an overwhelming sense of release . Was I going to cry ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I managed to hold it in . Instead , I recalled the words of one of my new orchestra friends at a bar in Paris a few days earlier . &amp;ldquo ; When you hear James play , you&amp;rsquo ; re going to want to throw your bra at him , &amp;rdquo ; she declared . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the moment of revelry , everyone laughed , but now I understood . The man is a musical genius , a rare talent whose playing connects with the deepest corners of one&amp;rsquo ; s soul . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;40329;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;40371;TOOLONG ... soloist : Fighting challenge after challenge , soprano Erin Wall rises to the **27;40406;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;40435;TOOLONG ... David DQ Lee wows the crowd in London with incredible , multi-octave **26;40470;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; I was not the only person to come to this conclusion during the National Arts Centre Orchestra&amp;rsquo ; s recent tour of Europe . Although Ehnes records and tours extensively and has won two Grammys , including this year&amp;rsquo ; s honour for the best classical instrumental solo , it seems many people in Europe had never heard of him , judging by the awestruck reaction of audiences after hearing him perform Mendelssohn&amp;rsquo ; s Violin Concerto with the orchestra . Whenever he played , jaws dropped and people rose to their feet shouting , &amp;ldquo ; Bravo . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; " We were very amazed , " said one Danish concertgoer , 28-year-old &lt;/span&gt; Mika Dahl , &amp;nbsp ; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;during the intermission in Copenhagen 's Danish Radio Konserthuset . " He put all of it in his head so he could just play ? That 's crazy . It was marvellous . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40498;TOOLONG ... title= " James Ehnes performing at Stockholm 's Royal Chapel . " alt= " James Ehnes performing at Stockholm 's Royal Chapel . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;40534;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403128 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Ehnes was one of several featured soloists during the orchestra&amp;rsquo ; s two-week journey , their guest appearances divided over seven concerts in five countries . It was the most ambitious tour of Alexander Shelley&amp;rsquo ; s four-year tenure as maestro of the Ottawa-based orchestra , and not something to be taken lightly . An orchestra has to be good to hold its own in the birthplace of classical music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After leading NACO to every region in Canada during the 2017 sesquicentennial celebrations , the idea of showing the musicians off in Europe for the NAC&amp;rsquo ; s 50th anniversary became a personal goal for Shelley , a 39-year-old Englishman who has conducted orchestras on five continents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The interesting part of the title &amp;lsquo ; national&amp;rsquo ; for any institution is that on the one hand , it implies the local responsibility , the responsibility to the country , &amp;rdquo ; he said between forkfuls of salad and sips of coffee during a pre-concert interview in his dressing room in Utrecht&amp;rsquo ; s TivoliVredenburg concert hall . &amp;ldquo ; But interestingly , it immediately also implies the representative , ambassadorial role of representing the country out in the world . We also take that role very seriously . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; *** &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Manitoba-born Ehnes was the crowd favourite on a tour expertly programmed to highlight world-class Canadian talent in performance and composition . For Ehnes , the experience never gets old . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; You always hope to cultivate new audiences , &amp;rdquo ; he said in an interview in the Royal Chapel . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve played in all these places but every concert is an opportunity . One of the great joys of doing what we do is there&amp;rsquo ; s always somebody there who&amp;rsquo ; s there for the first time , or somebody who will be left thinking about the music in a new way . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Other musicians joke that &amp;ldquo ; Jimmy&amp;rdquo ; must have sold his soul or been implanted with some sort of computer chip to be able to play so fluidly , without breaking a sweat or cracking a smile . But no : it takes discipline and hard work to make it look so easy . He said his primary goal is to get out of the way of the music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; In the rock world , there are people who perform in different ways to draw attention to different aspects of what they do , &amp;rdquo ; Ehnes said . &amp;ldquo ; But I think what we do with our music is to try to draw attention away from ourselves and draw more attention to the music being played . The performer plays a role of conduit more than a role of star . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; No matter what he says , Ehnes is undoubtedly a star , considered by many to be among the best violinists in the world , perhaps even a rival to the great Pinchas Zukerman , NACO&amp;rsquo ; s previous music director and a superstar in the classical world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; I&amp;rsquo ; m happy to report Ehnes is also a humble , down-to-earth fellow &amp;mdash ; a husband and father of two young children &amp;mdash ; with a surprising penchant for roller coasters , of all things . On his downtime in Copenhagen , he headed straight to Tivoli Gardens . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s the most wonderful place , &amp;rdquo ; he said of the amusement park . &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve played in Copenhagen a bunch over the years , and whenever possible , I try to amuse myself there . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40564;TOOLONG ... title= " Alexander Shelley ( R ) and Canadian violinist James Ehnes . The NAC orchestra on tour in Europe . " alt= " Alexander Shelley ( R ) and Canadian violinist James Ehnes . The NAC orchestra on tour in Europe . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;40600;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403119 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; An international orchestra tour does not come together overnight . In addition to the logistics of booking concerts and making travel arrangements , it&amp;rsquo ; s important to present a well-balanced evening . Shelley assembled five different programs , selecting both contemporary and classic material , and highlighting Canadian content . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; To anchor the traditional end , there were two crowd-pleasers , Brahms Symphony No. 2 and Dvorak&amp;rsquo ; s Symphony No. 9 in E minor , Op. 95 , a.k.a . From The New World , both of which sound glorious in NACO&amp;rsquo ; s hands ( and which Shelley conducts without a score ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As for the guest soloists , another budding superstar , the dazzling Calgary-born pianist Jan Lisiecki , was featured in the two United Kingdom concerts in London and Saffron Walden . Like Ehnes , he&amp;rsquo ; s a stupendously talented regular on the international circuit . Lesser known are the Korean-Canadian countertenor David D.Q. Lee and soprano Erin Wall , who both gained valuable exposure on the journey . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of particular significance was the inclusion of contemporary music by homegrown composers , a bold move for any ensemble , but one Shelley also considers a vital part of a national orchestra&amp;rsquo ; s role . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The amount of new music we&amp;rsquo ; re travelling with is unprecedented , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I can think of very few orchestras in the world that would do that . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A glowing review of the Cadogan Hall concert in Chelsea called it &amp;ldquo ; one of the major highlights of the current London orchestral season , &amp;rdquo ; with special praise for the piece &amp;ldquo ; Golden slumbers kiss your eyes&amp;hellip ; &amp;rdquo ; by Serbian-Canadian composer Ana Sokolovic , in which Lee is the featured soloist . A classicalsource.com reviewer described her as a &amp;ldquo ; completely assured composer &amp;hellip ; never losing sight of what this compelling work is intended to convey to its listeners . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In all , works by six Canadian composers were featured on the tour , including the four-part , multimedia flagship piece , Life Reflected , an NAC commission , which had its European premiere in Paris and was also performed in Gothenburg , Sweden . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40630;TOOLONG ... title= " Life Reflected on tour in Europe . " alt= " Life Reflected on tour in Europe . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;40666;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403123 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; With the text translated into French surtitles , the challenging Life Reflected went over well at La Seine Musicale , a spacious new facility just outside the core of Paris , and even better at the Konserthuset in Gothenburg . There , with Swedish surtitles , it was performed on the final night of the Point Music Festival , a celebration of new music , and received a standing ovation. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s so special when a piece does jump the border and leaves Canada , whether it&amp;rsquo ; s elsewhere in North America or to Europe , &amp;rdquo ; said composer John Estacio , who wrote the music to I Lost My Talk , one of the four parts of Life Reflected . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Usually a piece is performed in , and lives in , the country that commissioned it , and doesn&amp;rsquo ; t necessarily go beyond that so it&amp;rsquo ; s a lovely moment when another country gets to hear your music , &amp;rdquo ; he added . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His majestic score augments an arrangement of the poem by the late Mi&amp;rsquo ; kmaw poet laureate Rita Joe that was sparked by her time in residential school , where students were forbidden from speaking their languages . The poem is accompanied by a film depicting a company of Indigenous dancers performing on the rocky shores of Georgian Bay , and an Indigenous actor , Monique Mojica , whose film appearance is mirrored by an appearance on stage . Her real-life presence underscores the resilience of Indigenous Peoples who survived Canada&amp;rsquo ; s residential-school system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Life Reflected is produced and directed by Stratford hitmaker Donna Feore , who worked closely with Shelley as artistic director , and brought together artists from different generations , cultures and backgrounds . The piece also features segments on Nobel prize-winning author Alice Munro , astronaut Roberta Bondar and a particularly poignant section on B.C. teenager Amanda Todd , who took her own life after being bullied online . Amanda&amp;rsquo ; s mother , Carol Todd , was in the audience in Gothenburg . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40696;TOOLONG ... title= " The NACO on tour in Europe . " alt= " The NACO on tour in Europe . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;40732;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403130 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; As someone born outside Canada , Shelley lacks the typical Canuck reluctance to toot one&amp;rsquo ; s own horn . He tells everyone that NACO is one of the finest orchestras in the world . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; If it was a hockey league or any other sports league , they&amp;rsquo ; d be one of the top teams in the world , no question about that , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; The challenge on this tour is to take it out of the local league and go into the international league . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Stockholm , London , Paris , Copenhagen , they have their own teams . And they&amp;rsquo ; re great , but what I want is for our Canadian national team to be out there in those centres showcasing the quality and the craftsmanship of the orchestra . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His enthusiasm is convincing , and the orchestra lived up to the billing . Their playing was consistently excellent throughout the tour , and the team spirit grew with every day on the road as the group hustled to catch trains , buses and flights . Fortunately there was only one day when it was necessary to travel and perform a concert the same evening . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It helps us to bond in a very different way , &amp;rdquo ; said Elaine Klimasko , a violinist who&amp;rsquo ; s been with the orchestra since its first year in 1969. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re really a team . I find that people really become so much more friendly . Most are out without their spouses and you find you just sit down with a colleague you might have only shared a couple of stages with , &amp;rdquo ; she said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe width= " 100% " height= " 100% " frameborder= " 0 " allowfullscreen= " true " src= " https : **34;40762;TOOLONG ... &gt; &lt;/iframe&gt; &lt;p&gt; Now 69 , she&amp;rsquo ; s been on almost every tour , starting with the 1973 excursion to Russia and Eastern Europe with then-conductor Mario Bernardi. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; These days , she travels with her husband , Ed Blais , who considers it a vacation . He helps with luggage and scouts out interesting sites to see and restaurants to try . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Although her health is good and she feels she has more energy than many her age , Klimasko is beginning to consider retirement . She and Blais own a condo in Florida , and she&amp;rsquo ; s the artistic director of Ottawa Suzuki Strings , a music school co-founded by her sister . Teaching senior violin students has long been a passion . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In fact , one night in Utrecht , Klimasko returned to the hotel after a post-concert outing to a local bar in order to FaceTime a student in Ottawa who wanted help preparing some music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; She was also one of several orchestra musicians who lent their expertise during masterclasses with local students along the journey . Others visited schools to perform for , or with , youngsters . No fewer than 60 community engagement activities were on the schedule , including the noon-hour concert in the Stockholm&amp;rsquo ; s Royal Chapel that also featured Ehnes&amp;rsquo ; above-mentioned performance . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40798;TOOLONG ... title= " Alexander Shelley ( L ) , his wife Zoe , and baby Sasha at the train station with NAC staffer Fletcher Gailey-Snell in between . " alt= " Alexander Shelley ( L ) , his wife Zoe , and baby Sasha at the train station with NAC staffer Fletcher Gailey-Snell in between . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;40834;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403125 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Klimasko wasn&amp;rsquo ; t the only musician to bring a spouse . Some even brought children , including Shelley and his wife , Zoe , who travelled with their nine-month-old Ottawa-born son , Sasha , an inquisitive , good-natured baby who loved bouncing with Dad and didn&amp;rsquo ; t mind his mum passing him around for others to snuggle . The only problem was the virus he transmitted to both parents , leading to Shelley&amp;rsquo ; s first cold in two years . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Another couple with kids in tow was violist Paul Casey and cellist Karen Casey , with Karen&amp;rsquo ; s mother along to help care for almost two-year-old Oak and her busy big brother , Fitz , who&amp;rsquo ; s almost four , when the parents were in rehearsal or on stage . A few dozen orchestra pals also helped entertain the pre-schoolers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For some of the musical travellers , the tour offered a chance to sample fine restaurants in each city . In their time off , they visited museums , went on walking tours and checked out the nightlife . Their discipline was evident , too , as many sequestered themselves in their hotel rooms to practice , the sounds of viola or trumpet or flute filling the hallways. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40864;TOOLONG ... title= " NAC Orchestra viola player Paul Casey and his wife , cellist Karen Casey , travelled with both of their children on the orchestra 's 50th anniversary tour of Europe . " alt= " NAC Orchestra viola player Paul Casey and his wife , cellist Karen Casey , travelled with both of their children on the orchestra 's 50th anniversary tour of Europe . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;40900;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403124 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; The difficulties were infrequent . In London , two musicians were pickpocketed in separate incidents , an early-tour warning for everyone to secure their valuables . One musician suffered bruises after taking a tumble on the uneven cobblestone streets , while another lost a shoe in the scramble to get from concert to reception in Paris . An irreplaceable instrument was inadvertently left behind in Saffron Waldon , an oversight that required crew members to find a vehicle and drive back to the venue to retrieve it . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Bonding opportunities , on the other hand , were abundant . One of the most memorable moments happened during a whirlwind stop in Copenhagen , where the island hotel was conveniently located next to an outdoor ocean-water pool , the bottom secured with netting to separate swimmers from Baltic Sea life . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; That evening&amp;rsquo ; s fun started with a plentiful supply of post-concert beer on tap backstage , compliments of the Danish Symphony . It continued at a hipster cocktail bar , and culminated with an invigorating 2 a.m. dip in the Baltic Sea . Among the handful of musicians who plunged into the frigid ocean was cellist Julia MacLaine , who was celebrating her 37th birthday . &amp;ldquo ; Best . Birthday . Ever , &amp;rdquo ; she declared with a smile . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;40930;TOOLONG ... title= " Cellist Julia MacLaine ( left , in blue ) celebrated her 37th birthday in Copenhagen on May 21 . After a 2 a.m. dip in the Baltic Sea , she declared it the ' best birthday ever . ' " alt= " Cellist Julia MacLaine ( left , in blue ) celebrated her 37th birthday in Copenhagen on May 21 . ' " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;40966;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403122 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;nbsp ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Airfare , accommodations and ground transportation for more than 100 people doesn&amp;rsquo ; t come cheaply , and there was no extra funding from the federal government to pay for the tour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Instead , the bulk of the journey was funded by donors , about 25 of whom followed the orchestra on their own NAC staff-organized tour , which involved first-class travel , five-star hotels and formal receptions with Canada&amp;rsquo ; s dignitaries in each of the five countries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The group included the tour&amp;rsquo ; s main benefactors , Janice and Earl O&amp;rsquo ; Borne , as well as NAC Foundation patrons Dasha Shenkman and Elinor Gill Ratcliffe , who described herself as an &amp;ldquo ; orchestra groupie. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The reason why people donate to orchestras is we like the music , &amp;rdquo ; said the 77-year-old philanthropist from Newfoundland and Labrador during a pre-concert interview in the lobby of Copenhagen&amp;rsquo ; s elegant Angleterre Hotel . &amp;ldquo ; If you don&amp;rsquo ; t have the money to pay for the conductor , in this case a magnificent conductor , and to keep good musicians , you don&amp;rsquo ; t get any music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; So you do it for the music , you do it for your country . We are putting Canada , including Indigenous pieces , on the world stage . Personally I find that very exciting as a Canadian and as a human being , and I think this is a wonderful way to connect with people . For me , the arts is that little extra that gives us humanity , gives us the joy of life . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; NAC CEO Christopher Deacon , who was also on the tour , considered it one of the most successful NACO tours in its 50-year history . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; What was especially meaningful to me was the fact that we were able to bring the music of six Canadian composers , and present them in major European capitals , &amp;rdquo ; he said in Stockholm , also pointing to the high level of artistry displayed by the soloists . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This really aligns with one of our strategic priorities , to help put Canada&amp;rsquo ; s artistic expression on the world stage . I think the European public , which is quite discerning , was suitably impressed with the very high standard of excellence . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; As were we all . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;41220;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403108 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Erin Wall grew up with firsthand knowledge of the challenges of a career in classical music . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Canadian soprano is the daughter of a French horn player and a cellist who both played in the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra . During her childhood , the symphony&amp;rsquo ; s financial situation was a regular cause for concern in her family . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve lived that , &amp;rdquo ; the 43-year-old singer said during a candid and wide-ranging interview in Utrecht , Netherlands . &amp;ldquo ; Twice in my childhood there was either a lockout or strike , or bankruptcy problems . It was often a great cloud hanging over us. &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h2 class= " cat-head short " **40;41250;TOOLONG ... &lt;ul class= " relatedlinks " &gt; &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;41292;TOOLONG ... NACO just toured in Europe to ' amazed ' audiences , elevating the orchestra to one of the best **27;41327;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;41356;TOOLONG ... years of magic : CEO Christopher Deacon on the NAC 's **32;41391;TOOLONG &lt;li&gt;&lt;a href= " https : **33;41425;TOOLONG ... David DQ Lee wows the crowd in London with incredible , multi-octave **26;41460;TOOLONG &lt;/ul&gt; &lt;p&gt; Still , she found her way to a similar , arguably even more challenging career as an opera singer , a gig that doesn&amp;rsquo ; t usually offer the companionship of an entire orchestra and requires one to be comfortable performing demanding material in the spotlight . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Naturally , Wall was honoured to be invited along as a featured soloist on the NAC Orchestra&amp;rsquo ; s recent tour of Europe , even though it meant mastering some extremely difficult pieces . It was her fourth tour with an orchestra , but the first with an ensemble from Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Her voluptuous voice provides the ethereal upper thread in Dear Life , the Alice Munro-inspired segment of the multi-media new work , Life Reflected , which was performed in Paris and Gothenburg , Sweden . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For one Paris concertgoer , Wall&amp;rsquo ; s performance was the evening&amp;rsquo ; s standout moment . &amp;ldquo ; My God , she&amp;rsquo ; s incredible , &amp;rdquo ; said the Canadian ex-pat , who&amp;rsquo ; s been living in the City of Light for more than a decade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;41488;TOOLONG ... title= " Canadian soprano Erin Wall was the featured soloist in several concerts with the NAC Orchestra on its European tour , including Paris , Utrecht , Copenhagen , Stockholm and Gothenburg . " alt= " Canadian soprano Erin Wall was the featured soloist in several concerts with the NAC Orchestra on its European tour , including Paris , Utrecht , Copenhagen , Stockholm and Gothenburg . " data-portal-copyright= " CATTROLL FRED " **28;41524;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403111 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; In four cities on the tour , Wall also sang The Lonely Child , a haunting 1980 work for soprano and orchestra by Canadian composer Claude Vivier . It&amp;rsquo ; s considered the most personal and spiritual composition by the ill-fated character , who was abandoned by his parents as a baby , made no secret of the fact that he was gay and died before his time , murdered in Paris in 1983 , a month before his 35th birthday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Some audiences didn&amp;rsquo ; t know what to make of the piece , which is based on non-Western musical forms and calls for the singer , who&amp;rsquo ; s acting as a mother reassuring her lonely child , to touch her fingers to her lips to create musical noises , as if speaking gibberish to a child . It&amp;rsquo ; s especially intense for the singer because there are no breaks and she has to sing in an ever-escalating pitch . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; But as is often the case with love-it-or-hate-it nature of contemporary classical music , it was an exciting discovery for many adventurous listeners . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The Claude Vivier is completely new for us , &amp;rdquo ; said Adriaan Vanes , a Dutch music fan who attended the Utrecht concert with his wife and friends visiting from London . &amp;ldquo ; To not only hear his very tragic life story but ( to also hear ) his music , it&amp;rsquo ; s compelling . It&amp;rsquo ; s new . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His London friend concurred . &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s a very interesting and important experience to hear new voices and in this case , to hear the writing and the music of somebody who had , on the face of it , quite a difficult life , &amp;rdquo ; said James Welsh . &amp;ldquo ; We&amp;rsquo ; re extremely happy to have this opportunity . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Of course , audiences had no idea of the additional challenges Wall faced in getting to those European stages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; After she was invited on tour and given the repertoire , she was diagnosed with breast cancer . With an arts-employed husband and two young children at home in the Toronto area , she continued to work during her treatment . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Six rounds of chemo , two surgeries and a few months later , Wall was still determined to complete the tour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; I knew taking on the Vivier would be a really big challenge , &amp;rdquo ; she said , &amp;ldquo ; but because I had been involved in Dear Life from its inception , I wanted to be a part of that . It&amp;rsquo ; s fun to be part of something new . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; There are so many orchestras going , &amp;lsquo ; How can we reinvent this to get people to come , to make it modern and relevant and interesting ? &amp;rsquo ; I&amp;rsquo ; ve never done anything like Life Reflected before , and I think it works . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;hr&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;LISTEN TO THE DOWN TO BUSINESS PODCAST&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;iframe src= " **40;41554;TOOLONG ... " data-portal-copyright= " PROVIDED " **28;41716;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1403104 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; It&amp;rsquo ; s unlikely that British audiences have ever seen a singer quite like David DQ Lee . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Korean-Canadian countertenor , whose full name is David Dong-Qyu Lee , is the featured soloist in Ana Sokovic&amp;rsquo ; s Juno-winning piece of contemporary classical music , Golden slumbers kiss your eyes&amp;hellip ; , performed by the NAC Orchestra as part of its program at Cadogan Hall in London , England . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The 20-minute composition featured a choir &amp;mdash ; on this night , London Voices &amp;mdash ; with a spotlight role written specifically to show off Lee&amp;rsquo ; s incredible , multi-octave voice . Although billed as a countertenor , meaning he&amp;rsquo ; s a singer with a masterful command of the high end of the male range , he&amp;rsquo ; s also capable of resoundingly deep bass notes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In Sokovic&amp;rsquo ; s intricate and moving work , he gets the rare chance to show off both ends of his vocal spectrum , and he nailed it , demonstrating incredible control and impeccable phrasing . One seasoned British fan in the audience was so impressed he approached an NAC staff member to share his enthusiasm and find out Lee&amp;rsquo ; s name . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For Lee , who&amp;rsquo ; s 41 , the response was encouraging . It&amp;rsquo ; s been almost a decade since he last performed in London , and he knows that British music fans tend to prefer a different style of countertenor . Plus , he added , they&amp;rsquo ; re not used to diversity in classical singing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is their culture , &amp;rdquo ; he said , referring to classical music in general during an interview in his dressing room after the concert . &amp;ldquo ; It can be very racist . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;41746;TOOLONG ... title= " The NAC orchestra on tour in Europe with countertenor David D.Q. They definitely have a preference . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Born in South Korea , Lee had early training in classic vocal technique as a boy soprano in a prestigious Korean children&amp;rsquo ; s choir . When his family moved to Vancouver , he joined a boys&amp;rsquo ; choir . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Then my voice broke and I had this low voice as a male , but I still had the muscle memory so I could actually go into the higher register , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; I still had no idea what a countertenor was until my choir director in high school told me , &amp;lsquo ; You are a countertenor. &amp;rsquo ; &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He discovered the movie , Fattadelli , about a singer who had been castrated to maintain his high-pitched voice . NewsMusicFamily looks for answers after popular musician struck down by blood clothttp : **36;43148;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;43186;TOOLONG ... title= " Janet Di Giacomo 's son Daniel , 31 , died suddenly in late February of a pulmonary embolism several weeks after orthopaedic surgery . Julie Oliver " data-portal-copyright= " Julie Oliver " **28;43222;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1374201 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Daniel Di Giacomo died in the early morning of Feb. 21 , struggling for breath on the kitchen floor as his incredulous father looked on . He was 31 years old . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The bassist for the up-and-coming country band the River Town Saints , Di Giacomo was a fun-loving bear of a man who had suffered a broken lower leg and dislocated ankle about seven weeks earlier . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His family believes the break prompted a fatal chain of events . They&amp;rsquo ; re looking for answers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; No one should got through what we have been going through , &amp;rdquo ; said Di Giacomo&amp;rsquo ; s mother , Janet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The cause of death is believed to be a thrombosis , or blood clot , that had traveLled to his lung , causing a pulmonary embolism . Di Giacomo&amp;rsquo ; s family says that if they had known a blood clot was a potentially fatal risk , they would have asked more questions . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Six days before he died , he had clear symptoms of a blood clot , but we didn&amp;rsquo ; t know what it was , &amp;rdquo ; said his sister , Cristina. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Di Giacomo&amp;rsquo ; s father , Mike , says an embolism wasn&amp;rsquo ; t even on his radar . &amp;ldquo ; We didn&amp;rsquo ; t know what the warning signs were . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Janet said her attempts to get answers form Queensway Carleton Hospital about whether her son should have been sent home after his surgery with a list of warning signs and a prescription for blood thinners have been unsuccessful . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The hospital&amp;rsquo ; s chief of staff , Dr. Sanjay Acharya , wrote to Janet in an email dated March 22 that he has directed the department chief to review current practice relating to her concerns . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; We have already asked our risk managers to review the consents and how/if they need to be updated , &amp;rdquo ; Acharya wrote . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; This is part of our internal review and what we would do after any critical incident . It would be our normal practice to invite you and your family to participate in any way you feel appropriate when we have gathered the basic information we need to make analysis . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Di Giacomo broke his leg just before noon Dec. 31 while delivering a television on an icy day . While he spent the summers touring with the River Town Saints , Di Giacomo worked a day job in the winter months . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He went first to the Almonte General Hospital and was transferred to Queensway Carleton . It took him 12 hours to see specialist . As was his way , he never breathed a word of impatience , said Janet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Di Giacomo could not be scheduled for surgery the next day and went home . He had day surgery on Jan. 3 , and was sent home with seven pages of instructions , including two pages for using crutches , a prescription for painkillers and a knee walker , a scooter-like device that allowed him to get around without putting weight on his ankle . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; He left the instructions on the coffee table of his west-end home , but Janet read every one of them . There was no mention of thrombosis or the risks around it or the suggestion that the patient should follow an exercise regime , she says . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; The only mention was about wiggling his toes . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Daniel was the fourth of five children born to Janet and Mike . The family is musical . Janet played the guitar and piano and taught the boys to play . Di Giamcomo joined his first band at Bell High School , and was self-taught on the bass . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He loved being the centre of attention . Not in an offensive way . If you were in a room with Dan , he was the loudest guy and everyone would be laughing , &amp;rdquo ; &amp;nbsp ; said bandmate Jeremy Bortot. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;43252;TOOLONG ... title= " Dan Di Giacomo was the bassist with the Ottawa band the River Town Saints . Photo by Sean Sisk Photography " alt= " Dan Di Giacomo was the bassist with the Ottawa band the River Town Saints . Photo by Sean Sisk Photography " data-portal-copyright= " SEAN SISK " **28;43288;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1374198 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; Di Giamoco was also a deeply religious person and had studied at Bible college and spent two and a half years at a Los Angeles mission for the homeless called the Dream Center . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Dan had really strong beliefs . What people found super-cool about him was that he was pragmatic about it , &amp;rdquo ; says Bertot. &amp;ldquo ; He knew his theology , but he lived his life according to his beliefs . He was a good guy to other people . He was just kind . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The band criss-crossed the country in a 1988 Chevy van nicknamed Ron Burgundy and opened for a better-known acts . Di Giacomo&amp;rsquo ; s bandmates joked that he got his own room on tour because he snored like a grizzly bear sucking on a shop vac . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Saints played at every major country music festival in Eastern Canada and toured with country music stars Kip Moore and Dean Brody . The Saints&amp;rsquo ; singles Bonfire and Cherry Bomb got significant radio play and band was nominated for the Canadian Country Music Association award in the rising star category in 2016. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;43318;TOOLONG ... title= " Chris McComb , Dan Di Giacomo , Jeremy Bortot of the River Town Saints.Photo by Sean Sisk Photography " alt= " Chris McComb , Dan Di Giacomo , Jeremy Bortot of the River Town Saints.Photo by Sean Sisk Photography " data-portal-copyright= " Sean Sisk " **28;43354;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1374199 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s hard to make a living from music . You have to work so hard . If you&amp;rsquo ; re just doing it for the money , you would be disappointed , &amp;rdquo ; said Bortot. &amp;ldquo ; It can&amp;rsquo ; t be about the destination ; it has to be about the ride . And it was such a great ride . If you saw Dan on stage , you would see someone who loved what he did . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In the second week of February , Di Giacomo&amp;rsquo ; s recovery appeared to be slow . He later texted his friends that he still didn&amp;rsquo ; t feel back to normal and asked if future auditions could be spaced out . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He was exhausted . We just thought he was healing . He couldn&amp;rsquo ; t do that much , &amp;rdquo ; says Janet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Sunday before he died , Di Giacomo gave his father a scare when he complained of chest pains . Mike gave him an aspirin and the pain subsided . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Di Giacomo told his parents he thought he over-exerted himself . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; He wasn&amp;rsquo ; t the kind who abused the medical system , &amp;rdquo ; said Janet . &amp;ldquo ; A couple of people urged him to go to the hospital , but he probably didn&amp;rsquo ; t want to be packed up and sent home again . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; On the night of Feb. 20 , Di Giacomo spoke to his mother , who was in Pennsylvania , and spent his last few hours texting friends . It appears he got up for a glass of water in the early morning of Feb. 21. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; His father woke up shortly after 2 a.m. and heard Di Giacomo calling for help . Mike found his son sitting on the kitchen floor , struggling for breath and semi-coherent . Mike called 911. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; One paramedic team came and called for backup . Di Giacomo was hooked up to a monitor . His father , sitting on the stairs across the hall , said he saw his son&amp;rsquo ; s heartbeat flatline. &amp;nbsp ; Paramedics continued to administer CPR and rushed Di Gimacomo to the hospital with Mike following . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; When Mike saw the doctor&amp;rsquo ; s face , he knew his son was dead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Shortly after , Mike spoke to a coroner who asked a few questions , including whether Daniel was taking blood thinners . Di Giacomo didn&amp;rsquo ; t hide anything from his family , and as far as Mike knew , his son wasn&amp;rsquo ; t taking blood thinners . That question got the wheels turning for Mike . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; That begged the question &amp;mdash ; if it was a known risk , why was he not prescribed blood thinners ? My son just died . I was hearing a suggestion that it didn&amp;rsquo ; t have to happen , &amp;rdquo ; he said . &amp;ldquo ; If the risk was there , why didn&amp;rsquo ; t we know about it ? That&amp;rsquo ; s what we want to know . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; March was Deep Vein Thrombosis Awareness Month . According to a survey commissioned by Thrombosis Canada last fall , only 43 per cent of Canadians know about the condition and only 25 per cent are concerned about it even though it can kill quickly . Vein blood blots affect about 100,000 Canadians and cause 10,000 deaths . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Thrombosis Canada launched a campaign last month about the most common symptoms , which include chest pain , being lightheaded and out of breath , leg tenderness and leg swelling . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; A spokeswoman for the Queensway Carleton said the hospital can&amp;rsquo ; t comment on the specifics of Di Giacomo&amp;rsquo ; s case , but its standard processes include discussing potential side effects , like blood clots or infections . Patients deemed to be at a higher risk are supported and treated on an individual basis . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; For a patient who has had ankle surgery , the post-operative kit would include an information sheet indicating that &amp;ldquo ; some pain is normal for the first seven to 10 days , &amp;rdquo ; and urging the patient to call his or her surgeon or go to the nearest emergency department if there is severe pain not relieved with pain medication or if there is pain for more than seven to 10 days . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The standard information package includes things to watch for , like pain , swelling , and changes in colour , said the spokeswoman . &amp;ldquo ; Some of these symptoms may indicate a blood clot or other issue . But the general package does not go into more details . &amp;rdquo ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Blood clots are not a standard medical concern for ankle surgery , she said . &amp;ldquo ; Blood clots can be a general concern , depending on the type of surgery . We would have acted very differently , &amp;rdquo ; said Janet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s just another paragraph or two . The band name was adapted from a fondly remembered Sunday-night radio program on a Toronto radio station . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " That 's the stuff I grew up on , " Gouthro said in an interview , referring to the early material . At the festival , which runs from July 25 to Aug. 8 , there will also be concerts featuring young rising stars , collaborations between classical and world-music artists and an exploration of the Queer Songbook. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Roman Borys , Chamberfest&amp;rsquo ; s artistic and executive director , said presenting Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s &amp;ldquo ; essential&amp;rdquo ; chamber music would be the festival&amp;rsquo ; s mission not just this year , but in 2020 &amp;mdash ; 250 years after the great German composer&amp;rsquo ; s actual birth year &amp;mdash ; and in 2021. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; It&amp;rsquo ; s very nice at this point to be able to have a three-year Beethoven anniversary to sink our teeth into as we head into the next block of 25 years , &amp;rdquo ; Borys said in an interview . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;During the next three years , Chamberfest will feature Beethoven 's complete piano sonatas , violin sonatas , cello sonatas , piano trios and string quartets , as well as some other " smaller , idiosyncratic works , " Borys continued . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt; " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;Beethoven is really sort of the centre of the world as far as chamber music is concerned ... ( responsible for ) the massive tome of art that really represents greatest achievement in Western culture , " Borys said . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;43965;TOOLONG ... title= " Pianist Hinrich Alpers will perform 15 of Beethoven 's piano sonatas at this year 's Chamberfest. " alt= " Pianist Hinrich Alpers will perform 15 of Beethoven 's piano sonatas at this year 's Chamberfest. " data-portal-copyright= " HANDOUT " **28;44001;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 283620 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; This year&amp;rsquo ; s festival will see Berlin-based pianist Hinrich Alpers perform 15 of Beethoven&amp;rsquo ; s 32 piano sonatas over two &amp;ldquo ; marathon&amp;rdquo ; afternoon concerts at Dominion-Chalmers United Church , on July 30 and Aug. 1 . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Borys called Alpers , a frequent performer at Chamberfest , &amp;ldquo ; a musician of immense breadth and depth . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &amp;ldquo ; Audiences have really learned to appreciate the grace and absolute control and mastery and insightfulness and beauty with which he approaches his interpretations , &amp;rdquo ; Borys said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Also in the Essential Beethoven series , violinist James Ehnes will tackle the composer&amp;rsquo ; s 10 violin sonatas at Dominion-Chalmers during concerts on July 31 and Aug. 2 , joined by pianist Andrew Armstrong . As well , author and radio host Robert Harris , who wrote What To Listen For In Beethoven , will give two talks on Beethoven during Chamberfest. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Regarding baroque singer and composer Barbara Strozzi , who was born in Italy 400 years ago this August , Borys said &amp;ldquo ; the musical world has yet to truly understand her greatness . &amp;rdquo ; Strozzi&amp;rsquo ; s music will be heard during a July 26 concert at Dominion-Chalmers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; In connection with the 200th anniversary of her birth , Clara Schumann , the wife of German composer Robert Schumann and a formidable Romantic-era composer in her own right , will be celebrated at an afternoon performance on Aug. 7 at the National Gallery of Canada . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;This year 's Chamberfest will also mark two half-century anniversaries . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;In 1969 , The Beatles released Abbey Road . That classic album that has been reimagined and re-orchestrated by Toronto 's Art of Time Ensemble , the group that closed Chamberfest two years ago with its like-minded exploration of Sgt. Pepper 's Lonely Hearts Club Band . This year , the group will again close Chamberfest , delving into Abbey Road on Aug. 8 at Dominion-Chalmers. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The Toronto group&amp;rsquo ; s 2017 concert &amp;ldquo ; was such a huge hit I couldn&amp;rsquo ; t resist this opportunity , &amp;rdquo ; Borys said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-family : -apple-system , BlinkMacSystemFont , ' Segoe UI ' , Roboto , Oxygen-Sans , Ubuntu , Cantarell , ' Helvetica Neue ' , sans-serif ; " &gt;The festival will present the Canadian Brass , which marks its 50th anniversary this year , on Aug. 2 at Dominion-Chalmers . " They 've created an amazing brand that has always celebrated and absolutely championed the highest level of artistry , " Borys said . " They combine that virtuosity with a lighthearted approach ... They 've embraced their inner entertainer . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; String quartets will be well-represented at Chamberfest thanks to concerts by the St. Lawrence String Quartet ( Jul. 27 at 1 p.m. , National Gallery ) , Quatuor Danel ( July 30 at 7 p.m. , Dominion-Chalmers ) and the Dover Quartet ( Aug. 7 at 7 p.m. , Dominion-Chalmers ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the rising stars at Chamberfest this year are the Ottawa-raised duo of cellist Bryan Cheng and pianist Silvie Cheng , who perform Aug. 3 at the National Gallery . &amp;nbsp ; Another fresh-faced group returning to Chamberfest is the Netherlands-based all-female Syr&amp;egrave ; ne Saxafoonkwartet . The group , which played in Ottawa in 2016 , will play July 29 at 1 p.m. an the National Gallery . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Among the festival&amp;rsquo ; s Chamberfringe concerts at 10 p.m. nightly are an opening concert in Dominion-Chalmers by the St. Lawrence String Quartet and pianist Steven Prutsman , playing along with the Buster Keaton film College , a July 26 concert at the Ottawa Art Gallery ( OAG ) where guitarist Ben Verdery will play music from Bach to Jimi Hendrix . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Also in the Chamberfringe series , Toronto-based Cuban jazz pianist Hilario Duran and his trio will join forces at La Nouvelle Sc&amp;egrave ; ne on King Edward Avenue with violinist Annalee Patipatanakoon and Borys , who will pick up his cello . On Aug. 5 , Toronto&amp;rsquo ; s Al Qahwa Ensemble will present Arabic folk at the OAG and the following night , on Aug. 6 , the Toronto chamber-pop ensemble Queer Songbook Orchestra will perform music ranging from Billy Strayhorn to Taylor Swift at the OAG. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Festival passes ranging in price from $170 to $439 along with selected single tickets go on sale Tuesday at 9 a.m. at chamberfest.com/tickets and at the Chamberfest box office ( 4 Florence St. , Suite 301 ) . Pass prices increase on May 1 . But this year , for the first time , organizers are making it easier for fans to navigate the schedule by programming genre-specific blocks of music on the various stages . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Snoop Dogg , for example , will headline a rap night on July 13 that also features a return appearance by hip-hop pioneers Wu-Tang Clan , while Nashville singer Kane Brown shares the July 11 bill with the country-pop outfit Gone West . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;44345;TOOLONG ... title= " The Killers . The aforementioned night with Kane Brown on July 11 also features appearances by Shakey Graves , Murda Beatz , DJ Pauly D , Leikeli47 and more . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; The festival&amp;rsquo ; s final weekend will be hopping , starting with a rock night on July 12 that features Alexisonfire , The Offspring and The Dirty Nil , as well as rapper T-Pain , the enigmatic Guided By Voices and more.Snoop Dogg headlines what&amp;rsquo ; s expected to be a hiphop celebration of cannabis legalization on July 13 , although Pussy Riot , the Russian feminist punk band , roots gentleman Pokey LaFarge , and troubadour Matt Andersen and the Mellotones are also scheduled for other stages that day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; Finally , it&amp;rsquo ; s the long-awaited return of the pop superstars Backstreet Boys on July 14 . Regular sales , including single-day tickets , and three-day and five-day passes , start at 10 a.m . Friday . The electronic dance music festival takes place June 22 and 23 at Lansdowne Park . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The two seasoned DJs , who will perform separate sets and one together , are the final acts to be announced in a lineup that already includes headliners DJ Snake and Holland 's Martin Garrix , along with Canadians Adventure Club , Zeds Dead , Keys and Krates , Loud Luxury and dozens of others from North America and beyond . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;For Paris-based Snake , whose real name is William Sami ? tienne Grigahcine , it will be his first appearance in Ottawa . The Grammy-nominated producer/artist is one of the world 's most popular crossover DJs , having hit the billion mark on Spotify with more than one song . His latest massive hit , Taki Taki , features Cardi B and Selena Gomez . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Garrix is another DJ with commercial appeal , ranked by DJ Mag as No. 1 on the list of the world 's top 100 DJs for three consecutive years . He first played Escapade in 2016. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;44732;TOOLONG ... title= " Zeds Dead . " alt= " Zeds Dead . " The first year we did n't put much emphasis on it in terms of production but this year we 'll be stepping up our game . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Although Aberdeen is also notoriously challenging for live sound , organizers found curtains softened the reverb last year . According to Shafaee , the style of music makes a difference , too . " It 's not like rock or country because there are not as many vocals or live instruments so the sound is n't as bad in there , " he said . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;44798;TOOLONG ... title= " Martin Garrix performs onstage during day 4 of the Firefly Music Festival . With Deadmau5 headlining , it attracted an estimated 2,000 people . In subsequent years , it was also held at the Ottawa Baseball Stadium , the RA Centre and Rideau Carleton Raceway before moving to Lansdowne Park in 2017. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Noise complaints and overdoses have been the biggest problems in recent years , although Shafaee said organizers work with the community and authorities to mitigate both . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " We 've had noise complaints but we have n't broken any bylaws or anything like that , " he said . " We 're a large event in an urban , residential neighbourhood . We have a sound system that allows us to control as much of the sound as we can , and we try to work with the community as best as we can . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;They also work with police and paramedics to ensure the safety of festivalgoers . More than 100 naloxone-equipped security personnel are on site , as well as first-aid trained Canadian Ski Patrol volunteers . An amnesty bin at the front gate allows patrons to dispose of street drugs , no questions asked . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;44864;TOOLONG ... title= " The two-day Heineken Escapade 2017 electronic music festival has taken over Lansdowne Park . " We do whatever we can to make sure the audience is partying safely . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;This year 's event is expected to attract 30,000 people , most representing the 19-29-year-old demographic . If they go as quickly as anticipated , it will be the first time the festival has sold out in advance . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Shafaee said statistics show that up to 40 per cent of festivalgoers visit Ottawa from out of town , and the event generates an economic impact estimated at $3.1 million . ArtsMusicPatrick Watson teams up with NAC Orchestra to show emotional range of songwritinghttp : **29;46259;TOOLONG ... &lt;img src= " https : **34;46290;TOOLONG ... title= " Montreal musician Patrick Watson . " alt= " Montreal musician Patrick Watson . " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;46326;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1337969 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Patrick Watson with the NAC Orchestra&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;strong&gt;Reviewed Saturday&lt;/strong&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Patrick Watson and his band performed with the NAC Orchestra on Saturday , and the results were downright enthralling . Hunched over the grand piano and warbling in his expressive falsetto , the classically trained Montreal singer-songwriter was in his element amid the lush textures of Ottawa 's world-class orchestra . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;On a bitterly cold and snowy night in the capital , Watson and the dozens of musicians on stage -- conducted by Kingston Symphony music director Evan Mitchell -- created a sense of warmth and intimacy in front of a soldout crowd of more than 2,000 people at Southam Hall . The concert was part of the NAC Presents ' Sessions series , an initiative that matches singer-songwriters with the orchestra , and provides the artist with the opportunity to work with a pro to come up with arrangements of their material . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;46356;TOOLONG ... title= " Montreal musician Patrick Watson . " alt= " Montreal musician Patrick Watson . " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;46392;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1337969 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The unusual arrangements were definitely a highlight of the concert . While Watson 's songs are meticulously composed and layered to start with , the orchestral arrangements created by English conductor/arranger Jules Buckley , who 's 39 and greatly inspired by Looney Tunes composer Carl Stalling , brought them to another level with unexpected sounds and flourishes , including sliding whistles , squealing balloons and other non-traditional effects . Those surprises were used most effectively in the simmering build of Where The Wild Things Are . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The evening offered a superb demonstration of the emotional range of songwriting , from the hushed dreaminess of Lighthouse to the bustling peaks and lonely valleys of Beijing , to the soothing sentiment of To Build A Home , with its central lyric , " This is a place where I do n't feel alone . " Adding to the ethereal atmosphere were the mood-enhancing spotlights and a murky haze that emanated from a fog machine . There was also a chance for the orchestra to strut its stuff on a piece by Ravel. &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;To Build A Home is one of Watson 's biggest hits , a quiet , piano-driven ballad that 's been streamed tens of millions of times , racking up numbers that rival the latest Lady Gaga mega hit . In an interview before the concert , Watson said its popularity has made him realize that people prefer to listen to something other than frenzied pop music when they get home . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;img src= " https : **34;46422;TOOLONG ... title= " Montreal musician Patrick Watson took a moment after rehearsals at the National Arts Centre on Saturday . " alt= " Montreal musician Patrick Watson took a moment after rehearsals at the National Arts Centre on Saturday . " data-portal-copyright= " Ashley Fraser " **28;46458;TOOLONG " 1 " data-license-id= " 1337968 " /&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " It does n't seem that people want to listen to crazy new rock ' n ' roll or catchy bubblegum pop music as much as they want to talk about it , " he said . " I think they want something that slows down time , and brings you out of this world . That 's what I 'm banking on . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Watson has been working on a new album , his first since 2015 's acclaimed Love Songs For Robots , which never got much radio play but helped him continue building an audience on both sides of the Atlantic . Last month 's European tour featured a string of soldout concerts in increasingly larger venues . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " There 's never any hype about what we do , " observed Watson . " We put out a record , and then slowly it digs into people 's lives . They play it more than once , and they show their friends . It just seems like the kind of music we do just slowly grows every day . And it 's a very young audience , which is interesting . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;It seems millennials are discovering Watson 's songs through other avenues , including TV shows , advertising and video games . Popular shows such as The Walking Dead , Homeland , This is Us and Orange is the New Black have all featured his work . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;The 39-year-old father of three young children said his forthcoming album may be his last full-length project , largely because of the music industry 's Spotify-driven shift to singles . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " It 's a different musical landscape , " he said . " I will probably never make another full-length record again . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;Whether or not it 's the last one , he 's determined to make it count . " I 've taken my time over the last four years , " he said . " I want to put out nine heavy-hitting songs . No fluff . To enter the Spotify world , which is so overwhelmingly flushed with so much music , I just did n't feel like putting anything out unless I felt it was really , really good . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " Instead of making a long 45-minute story , I 'm more interested in making songs that can stand on their own as well , outside the story , which is incredibly difficult . That 's why it 's taking so goddamn long . " &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt;He 's released two new songs so far , introducing the evocative Venezuelan-inspired Melody Noir during Saturday 's concert . There will be a third single soon , but we 'll have to wait until September for the full album . &lt;/span&gt; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; &lt;span style= " font-weight:400 ; " &gt; " I do n't want to flood the market , " he said . " Some people want to release a million things and maybe get some on a playlist . That works , but I just want to put something out that blows people 's minds . It is one of the most bizarre symptoms of global warming . An individual virion , the unit of viral existence , makes many copies of itself over its life cycle , but it never does something that can be described as living . It never breathes or mates . It punctures a cell 's wall , hijacks its protein factories , and forces it to make more of itself . A single virion can make tens of thousands of copies of itself near instantly . Viruses are living nonlife , a desirous but mindless substance . <p> At the frontier of viral life are Jean-Michel Claverie and Chantal Abergel , two professors of microbiology at Aix-Marseilles University who happen to be married to each other . @@31743055 <h> Abstract <p> Removal of atmospheric carbon dioxide ( CO2 ) combined with emission reduction is necessary to keep climate warming below the internationally agreed upon 2 ? C target . Soil organic carbon sequestration through agricultural management has been proposed as a means to lower atmospheric CO2 concentration , but the magnitude needed to meaningfully lower temperature is unknown . We show that sequestration of 0.68 Pg C year-1 for 85 years could lower global temperature by 0.1 ? C in 2100 when combined with a low emission trajectory Representative Concentration Pathway ( RCP ) 2.6 . This value is potentially achievable using existing agricultural management approaches , without decreasing land area for food production . Existing agricultural mitigation approaches could lower global temperature by up to 0.26 ? C under RCP 2.6 or as much as 25% of remaining warming to 2 ? C. This declines to 0.14 ? C under RCP 8.5 . Results were sensitive to assumptions regarding the duration of carbon sequestration rates , which is poorly constrained by data . Results provide a framework for the potential role of agricultural soil organic carbon sequestration in climate change mitigation . <h> INTRODUCTION <p> The @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ subsequent storage in soils may be an effective means to lower atmospheric carbon dioxide ( CO2 ) concentrations and to help mitigate climate change . Integrated assessment models ( IAMs ) , which are used to explore future energy , land-use , and greenhouse gas ( GHG ) emission scenarios , currently rely on bioenergy with carbon capture and storage ( BECCS ) as a principal negative emission technology to reach climate change mitigation targets , but generally do not consider the possibility of C drawdown and soil organic C ( SOC ) sequestration from improved land management ( 1 , 2 ) . Improved land management , without changing land use , may be an additional C sequestration option that does not require more land conversion . Land-use change and poor management practices have resulted in the loss of more than 130 Pg C from agricultural soil ( 3 ) , leaving &gt;1 billion hectares of degraded soil worldwide ( 4 ) . Site-based studies and ecosystem-scale models have shown that degraded and managed agricultural lands have great potential to contribute to increased SOC sequestration through improved management ( @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ as a net increase in SOC storage . Several agricultural ( cropland and grazing land ) management practices have been shown to increase soil C sequestration including organic amendments ( 8 -- 10 ) , cover crops , reduced tillage , improved crop rotations ( 5 , 11 , 12 ) , and improved grazing management ( 13 , 14 ) . Citing these proven practices and others , France and 33 other countries recently instituted a challenge to increase soil C by 4 per mil per year ( 15 ) . However , the actual potential of these practices to contribute to lowering global temperature over time is poorly understood , despite recent efforts to quantify the amenable global land area and near-term sequestration rates associated with various practices ( 16 -- 18 ) . This is primarily due to uncertainty regarding the maintenance of soil C sequestration rates over time , the C sequestration capacity of different soils under different managements , and the sensitivity of global temperature changes to CO2 emission and sequestration . <p> Here , we use a climate model emulator to translate SOC sequestration @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ surface temperature changes over time , consistent with global-scale outputs from the latest generation of Earth system models ( ESMs ; see Materials and Methods and fig . S1 ) . Much of the research to date on the potential of land use -- based SOC sequestration has focused on quantifying current sequestration rates with the implicit assumption that rates remain constant over time , often assuming a constrained time period of 20 to 50 years ( 12 , 16 ) . The potential for SOC sequestration to contribute to a portfolio of mitigation strategies aimed at reducing climate change depends not only on the rates soon after C sequestering practices are implemented but also on the time-integrated dynamics of those rates , that is , how quickly land-use changes can be adopted , how long they remain in effect , and how SOC stocks change over time ( 19 ) . This temporal dynamic is poorly understood but is critical to accurately estimate the potential for land-based management to slow climate change . <p> In practice , rates of SOC sequestration are likely to decline over time at any @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , but the time scale and shape of these declines are not well constrained by data and are likely to vary significantly among locations and management practices . To help bound this uncertainty , we model the effects of SOC sequestration on global surface temperature with and without consideration of effective sequestration years , defined as the number of years it would take to reach the maximum SOC stock ( SOC max ) at the current potential sequestration rate ( see fig . S3 ) . The SOC max is a concept proposed by Six et al . ( 21 ) and is poorly constrained by data at both site and global scales . An SOC max provides a theoretical limit on the amount of SOC storage in soils . As opposed to applying an arbitrary SOC max at a fixed time period ( for example , 20 or 50 years ) , we model effective sequestration years as a continuum of time periods required to reach an SOC max ( from 0 to 85 years ) for a range of SOC sequestration rates . The current potential sequestration rate @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ S1 ) . Our analysis focuses specifically on the temperature response to SOC sequestration . SOC storage is sensitive to a suite of global change factors such as elevated atmospheric CO2 concentration and changes in climate , among others ( 22 , 23 ) . These factors will likely have additional , albeit poorly constrained , impacts on management-induced SOC sequestration ( 24 ) . Our goal here is not to quantify the ecological controls on SOC storage and loss in agricultural ecosystems but to determine the magnitude of SOC sequestration needed at a global scale to meaningfully affect temperatures and to explore the sensitivity of atmospheric temperature change to a range of possible temporal limits to soil C sequestration ( effective sequestration years ) . <h> RESULTS <p> The model shows that a global SOC sequestration rate of 0.68 Pg C year-1 from 2015 to 2100 would be required to yield a 0.1 ? C reduction in mean surface temperature in target year 2100 when coupled with an aggressive emission reduction scenario Representative Concentration Pathway ( RCP ) 2.6 ; Fig. 1 . These results assumed a constant sequestration @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ year-1 global sequestration rate is at the low end of the ranges of published estimates , which vary from a low of 0.36 Pg C year-1 to a high of 1.56 Pg C year-1 ( 12 , 17 , 25 , 26 ) . There is considerable uncertainty in the actual time horizon of soil C sequestration rates within sites , which is likely to vary in response to social , economic , and biophysical factors ( 17 , 27 ) . Few studies have measured long-term ( &gt;20 years ) patterns in soil C sequestration with agricultural management , and those have shown a wide range of continued sequestration rates from 20 to over 150 years ( 11 , 28 -- 30 ) . For this reason , we applied no a priori assumption on the time horizon required of soil C sequestration and , instead , modeled a continuum of effective sequestration years at SOC sequestration rates from 0 to 2.0 Pg C year-1 .
